1.186.s:
bhāskara uvāca .. ..
śrāvaṇyāṃ tu baliḥ kāryaḥ sarpāṇāṃ maṃtrapūrvakaḥ ..
śayanārohaṇe caiva kārye sukhamabhīpsatā .. 1 ..
1.186.d:
भास्कर उवाच ॥ ॥
श्रावण्यां तु बलिः कार्यः सर्पाणां मंत्रपूर्वकः ॥
शयनारोहणे चैव कार्ये सुखमभीप्सता ॥ 1 ॥

1.186.s:
kāryaḥ pratyavarohastu mārgaśīrṣyāṃ na saṃśayaḥ ..
phalaṃ vinā tvanuṣṭhānaṃ nityānāmiṣyate sphuṭam .. 2 ..
1.186.d:
कार्यः प्रत्यवरोहस्तु मार्गशीर्ष्यां न संशयः ॥
फलं विना त्वनुष्ठानं नित्यानामिष्यते स्फुटम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.186.m:
The descent [from the high bed] must without doubt be performed on the full-moon day of Mārgaśīrṣa;
the performance of regular duties is clearly accepted as being without a [specific] reward.

1.186.s:
kāmyānāṃ saphalārthaṃ tu doṣaprāptyarthameva ca ..
naimittikānāṃ karaṇaṃ trividhaṃ karmaṇāṃ phalam .. 3 ..
1.186.d:
काम्यानां सफलार्थं तु दोषप्राप्त्यर्थमेव च ॥
नैमित्तिकानां करणं त्रिविधं कर्मणां फलम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.186.m:
The performance of optional rites is for a reward, and that of occasional rites is to avoid demerit;
thus threefold is the fruit of actions.

1.186.s:
phalaṃ kecidupāttasya duritasya pracakṣate ..
anutpattiṃ tathā cānye pratyetyābhyupamaṃtrya ca .. 4 ..
1.186.d:
फलं केचिदुपात्तस्य दुरितस्य प्रचक्षते ॥
अनुत्पत्तिं तथा चान्ये प्रत्येत्याभ्युपमंत्र्य च ॥ 4 ॥
1.186.m:
Some describe the fruit as the [removal] of accumulated sin,
and others, having understood and declared it, as its non-arising.

1.186.s:
nityakriyaṃ tathā cānye anuṣaṃgātphalaṃ śrutiḥ ..
agnyādheyaṃ tathā darśaṃ paurṇamāsaṃ dvitīyakam..5..
1.186.d:
नित्यक्रियं तथा चान्ये अनुषंगात्फलं श्रुतिः ॥
अग्न्याधेयं तथा दर्शं पौर्णमासं द्वितीयकम्॥5॥
1.186.m:
Others say the regular rite produces a result as a secondary consequence; sacred tradition says:
establishing the sacrificial fires, the new-moon sacrifice, and the full-moon sacrifice as the second;

1.186.s:
cāturmāsyamagnihotraṃ paśubaṃdho nirūḍhakāḥ ..
sautrāmaṇī saṃsthāḥ syurhaviṣaḥ śrutinoditāḥ .. 6 ..
1.186.d:
चातुर्मास्यमग्निहोत्रं पशुबंधो निरूढकाः ॥
सौत्रामणी संस्थाः स्युर्हविषः श्रुतिनोदिताः ॥ 6 ॥
1.186.m:
the Cāturmāsya, the Agnihotra, the animal sacrifice, the Nirūḍhapaśubandha,
and the Sautrāmaṇī—these are the forms of oblations prescribed by the Veda.

1.186.s:
agniṣṭomo'tyagniṣṭoma ukthyaḥ saṃṣoḍaśī tathā ..
vājapeyātirātraśca āpyoryāmaḥ śrutau śrutaḥ ..7..
1.186.d:
अग्निष्टोमोऽत्यग्निष्टोम उक्थ्यः संषोडशी तथा ॥
वाजपेयातिरात्रश्च आप्योर्यामः श्रुतौ श्रुतः ॥7॥
1.186.m:
The Agniṣṭoma, Atyagniṣṭoma, Ukthya, Ṣoḍaśin,
Vājapeya, Atirātra, and Āptoryāma are recorded in the Veda.

1.186.s:
dayā syātsarvabhūteṣu anasūyātha maṃgalam ..
kṣāṃtirdayā tvanāyāsaḥ śaucamaspṛhatā vratam .. 8 ..
1.186.d:
दया स्यात्सर्वभूतेषु अनसूयाथ मंगलम् ॥
क्षांतिर्दया त्वनायासः शौचमस्पृहता व्रतम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.186.m:
There should be compassion toward all beings, absence of envy, auspiciousness,
forbearance, kindness, lack of strain, purity, absence of greed, and vows.

1.186.s:
samyaguktāstu saṃskārā brahmaprāptinimittakāḥ ..
anaṃtaraṃ pravakṣyāmi viprāṇāṃ vṛttayaḥ śubhāḥ .. 9 ..
1.186.d:
सम्यगुक्तास्तु संस्कारा ब्रह्मप्राप्तिनिमित्तकाः ॥
अनंतरं प्रवक्ष्यामि विप्राणां वृत्तयः शुभाः ॥ 9 ॥
1.186.m:
These purificatory rites aimed at attaining Brahman have been duly spoken of;
next I shall declare the auspicious livelihoods of brāhmaṇas.

1.186.s:
ṛtāmṛte ca viprāṇāmṛtaṃ pramṛtameva ca ..
pratigrahavaṇijyādi śreyasī nottarottarā .. 1.186.10 ..
1.186.d:
ऋतामृते च विप्राणामृतं प्रमृतमेव च ॥
प्रतिग्रहवणिज्यादि श्रेयसी नोत्तरोत्तरा ॥ 1.186.10 ॥
1.186.m:
For brāhmaṇas there are Ṛta and Amṛta, as well as Mṛta and Pramṛta;
acceptance of gifts, trade, and the like—each later one is not superior [to the former].

1.186.s:
ājīvikāvṛttayastu ityādyāḥ saṃpravartitāḥ ..
tāsāṃ kayāpi jīvettu anutiṣṭhedyathāvidhi .. 11 ..
1.186.d:
आजीविकावृत्तयस्तु इत्याद्याः संप्रवर्तिताः ॥
तासां कयापि जीवेत्तु अनुतिष्ठेद्यथाविधि ॥ 11 ॥
1.186.m:
Such occupations have been set forth for livelihood;
living by any one of them, one should perform [rites] according to rule.

1.186.s:
nityaṃ śuciḥ sugaṃdhaśca snānaśīlaḥ priyaṃvadaḥ ..
pūjyaśca pūjayeddevānkāryāṇi svayamācaret .. 12 ..
1.186.d:
नित्यं शुचिः सुगंधश्च स्नानशीलः प्रियंवदः ॥
पूज्यश्च पूजयेद्देवान्कार्याणि स्वयमाचरेत् ॥ 12 ॥
1.186.m:
Constantly clean, fragrant, accustomed to bathing, speaking kindly,
and worthy of honour, one should worship the gods and conduct affairs oneself.

1.186.s:
nekṣetārkaṃ na nagnāṃ strīṃ na ca saṃspṛṣṭa maithunam ..
nāpsu mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vā nāśucī rātritārakāḥ .. 13 ..
1.186.d:
नेक्षेतार्कं न नग्नां स्त्रीं न च संस्पृष्ट मैथुनम् ॥
नाप्सु मूत्रं पुरीषं वा नाशुची रात्रितारकाः ॥ 13 ॥
1.186.m:
One should not look at the [rising/setting] sun, nor at a naked woman, nor at copulation taking place,
nor pass urine or faeces in water, nor gaze while impure at the stars of the night.

1.186.s:
śāstroktā yaṃtraṇā yā tu nānuktāni vratāni ca ..
svargārthaṃ sādhayettaiśca śaktimānmanasā tathā ..14..
1.186.d:
शास्त्रोक्ता यंत्रणा या तु नानुक्तानि व्रतानि च ॥
स्वर्गार्थं साधयेत्तैश्च शक्तिमान्मनसा तथा ॥14॥
1.186.m:
With whatever restraint is taught in scripture, and with vows not prohibited,
one who is capable should achieve heaven through them, and likewise in mind.

1.186.s:
nityāni kecidicchaṃti kāmyāni ca tathāpare ..
kāmyāpravṛttau saṃge ca prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate ..15..
1.186.d:
नित्यानि केचिदिच्छंति काम्यानि च तथापरे ॥
काम्याप्रवृत्तौ संगे च प्रायश्चित्तं विधीयते ॥15॥
1.186.m:
Some desire regular rites, and others desire optional rites;
if an optional rite is not begun, or if there is attachment [to the fruit], an expiation is prescribed.

1.186.s:
vratāni manasā tviṣṭasaṃkalpa iti mānasaḥ ..
aṃtarānuphalaṃ yattadṛṣivādāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ..16..
1.186.d:
व्रतानि मनसा त्विष्टसंकल्प इति मानसः ॥
अंतरानुफलं यत्तदृषिवादाः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥16॥
1.186.m:
Vows are mental when their desired resolve is made in the mind;
that which brings an intermediate fruit is proclaimed in the sayings of the ṛṣis.

1.186.s:
anadhyāyaṃ svayaṃ samyagvarjayetphalasādhanam ..
ātmā śuddhastathā deśo hyasuhāraḥ prajāpadaḥ .. 17 ..
1.186.d:
अनध्यायं स्वयं सम्यग्वर्जयेत्फलसाधनम् ॥
आत्मा शुद्धस्तथा देशो ह्यसुहारः प्रजापदः ॥ 17 ॥
1.186.m:
One should oneself properly avoid a time unsuitable for Vedic study, which accomplishes the result.
The self should be pure, and likewise the place; life-taking brings calamity to progeny.

1.186.s:
aśubhāni nimittāni utpāto vikṛtaṃ tathā ..
parvāṇi manaso'śuddhiranadhyāya iti smṛtaḥ ..18..
1.186.d:
अशुभानि निमित्तानि उत्पातो विकृतं तथा ॥
पर्वाणि मनसोऽशुद्धिरनध्याय इति स्मृतः ॥18॥
1.186.m:
Inauspicious omens, portents, unnatural events,
the transitional days of the lunar month, and impurity of mind are considered times unsuitable for study.

1.186.s:
anadhyāyāśca dṛṣṭārthā adṛṣṭārthāstathāpare ..
vedādhyayanameveti tridhā maddhyānadarśanam ..19..
1.186.d:
अनध्यायाश्च दृष्टार्था अदृष्टार्थास्तथापरे ॥
वेदाध्ययनमेवेति त्रिधा मद्ध्यानदर्शनम् ॥19॥
1.186.m:
Some times unsuitable for study have visible purposes, while others have invisible purposes.
In this way, study of the Veda is viewed as threefold by my doctrine.

1.186.s:
abhakṣyaṃ sarvavarṇānāṃ śāvāśaucaṃ khagādhipa ..
dravyaśuddhistathaiva syādanyathā tvasamaṃjasam ..1.186.20..
1.186.d:
अभक्ष्यं सर्ववर्णानां शावाशौचं खगाधिप ॥
द्रव्यशुद्धिस्तथैव स्यादन्यथा त्वसमंजसम् ॥1.186.20॥
1.186.m:
Inedible food is forbidden to all social classes, as is impurity from death, O king of birds;
purification of articles must be observed likewise, for otherwise there is impropriety.

1.186.s:
jātiduṣṭaṃ kriyāduṣṭaṃ kāladuṣṭaṃ vibhūṣitam..
saṃsargāśrayaduṣṭaṃ ca sahṛllekhaṃ svabhāvataḥ ..21..
1.186.d:
जातिदुष्टं क्रियादुष्टं कालदुष्टं विभूषितम्॥
संसर्गाश्रयदुष्टं च सहृल्लेखं स्वभावतः ॥21॥
1.186.m:
Food ruined by its species, ruined by preparation, ruined by time, though garnished,
ruined by contact, ruined by its container, and causing nausea by its very nature;

1.186.s:
laśunaṃ gṛṃjanaṃ caiva palāṃḍuṃ kavakāni ca ..
vārtākaṃ nālikeraṃ tu mūlakaṃ jātiduṣṭakam..22..
1.186.d:
लशुनं गृंजनं चैव पलांडुं कवकानि च ॥
वार्ताकं नालिकेरं तु मूलकं जातिदुष्टकम्॥22॥
1.186.m:
Garlic, carrots, onions, and mushrooms,
eggplant, coconut, and radish are ruined by their species.

1.186.s:
no bhuñjīta kriyāduṣṭaṃ duṣṭaṃ ca patitaiḥ pṛthak..
kāladuṣṭaṃ tu vijñeyaṃ hānidaṃ cirasaṃsthitam ..23..
1.186.d:
नो भुञ्जीत क्रियादुष्टं दुष्टं च पतितैः पृथक्॥
कालदुष्टं तु विज्ञेयं हानिदं चिरसंस्थितम् ॥23॥
1.186.m:
One should not eat what is ruined by preparation, nor what has been separately spoiled by outcasts;
and food ruined by time should be known as harmful if it has stood for a long period.

1.186.s: dadhibhakṣyavikārāśca madhuvarjyāstadiṣyate ..24..
1.186.d: दधिभक्ष्यविकाराश्च मधुवर्ज्यास्तदिष्यते ॥24॥
1.186.m: Preparations made from curd and flour, excluding honey, are approved in such a case.

1.186.s:
surālaśunasaṃspṛṣṭaṃ peyūṣādisamanvitam ..
saṃsargaduṣṭametaddhi śunocchiṣṭaṃ khageśvara..25..
1.186.d:
सुरालशुनसंस्पृष्टं पेयूषादिसमन्वितम् ॥
संसर्गदुष्टमेतद्धि शुनोच्छिष्टं खगेश्वर॥25॥
1.186.m:
Food touched by liquor or garlic, or mixed with biestings and the like,
is ruined by contact, as is food left over by a dog, O lord of birds.

1.186.s:
śūdrasaktaṃ khaṃḍasaktaṃ jñeyamāśrayadūṣitam..
vicikitsā tu hṛdaye bhakṣye yasmintsujāyate..26..
1.186.d:
शूद्रसक्तं खंडसक्तं ज्ञेयमाश्रयदूषितम्॥
विचिकित्सा तु हृदये भक्ष्ये यस्मिन्त्सुजायते॥26॥
1.186.m:
Food adhering to a Śūdra or to a fragment is known as spoiled by its container.
When doubt arises in the heart regarding an edible item,

1.186.s:
sahṛllekhaṃ tu tajjñeyaṃ purīṣaṃ tu svabhāvataḥ ..
rasaduṣṭe vikāro'pi rasasyeti pradarśitaḥ..27..
1.186.d:
सहृल्लेखं तु तज्ज्ञेयं पुरीषं तु स्वभावतः ॥
रसदुष्टे विकारोऽपि रसस्येति प्रदर्शितः॥27॥
1.186.m:
that is to be known as causing nausea, while feces is impure by its very nature.
When the flavor is spoiled, the modification of the taste is likewise shown.

1.186.s:
pāyasaṃ kṣīrapākādi tasminneva dine tathā..
yathāśāstraṃ khagaśreṣṭha bhakṣyābhakṣye nirūpayet..28..
1.186.d:
पायसं क्षीरपाकादि तस्मिन्नेव दिने तथा॥
यथाशास्त्रं खगश्रेष्ठ भक्ष्याभक्ष्ये निरूपयेत्॥28॥
1.186.m:
Rice cooked in milk, milk-dishes, and the like must be consumed on that very day.
According to the treatise, O best of birds, one should determine what is edible and inedible.

1.186.s:
prāṇātyaye prokṣitaṃ ca śrāddhe ca dvijakāmyayā ..
pitṝndevāṃścārpayitvā bhuṃjanmāṃsaṃ na doṣabhāk..29..
1.186.d:
प्राणात्यये प्रोक्षितं च श्राद्धे च द्विजकाम्यया ॥
पितॄन्देवांश्चार्पयित्वा भुंजन्मांसं न दोषभाक्॥29॥
1.186.m:
When life is in danger, when it is consecrated with water, or in an ancestral rite at the wish of a twice-born,
one incurs no sin by eating meat after having offered it to the ancestors and the gods.

1.186.s:
pretāśuddhiḥ sapiṃḍānāṃ tasminneva mṛte sati..
daśāhaṃ dvādaśāhaṃ vā pakṣaṃ māsaṃ tvaśuddhatā .. 1.186.30 ..
1.186.d:
प्रेताशुद्धिः सपिंडानां तस्मिन्नेव मृते सति॥
दशाहं द्वादशाहं वा पक्षं मासं त्वशुद्धता ॥ 1.186.30 ॥
1.186.m:
Impurity due to a deceased person applies to sapinda-kinsmen upon their death;
the impurity lasts for ten days, twelve days, a fortnight, or a month.

1.186.s:
daśāhāditrike bhāge varṇaśo na bhavaṃti hi ..
daśāhena tu bhojyāḥ syuḥ sūtakāśaucayostathā .. 31..
1.186.d:
दशाहादित्रिके भागे वर्णशो न भवंति हि ॥
दशाहेन तु भोज्याः स्युः सूतकाशौचयोस्तथा ॥ 31॥
1.186.m:
In the triad of periods beginning with ten days, it does not apply strictly by class;
for ten days they may eat food together during impurity caused by birth or death.

1.186.s:
ūrdhvaṃ daśāhādekāhaśravaṇe sati jāyate ..
saṃvatsare vyatīte tu snānādeva viśudhyati .. 32 ..
1.186.d:
ऊर्ध्वं दशाहादेकाहश्रवणे सति जायते ॥
संवत्सरे व्यतीते तु स्नानादेव विशुध्यति ॥ 32 ॥
1.186.m:
After ten days have passed, an impurity of one day occurs upon hearing of it;
when a full year has elapsed, however, one becomes pure merely by bathing.

1.186.s:
samānodakatā proktā janmanāmnoraparyaye ..
sapiṃḍāḥ saptapuruṣāḥ śrutāvetannidarśanam .. 33 ..
1.186.d:
समानोदकता प्रोक्ता जन्मनाम्नोरपर्यये ॥
सपिंडाः सप्तपुरुषाः श्रुतावेतन्निदर्शनम् ॥ 33 ॥
1.186.m:
The relationship of samānodaka is declared as long as birth and name are remembered;
sapiṇḍas extend to seven generations, as is exemplified in Vedic tradition.

1.186.s:
ā daṃtajanmanaḥ sadya ācūḍānnaiṣṭhikī smṛtā ..
trirātramāvratādeśātsapiṃḍeṣu mṛteṣu ca .. 34 ..
1.186.d:
आ दंतजन्मनः सद्य आचूडान्नैष्ठिकी स्मृता ॥
त्रिरात्रमाव्रतादेशात्सपिंडेषु मृतेषु च ॥ 34 ॥
1.186.m:
Until the eruption of teeth, purity is immediate; until tonsure, it is observed as fixed;
for three nights after tonsure until investiture, when sapiṇḍas die.

1.186.s:
teṣāmapi tadekaṃ syādvayovasthāpyapekṣyate ..
samānodakāttrirātreṇa śudhyedvai mṛtyujanmanoḥ .. 35 ..
1.186.d:
तेषामपि तदेकं स्याद्वयोवस्थाप्यपेक्ष्यते ॥
समानोदकात्त्रिरात्रेण शुध्येद्वै मृत्युजन्मनोः ॥ 35 ॥
1.186.m:
For them too, it may be for one day, and the stage of age is also taken into account.
Through a samānodaka, one is purified in three nights in matters of death and birth.

1.186.s:
garbhasrāve trirātreṇa udakyā śudhyate tathā ..
anaṃtajanma maraṇe taccheṣeṇa viśudhyati .. 36 ..
1.186.d:
गर्भस्रावे त्रिरात्रेण उदक्या शुध्यते तथा ॥
अनंतजन्म मरणे तच्छेषेण विशुध्यति ॥ 36 ॥
1.186.m:
In case of miscarriage, a menstruating woman is purified in three nights;
upon death following another birth, she is purified by the remainder of that period.

1.186.s:
dvijānāṃ tvevameva syātpitrarthaṃ mātureva vā ..
agnihotrārthaṃ vijñeyaṃ sadyaḥ śaucamiti sthitiḥ ..37..
1.186.d:
द्विजानां त्वेवमेव स्यात्पित्रर्थं मातुरेव वा ॥
अग्निहोत्रार्थं विज्ञेयं सद्यः शौचमिति स्थितिः ॥37॥
1.186.m:
For twice-born men it is just so, on account of the father or indeed the mother;
for the purpose of the Agnihotra fire, immediate purity is known to be the rule.

1.186.s:
asapiṃḍe tu nirhārāttrirātramapi mānavaḥ ..
tasyaivānugatau jñeyaṃ sadyaḥ śaucaṃ khagādhipa .. 38 ..
1.186.d:
असपिंडे तु निर्हारात्त्रिरात्रमपि मानवः ॥
तस्यैवानुगतौ ज्ञेयं सद्यः शौचं खगाधिप ॥ 38 ॥
1.186.m:
In the case of a non-sapiṇḍa, a person becomes impure for three nights from carrying the corpse;
if merely following it, immediate purity is known, O lord of birds.

1.186.s:
śudhyeddvijo daśāhena janmahānau dviyoniṣu ..
ṣaṅbhistribhirahai kena kṣatraviṭśūdrayoniṣu .. 39 ..
1.186.d:
शुध्येद्द्विजो दशाहेन जन्महानौ द्वियोनिषु ॥
षङ्भिस्त्रिभिरहै केन क्षत्रविट्शूद्रयोनिषु ॥ 39 ॥
1.186.m:
A twice-born man is purified in ten days upon birth or death in families of twice-born origin;
in six, three, or one day among descendants of Kṣatriyas, Vaiśyas, and Śūdras.

1.186.s:
uktaśaucaṃ yathānyāyaṃ śārīraṃ tattvadarśibhiḥ ..
dravyaśuddhividhānaṃ tu yathāvadabhidhīyate .. 1.186.40 ..
1.186.d:
उक्तशौचं यथान्यायं शारीरं तत्त्वदर्शिभिः ॥
द्रव्यशुद्धिविधानं तु यथावदभिधीयते ॥ 1.186.40 ॥
1.186.m:
Bodily purity has been properly declared by the seers of truth;
now the procedure for the purification of articles is stated as it truly is.

1.186.s:
taijasī mārtikī vīra vāriśuddhiḥ smṛtā tathā ..
nirlepakṣālanenaiva sparśe tu prokṣaṇena vai .. 41 ..
1.186.d:
तैजसी मार्तिकी वीर वारिशुद्धिः स्मृता तथा ॥
निर्लेपक्षालनेनैव स्पर्शे तु प्रोक्षणेन वै ॥ 41 ॥
1.186.m:
Purification by fire, by earth, and likewise by water is remembered, O hero:
by wiping off stains and washing, or merely by sprinkling with water upon contact.

1.186.s:
aśuddhaṃ naiva kiṃciddhi dravyamastīti khecara ..
vacanācchuddhyaśuddhī tu dravyāṇāmiha khecara .. 42 ..
1.186.d:
अशुद्धं नैव किंचिद्धि द्रव्यमस्तीति खेचर ॥
वचनाच्छुद्ध्यशुद्धी तु द्रव्याणामिह खेचर ॥ 42 ॥
1.186.m:
Indeed, no substance is inherently impure, O sky-wanderer;
purity and impurity of objects in this world exist entirely through scriptural injunction, O sky-wanderer.

1.186.s:
snānaṃ śaucaṃ ca kartavyaṃ dravyaśaucādanaṃtaram ..
prātaḥsnānaṃ tu nityaṃ syādgrahaṇe kāmyameva ca .. 43 ..
1.186.d:
स्नानं शौचं च कर्तव्यं द्रव्यशौचादनंतरम् ॥
प्रातःस्नानं तु नित्यं स्याद्ग्रहणे काम्यमेव च ॥ 43 ॥
1.186.m:
Bathing and purification should be performed immediately after the purification of articles;
the morning bath is obligatory, while that during an eclipse is optional.

1.186.s:
naimittikaṃ kṣurāśaucaṃ tena pāpādviśudhyati ..
uktaṃ tu śaucaṃ vijñeyaṃ doṣakṣayakaraṃ khaga .. 44 ..
1.186.d:
नैमित्तिकं क्षुराशौचं तेन पापाद्विशुध्यति ॥
उक्तं तु शौचं विज्ञेयं दोषक्षयकरं खग ॥ 44 ॥
1.186.m:
Occasional is the impurity from shaving, through which one is cleansed of sin;
the declared purification, O bird, should be understood as destroying flaws.

1.186.s:
karmāṃgaṃ ceti vijñeyaṃ ṣaṭprakārā samāsataḥ ..
evamācamanaṃ vidyādviśiṣṭaṃ tu dvijanmanām ..45..
1.186.d:
कर्मांगं चेति विज्ञेयं षट्प्रकारा समासतः ॥
एवमाचमनं विद्याद्विशिष्टं तु द्विजन्मनाम् ॥45॥
1.186.m:
It should be understood as an auxiliary of rites, sixfold in brief;
thus one should know sipping water as especially prescribed for twice-born men.

1.186.s:
tadā mṛtānāṃ tadvatsyādanyeṣāṃ tu yathāsukham ..
kanyānivṛttiṃ putraistu yathānyāyaṃ samācaret.. 46 ..
1.186.d:
तदा मृतानां तद्वत्स्यादन्येषां तु यथासुखम् ॥
कन्यानिवृत्तिं पुत्रैस्तु यथान्यायं समाचरेत्॥ 46 ॥
1.186.m:
Then it applies likewise to those who have died; for others, however, it is according to convenience.
The marriage of daughters should be properly performed by the sons.

1.186.s: kalāśilpānisarvāṇi gṛhrīyātparituṣṭaye .. 47 ..
1.186.d: कलाशिल्पानिसर्वाणि गृह्रीयात्परितुष्टये ॥ 47 ॥
1.186.m: One should acquire all arts and crafts for personal satisfaction.

1.186.s:
śuśrūṣeta patiṃ bhāryā paritoṣaṃ yathā vrajet ..
gurūṇāṃ paritoṣaśca dharmaḥ strīṇāṃ sanātanaḥ..48..
1.186.d:
शुश्रूषेत पतिं भार्या परितोषं यथा व्रजेत् ॥
गुरूणां परितोषश्च धर्मः स्त्रीणां सनातनः॥48॥
1.186.m:
A wife should serve her husband so that he attains contentment;
and pleasing the elders is the eternal duty of women.

1.186.s:
vṛddhā'putrā yadi mṛtā tadabhāve nṛpasya tu ..
mṛtāpatyāpyagarbhā ca vṛddhāpatyā pativratā .. 49 ..
1.186.d:
वृद्धाऽपुत्रा यदि मृता तदभावे नृपस्य तु ॥
मृतापत्याप्यगर्भा च वृद्धापत्या पतिव्रता ॥ 49 ॥
1.186.m:
If an old woman dies without sons, then in the absence of [heirs], her property goes to the king;
whether her children have died, or she is barren, or her children are grown, a faithful wife

1.186.s:
kuryādanirvṛtaṃ bharturgate sannihitepi vā ..
etāṃ dharma samāṃ niṣṭhāṃ bhartṛlokamavāpnuyāt ..1.186.50..
1.186.d:
कुर्यादनिर्वृतं भर्तुर्गते सन्निहितेपि वा ॥
एतां धर्म समां निष्ठां भर्तृलोकमवाप्नुयात् ॥1.186.50॥
1.186.m:
should perform her husband’s unfinished duty, whether he has departed or is present;
observing this steadfast devotion equal to righteousness, she attains her husband's world.

1.186.s:
strī dharmacāriṇī sādhvī mṛtā dāhyā tathāgnibhiḥ ..
viparītādadāhyā tu punardārakriyā tathā ..51..
1.186.d:
स्त्री धर्मचारिणी साध्वी मृता दाह्या तथाग्निभिः ॥
विपरीताददाह्या तु पुनर्दारक्रिया तथा ॥51॥
1.186.m:
A virtuous wife who lives righteously should, upon death, be cremated with fires;
if she is the opposite, she is not to be cremated, and the rite of taking another wife [may be performed].

1.186.s:
strīṇāṃ niyogo vihito maraṇādbrahmacārakam ..
prāptavyaśca yathādharmo dṛṣṭādṛṣṭaphalapradaḥ .. 52 ..
1.186.d:
स्त्रीणां नियोगो विहितो मरणाद्ब्रह्मचारकम् ॥
प्राप्तव्यश्च यथाधर्मो दृष्टादृष्टफलप्रदः ॥ 52 ॥
1.186.m:
For women, appointment is ordained, or celibacy following the husband’s death;
and righteous duty, yielding visible and invisible results, is to be pursued.

1.186.s:
tasmāddharmaṃ sadā kuryātkurvatī svargamāpnuyāt .. 53 ..
sauradharme dhenumāhātmyavarṇanam
1.186.d:
तस्माद्धर्मं सदा कुर्यात्कुर्वती स्वर्गमाप्नुयात् ॥ 53 ॥
सौरधर्मे धेनुमाहात्म्यवर्णनम्
1.186.m:
Therefore, she should always practice virtue; practicing it, she attains heaven.
In the Solar Ordinances: Description of the Greatness of the Cow.

1.187.s:
.. anūruruvāca .. ..
kāni puṇyāni kṛtveha svargaṃ gacchaṃti mānavāḥ ..
manuṣyaloke saṃbhūtāḥ svarloke gāminaḥ param ..1..
1.187.d:
॥ अनूरुरुवाच ॥ ॥
कानि पुण्यानि कृत्वेह स्वर्गं गच्छंति मानवाः ॥
मनुष्यलोके संभूताः स्वर्लोके गामिनः परम् ॥1॥
1.187.m:
Anūru said:
By performing what merits here do men go to heaven?
Born in the world of mortals, how do they proceed to the supreme celestial realm?

1.187.s:
karmayajñastapoyajñaḥ svādhyāyo dhyānanirmitaḥ ..
jñānayajñaśca paṃcaite mahāyajñāḥ prakīrtitāḥ .. 2 ..
1.187.d:
कर्मयज्ञस्तपोयज्ञः स्वाध्यायो ध्याननिर्मितः ॥
ज्ञानयज्ञश्च पंचैते महायज्ञाः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ 2 ॥
1.187.m:
The sacrifice of action, the sacrifice of penance, private recitation, that made of meditation,
and the sacrifice of knowledge: these five are proclaimed as great sacrifices.

1.187.s:
eteṣāmeva yajñānāmuttamaḥ katamaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
etadyajñaphalānāṃ ca kiṃ phalaṃ kā gatirbhavet ..3..
1.187.d:
एतेषामेव यज्ञानामुत्तमः कतमः स्मृतः ॥
एतद्यज्ञफलानां च किं फलं का गतिर्भवेत् ॥3॥
1.187.m:
Among these very sacrifices, which one is considered the best?
And what is the fruit of the fruits of these sacrifices, and what will be the destination?

1.187.s:
dharmādharmaprabhedāśca kiyantaḥ parikīrtitāḥ ..
tatsādhanāni katidhā gatayaśca yathā vada ..4..
1.187.d:
धर्माधर्मप्रभेदाश्च कियन्तः परिकीर्तिताः ॥
तत्साधनानि कतिधा गतयश्च यथा वद ॥4॥
1.187.m:
How many divisions of righteousness and unrighteousness are proclaimed?
In how many ways are their means accomplished, and what are the destinations? Tell me.

1.187.s:
khaga nārakiṇāṃ puṃsāmāgatānāṃ punaḥ kṣitau ..
kāni cihnāni jāyante muktaśeṣeṇa karmaṇā .. 5 ..
1.187.d:
खग नारकिणां पुंसामागतानां पुनः क्षितौ ॥
कानि चिह्नानि जायन्ते मुक्तशेषेण कर्मणा ॥ 5 ॥
1.187.m:
O bird, for men who were in hell and have returned once more to earth,
what signs appear as a remnant of their discharged karma?

1.187.s:
mahābhavārṇavādghorāddharmādharmābhisaṃkulāt ..
garbhādiduḥkhaphenāḍhyānmucyaṃte dehinaḥ katham .. .. 6 ..
1.187.d:
महाभवार्णवाद्घोराद्धर्माधर्माभिसंकुलात् ॥
गर्भादिदुःखफेनाढ्यान्मुच्यंते देहिनः कथम् ॥ ॥ 6 ॥
1.187.m:
From the dreadful, great ocean of mundane existence, thronged with virtue and vice,
rich with the foam of the suffering of the womb and so forth, how are embodied beings released?

1.187.s:
ityukto bhagavānbhānuḥ sarvapraśnārthamādarāt .. 7 ..
pratyuvāca mahātejāḥ samāsavyāsayogataḥ .. 7 ..
1.187.d:
इत्युक्तो भगवान्भानुः सर्वप्रश्नार्थमादरात् ॥ 7 ॥
प्रत्युवाच महातेजाः समासव्यासयोगतः ॥ 7 ॥
1.187.m:
Having been thus addressed, the blessed Sun, for the sake of all these questions, with care
replied, possessed of great splendour, by means of summary and expansion.

1.187.s:
.. āditya uvāca .. ..
svargāpavargaphaladaṃ narakārṇavatāraṇam ..
dharmaṃ pāpaharaṃ puṇyaṃ śṛṇu śūra prabhāṣataḥ .. 8 ..
1.187.d:
॥ आदित्य उवाच ॥ ॥
स्वर्गापवर्गफलदं नरकार्णवतारणम् ॥
धर्मं पापहरं पुण्यं शृणु शूर प्रभाषतः ॥ 8 ॥
1.187.m:
Āditya said:
Listen, O hero, as I speak of righteous duty, which bestows the fruits of heaven and final liberation, / carries [one] across the ocean of hell, removes sin, and is meritorious.

1.187.s:
śraddhāpūrvaḥ sadā dharmaḥ śraddhāmadhyāṃtasaṃsthitaḥ ..
śraddhāniṣṭhapratiṣṭhaśca dharmaḥ śraddhā prakīrtitā .. 9 ..
1.187.d:
श्रद्धापूर्वः सदा धर्मः श्रद्धामध्यांतसंस्थितः ॥
श्रद्धानिष्ठप्रतिष्ठश्च धर्मः श्रद्धा प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 9 ॥
1.187.m: Righteous duty always begins with faith, is established with faith in its middle and end, / and has its foundation in the steadfastness of faith; righteous duty is proclaimed to be faith itself.

1.187.s:
śrutimaṃtrarasāḥ sūkṣmāḥ pradhānapuruṣeśvaraḥ ..
śraddhāmātreṇa gṛhyaṃte na pareṇa ca cakṣuṣā .. 1.187.10 ..
1.187.d:
श्रुतिमंत्ररसाः सूक्ष्माः प्रधानपुरुषेश्वरः ॥
श्रद्धामात्रेण गृह्यंते न परेण च चक्षुषा ॥ 1.187.10 ॥
1.187.m: The subtle essences of the Vedic mantras, nature, the cosmic person, and the supreme Lord— / these are grasped through faith alone, and not by any other eye.

1.187.s:
kāyakleśairna bahubhirna caivārthasya rāśibhiḥ ..
dharmaḥ saṃprāpyate sūkṣmaḥ śraddhāhīnaiḥ surairapi .. 11 ..
1.187.d:
कायक्लेशैर्न बहुभिर्न चैवार्थस्य राशिभिः ॥
धर्मः संप्राप्यते सूक्ष्मः श्रद्धाहीनैः सुरैरपि ॥ 11 ॥
1.187.m: Neither by many bodily afflictions nor by heaps of wealth / is subtle righteous duty attained, even by the gods, if they are devoid of faith.

1.187.s:
śraddhā dharmaḥ paraḥ sūkṣmaḥ śraddhā yajñāhutaṃ tapaḥ..
śraddhā mokṣaśca svargaśca śraddhā sarvamidaṃ jagat .. 12 ..
1.187.d:
श्रद्धा धर्मः परः सूक्ष्मः श्रद्धा यज्ञाहुतं तपः॥
श्रद्धा मोक्षश्च स्वर्गश्च श्रद्धा सर्वमिदं जगत् ॥ 12 ॥
1.187.m: Faith is the supreme, subtle righteous duty; faith is the sacrifice, the oblation, and asceticism; / faith is both liberation and heaven; faith is this entire world.

1.187.s:
sarvasvaṃ jīvitaṃ vāpi dadyādaśraddhayā ca yaḥ ..
nāpnuyātsa phalaṃ kiṃcittasmācchraddhāparo bhavet ...13 ..
1.187.d:
सर्वस्वं जीवितं वापि दद्यादश्रद्धया च यः ॥
नाप्नुयात्स फलं किंचित्तस्माच्छ्रद्धापरो भवेत् ॥.13 ॥
1.187.m: Even if one were to give one’s all, or even one’s very life, without faith, / one would not obtain any fruit; therefore, one should be dedicated to faith.

1.187.s:
evaṃ śraddhāmayāḥ sarve mama dharmāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ..
pūjyastu śraddhayā puṃsā dhyeyaḥ pūjyaśca śraddhayā .. 14 ..
1.187.d:
एवं श्रद्धामयाः सर्वे मम धर्माः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
पूज्यस्तु श्रद्धया पुंसा ध्येयः पूज्यश्च श्रद्धया ॥ 14 ॥
1.187.m: Thus all my righteous duties are proclaimed to consist of faith. / He should be worshipped with faith by a man; he is to be meditated upon and worshipped with faith.

1.187.s:
adhikārasya prāptyarthaṃ mahāsāravimuktidam ..
ajñāduktaṃ sasaṃdigdhaṃ vākyametanmamādbhutam .. 15 ..
1.187.d:
अधिकारस्य प्राप्त्यर्थं महासारविमुक्तिदम् ॥
अज्ञादुक्तं ससंदिग्धं वाक्यमेतन्ममाद्भुतम् ॥ 15 ॥
1.187.m: In order to attain qualification, granting supreme substance and liberation, / this wonderful word of mine was spoken by the unknowing one, full of doubt:

1.187.s:
nānāsiddhikaraṃ divyaṃ lokacittānuraṃjanam ..
suniścitārthagaṃbhīraṃ vākyaṃ mama manoramam .. 16 ..
1.187.d:
नानासिद्धिकरं दिव्यं लोकचित्तानुरंजनम् ॥
सुनिश्चितार्थगंभीरं वाक्यं मम मनोरमम् ॥ 16 ॥
1.187.m: Delighting the hearts of the world, divine, yielding various supernatural powers, / profound with well-ascertained meaning, is my delightful word.

1.187.s:
manmānasasamudro hi dvipadoyaṃ vidurbudhāḥ ..
sa khaṣolketi vikhyātaḥ saśivaṃ maṃḍalaṃ khaga .. 17 ..
1.187.d:
मन्मानससमुद्रो हि द्विपदोयं विदुर्बुधाः ॥
स खषोल्केति विख्यातः सशिवं मंडलं खग ॥ 17 ॥
1.187.m: For the wise know that this two-footed being is the ocean of my mind; / he is renowned as Khaṣolka, O bird, an orb accompanied by Śiva.

1.187.s:
devatrayaguṇātītaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavitprabhuḥ ..
omityekākṣare maṃtre sthitaḥ sa paramo mama ..18..
1.187.d:
देवत्रयगुणातीतः सर्वज्ञः सर्ववित्प्रभुः ॥
ओमित्येकाक्षरे मंत्रे स्थितः स परमो मम ॥18॥
1.187.m: Transcending the qualities of the triad of deities, all-knowing, all-understanding, the Lord, / abiding in the single-syllable mantra 'Oṃ'—he is my supreme [form].

1.187.s:
yathānādipravṛttoyaṃ ghoraḥ saṃsārasāgaraḥ ..
khaṣolkopi tathānādiḥ saṃsārārṇavaśodhanaḥ ..19..
1.187.d:
यथानादिप्रवृत्तोयं घोरः संसारसागरः ॥
खषोल्कोपि तथानादिः संसारार्णवशोधनः ॥19॥
1.187.m: Just as this terrible ocean of transmigratory existence has proceeded from beginningless time, / so too is Khaṣolka beginningless, the purifier of the ocean of transmigratory existence.

1.187.s:
vyādhīnāṃ bheṣajaṃ yadvatpra tipakṣasvabhāvataḥ ..
mokṣiṇāṃ muktihetuśca siddhaḥ sarvārthasādhakaḥ .. 1.187.20 ..
1.187.d:
व्याधीनां भेषजं यद्वत्प्र तिपक्षस्वभावतः ॥
मोक्षिणां मुक्तिहेतुश्च सिद्धः सर्वार्थसाधकः ॥ 1.187.20 ॥
1.187.m: Just as medicine cures diseases by its counteracting nature, / he is the cause of liberation for seekers of release, accomplished, the fulfiller of all aims.

1.187.s:
mamābhidhānamantroyamabhidheyaḥ sadā smṛtaḥ ..
abhidhānābhidheyohaṃ mantrasiddho'smi khecara .. 21 ..
1.187.d:
ममाभिधानमन्त्रोयमभिधेयः सदा स्मृतः ॥
अभिधानाभिधेयोहं मन्त्रसिद्धोऽस्मि खेचर ॥ 21 ॥
1.187.m: This is my name-mantra; he is traditionally remembered as that which is to be designated. / I am both designation and designated; I am accomplished through mantra, O sky-wanderer.

1.187.s:
vedo manogame cātra ṣaḍakṣaramaṃtrasthitaḥ ..
yadvā mukto'kṣaraikena loke pañcākṣaraḥ smṛtaḥ .. 22 ..
1.187.d:
वेदो मनोगमे चात्र षडक्षरमंत्रस्थितः ॥
यद्वा मुक्तोऽक्षरैकेन लोके पञ्चाक्षरः स्मृतः ॥ 22 ॥
1.187.m: And here the Veda, accessible to the mind, resides in the six-syllable mantra; / or, when released of one syllable, it is remembered in the world as having five syllables.

1.187.s:
kiṃ tasya bahubhirmantraiḥ śāstrairvā bahuvistaraiḥ ..
yasyoṃ namaḥ khaṣolketi mantro'yaṃ hṛdi saṃsthitaḥ .. 23 ..
1.187.d:
किं तस्य बहुभिर्मन्त्रैः शास्त्रैर्वा बहुविस्तरैः ॥
यस्यों नमः खषोल्केति मन्त्रोऽयं हृदि संस्थितः ॥ 23 ॥
1.187.m: What need has he of many mantras, or of scriptures of vast extent, / in whose heart resides this mantra: 'Oṃ, homage to Khaṣolka'?

1.187.s:
tenādhītaṃ śrutaṃ tena tena sarvamanuṣṭhitam ..
yenoṃ namaḥ khaṣolketi mama vākyaṃ ṣaḍakṣaram .. 24 ..
1.187.d:
तेनाधीतं श्रुतं तेन तेन सर्वमनुष्ठितम् ॥
येनों नमः खषोल्केति मम वाक्यं षडक्षरम् ॥ 24 ॥
1.187.m: By him it is studied, by him heard, by him all has been performed, / by whom this six-syllable word of mine [is held]: 'Oṃ, homage to Khaṣolka.'

1.187.s:
vidhivākyamidaṃ sarvaṃ nārthavādaṃ vaco mama ..
etatte vakṣyate'śeṣaṃ mama vākyārthamuttamam ..
pṛcchasvemaṃ praṇamyāśu vainateya mahāmate .. 25 ..
1.187.d:
विधिवाक्यमिदं सर्वं नार्थवादं वचो मम ॥
एतत्ते वक्ष्यतेऽशेषं मम वाक्यार्थमुत्तमम् ॥
पृच्छस्वेमं प्रणम्याशु वैनतेय महामते ॥ 25 ॥
1.187.m: All this is an injunction-statement; my speech is not [mere] commendatory discourse. / This excellent meaning of my words will be told to you in its entirety. / Bowing down quickly, ask him, O wise Vainateya.

1.187.s:
.. sumanturuvāca .. ..
śrutvā tu vacanaṃ bhānorvainateyo mahābalaḥ ..
saptāśvatilakaṃ bhaktyā praṇamyovāca bhārata .. 26 ..
1.187.d:
॥ सुमन्तुरुवाच ॥ ॥
श्रुत्वा तु वचनं भानोर्वैनतेयो महाबलः ॥
सप्ताश्वतिलकं भक्त्या प्रणम्योवाच भारत ॥ 26 ॥
1.187.m:
Sumantu said:
Having heard the words of the sun, the mighty Vainateya, / bowing with devotion to Saptāśvatilaka, spoke, O descendant of Bharata.

1.187.s:
.. anūruruvāca .. ..
brūhi māṃ devaśārdūla yatpṛcchāmi mahāmate ..
kīdṛgvākyamidaṃ bhānorvākyārthaṃ brūhi ca prabho .. 27.. ..
1.187.d:
॥ अनूरुरुवाच ॥ ॥
ब्रूहि मां देवशार्दूल यत्पृच्छामि महामते ॥
कीदृग्वाक्यमिदं भानोर्वाक्यार्थं ब्रूहि च प्रभो ॥ 27॥ ॥
1.187.m:
Anūru said:
Speak to me, O tiger among gods, what I ask, O high-minded one; / tell me, O Lord, what kind of word this of the sun is, and the meaning of his words.

1.187.s:
.. saptāśvatilaka uvāca .. ..
vimuktāśeṣadoṣeṇa sarvajñena bhagena yat ..
praṇītamamalaṃ vākyaṃ tatpramāṇaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 28 ..
1.187.d:
॥ सप्ताश्वतिलक उवाच ॥ ॥
विमुक्ताशेषदोषेण सर्वज्ञेन भगेन यत् ॥
प्रणीतममलं वाक्यं तत्प्रमाणं न संशयः ॥ 28 ॥
1.187.m:
Saptāśvatilaka said:
That flawless word which has been composed by the all-knowing Bhaga, / free from all defects, is authoritative without doubt.

1.187.s:
yasmānmārtaṃḍa nāmāsau kathyate ca manīṣibhiḥ ..
yathārthaṃ puṇyamāpnoti patatyaśraddhayā tvadhaḥ .. 29 ..
1.187.d:
यस्मान्मार्तंड नामासौ कथ्यते च मनीषिभिः ॥
यथार्थं पुण्यमाप्नोति पतत्यश्रद्धया त्वधः ॥ 29 ॥
1.187.m: Because he is called Mārtaṇḍa by the wise, / one obtains merit according to reality, but through lack of faith one falls down.

1.187.s:
sauravākyapravaktāraṃ sūravatpūjayedgurum ..
saṃsārārṇava nirmagnaṃ yaḥ samuddharate janam .. 1.187.30 ..
1.187.d:
सौरवाक्यप्रवक्तारं सूरवत्पूजयेद्गुरुम् ॥
संसारार्णव निर्मग्नं यः समुद्धरते जनम् ॥ 1.187.30 ॥
1.187.m: One should worship the guru who proclaims the Saura teaching as if he were the sun, / who rescues a person submerged in the ocean of transmigratory existence.

1.187.s:
sauradharmāmbuhastena kastena sadṛśo guruḥ ..
ajñānavahnisaṃtaptaṃ nirvāpayati yaḥ śanaiḥ ..
jñānāmṛtena vai bhaktā kastaṃ na pratipūjayet .. 31 ..
1.187.d:
सौरधर्माम्बुहस्तेन कस्तेन सदृशो गुरुः ॥
अज्ञानवह्निसंतप्तं निर्वापयति यः शनैः ॥
ज्ञानामृतेन वै भक्ता कस्तं न प्रतिपूजयेत् ॥ 31 ॥
1.187.m: With the hand that holds the water of Saura duty, what guru is equal to him / who gradually extinguishes one scorched by the fire of ignorance? / Who would not worship him devotedly with the nectar of knowledge?

1.187.s:
naiva rājyena mahatā na caivārthasya rāśibhiḥ ..
prāptamajñānaśamanaṃ paraloke sukhāvaham .. 32 ..
1.187.d:
नैव राज्येन महता न चैवार्थस्य राशिभिः ॥
प्राप्तमज्ञानशमनं परलोके सुखावहम् ॥ 32 ॥
1.187.m: Neither by great kingship nor by heaps of wealth / is the quelling of ignorance attained, bringing happiness in the other world.

1.187.s:
svargāpavarga siddhyarthaṃ bhāṣitaṃ yattu śobhanam ..
vākyaṃ te devadevena tadvijñeyaṃ subhāṣitam .. 33 ..
1.187.d:
स्वर्गापवर्ग सिद्ध्यर्थं भाषितं यत्तु शोभनम् ॥
वाक्यं ते देवदेवेन तद्विज्ञेयं सुभाषितम् ॥ 33 ॥
1.187.m: That splendid word which was spoken to you by the god of gods / for the attainment of heaven and final liberation should be known as well-spoken.

1.187.s:
rāgadveṣākṣamākrodhakāmatṛṣṇānusāriṇām ..
vākyaṃ niraya hetutvāttaddurbhāṣitamucyate .. 34 ..
1.187.d:
रागद्वेषाक्षमाक्रोधकामतृष्णानुसारिणाम् ॥
वाक्यं निरय हेतुत्वात्तद्दुर्भाषितमुच्यते ॥ 34 ॥
1.187.m: Because it is the cause of hell, the speech of those who follow / passion, hatred, intolerance, anger, lust, and thirst is called ill-spoken.

1.187.s:
saṃskṛtenāpi kiṃ tena mṛdulālāpasaṃginā ..
avidyārāmavākyena saṃsārakleśahetunā .. 35 ..
1.187.d:
संस्कृतेनापि किं तेन मृदुलालापसंगिना ॥
अविद्यारामवाक्येन संसारक्लेशहेतुना ॥ 35 ॥
1.187.m: What is the use of that speech, though refined, attached to soft prattle, / which is the playground of ignorance and the cause of the afflictions of worldly existence?

1.187.s:
yacchrutvā jāyate puṇyaṃ rāgādīnāṃ ca saṃkṣayaḥ ..
virūpamapi tadvākyaṃ vijñeyamatiśobhanam .. 36 ..
1.187.d:
यच्छ्रुत्वा जायते पुण्यं रागादीनां च संक्षयः ॥
विरूपमपि तद्वाक्यं विज्ञेयमतिशोभनम् ॥ 36 ॥
1.187.m: That word, hearing which merit is born and passion and the rest are destroyed, / even if unpleasing, should be known as exceedingly splendid.

1.187.s:
smṛtayo bhārataṃ vedāḥ śāstrāṇi sumahāṃti ca ..
svāyuṣaḥ kṣapaṇāyaiva dhamo'rthasamagranthitaḥ .. 37 ..
1.187.d:
स्मृतयो भारतं वेदाः शास्त्राणि सुमहांति च ॥
स्वायुषः क्षपणायैव धमोऽर्थसमग्रन्थितः ॥ 37 ॥
1.187.m: The traditional codes of law, the Mahābhārata, the Vedas, and very great treatises— / composed of righteousness and wealth—are merely for the wearing away of one’s lifespan.

1.187.s:
putradārādisaṃsāre narāṇāṃ mūḍhacetasām ..
saṃsāraviduṣāṃ śāstramanādi mukhanirgatam .. 38..
1.187.d:
पुत्रदारादिसंसारे नराणां मूढचेतसाम् ॥
संसारविदुषां शास्त्रमनादि मुखनिर्गतम् ॥ 38॥
1.187.m: In worldly existence consisting of sons, wives, and the rest, for men of deluded minds, / the treatise emerged from the beginningless mouth of those who know worldly existence.

1.187.s:
idaṃ śreṣṭhamidaṃ jñeyaṃ sarvaṃ tvaṃ jñātumicchasi ..
api varṣasahasrāyuḥ śāstrāntaṃ nādhigacchati .. 39 ..
1.187.d:
इदं श्रेष्ठमिदं ज्ञेयं सर्वं त्वं ज्ञातुमिच्छसि ॥
अपि वर्षसहस्रायुः शास्त्रान्तं नाधिगच्छति ॥ 39 ॥
1.187.m: 'This is the best, this is to be known'—you wish to know everything; / even with a lifespan of a thousand years, one does not reach the end of the scriptures.

1.187.s:
vijñāyākṣaratanmātraṃ jīvitaṃ cātivaṃcanam ..
vihāya sarvaśāstrāṇi paralokaṃ samācaret .. 1.187.40 ..
1.187.d:
विज्ञायाक्षरतन्मात्रं जीवितं चातिवंचनम् ॥
विहाय सर्वशास्त्राणि परलोकं समाचरेत् ॥ 1.187.40 ॥
1.187.m: Having understood that the syllable alone [is real] and that life is utter deception, / one should abandon all scriptures and attend to the other world.

1.187.s:
paṇḍitenāpi kiṃ tena samarthena ca dehinām ..
yaḥ puṇyabhāramudvoḍhumaśaktaḥ pāralaukikam .. 41 ..
1.187.d:
पण्डितेनापि किं तेन समर्थेन च देहिनाम् ॥
यः पुण्यभारमुद्वोढुमशक्तः पारलौकिकम् ॥ 41 ॥
1.187.m: What is the use of that scholar, or of that capable person among embodied beings, / who is unable to bear the burden of merit pertaining to the next world?

1.187.s:
paṇḍito'pi sa mūrkhaḥ syācchaktiyukto'pyaśaktikaḥ ..
yaḥ saurajñānamāhātmyamuccārayitumakṣamaḥ .. 42 ..
1.187.d:
पण्डितोऽपि स मूर्खः स्याच्छक्तियुक्तोऽप्यशक्तिकः ॥
यः सौरज्ञानमाहात्म्यमुच्चारयितुमक्षमः ॥ 42 ॥
1.187.m: Even if learned, he would be a fool; even if endowed with power, he is powerless, / who is unable to recite the majesty of Saura knowledge.

1.187.s:
tasmātsa paṃḍitaḥ śaktaḥ sa tapasvī jitendriyaḥ ..
yaḥ saurajñānasadbhāvamālocayitumudyataḥ .. 43 ..
1.187.d:
तस्मात्स पंडितः शक्तः स तपस्वी जितेन्द्रियः ॥
यः सौरज्ञानसद्भावमालोचयितुमुद्यतः ॥ 43 ॥
1.187.m: Therefore, he is learned, he is capable, he is an ascetic who has subdued his senses, / who is intent upon reflecting on the reality of Saura knowledge.

1.187.s:
yaḥ pradadyānnṛpaḥ kṛtsnāṃ kṣmāṃ dhanaṃ kāṃcanaṃ tathā ..
sarvamanyāyataḥ pṛchenna tasyopadiśedguruḥ .. 44 ..
1.187.d:
यः प्रदद्यान्नृपः कृत्स्नां क्ष्मां धनं कांचनं तथा ॥
सर्वमन्यायतः पृछेन्न तस्योपदिशेद्गुरुः ॥ 44 ॥
1.187.m: If a king were to give the entire earth, wealth, and likewise gold, / but should ask everything unjustly, the guru should not instruct him.

1.187.s:
yaḥ śṛṇoti raverdharmaṃ nyāyataḥ sa ca vakti ca ..
tato gacchati susthānaṃ narakaṃ tadviparyaye .. 45 ..
1.187.d:
यः शृणोति रवेर्धर्मं न्यायतः स च वक्ति च ॥
ततो गच्छति सुस्थानं नरकं तद्विपर्यये ॥ 45 ॥
1.187.m: He who listens to the duty of Ravi according to proper method and speaks it, / goes from there to a good state; in the reverse case, to hell.

1.187.s:
dattagodohasaṃbhūtaḥ ṣaḍakṣaravidhānataḥ ..
raviḥ saṃpūjitaḥ śīghraṃ narāṇāṃ tulyatā bhṛśam .. 46 ..
1.187.d:
दत्तगोदोहसंभूतः षडक्षरविधानतः ॥
रविः संपूजितः शीघ्रं नराणां तुल्यता भृशम् ॥ 46 ॥
1.187.m: When Ravi is worshipped with what is produced from the milk of cows given according to the six-syllable rite, / equality with him is swiftly and greatly [attained] by men.

1.187.s:
surāsurairmathyamānātkṣīrodātsāgarātpurā ..
pañca gāvaḥ samutpannāḥ sarvalo kasya mātaraḥ .. 47 ..
1.187.d:
सुरासुरैर्मथ्यमानात्क्षीरोदात्सागरात्पुरा ॥
पञ्च गावः समुत्पन्नाः सर्वलो कस्य मातरः ॥ 47 ॥
1.187.m: Anciently, as the ocean of milk was being churned by the gods and asuras, / five cows were born, the mothers of all the world:

1.187.s:
naṃdā subhadrā surabhī sumanā śobhanāvatī ..
gāvaḥ sūryasamā bhāsā utpannāḥ kṛtimāgatāḥ .. 48 ..
1.187.d:
नंदा सुभद्रा सुरभी सुमना शोभनावती ॥
गावः सूर्यसमा भासा उत्पन्नाः कृतिमागताः ॥ 48 ॥
1.187.m: Nandā, Subhadrā, Surabhī, Sumanā, and Śobhanāvatī— / cows equal to the sun in brilliance, were born and came into being.

1.187.s:
sarvalokopakārārthaṃ devānāṃ tarpaṇāya ca ..
māmāśritya sthitā gāvaḥ snānārthaṃ bhāskarasya tu .. 49 ..
1.187.d:
सर्वलोकोपकारार्थं देवानां तर्पणाय च ॥
मामाश्रित्य स्थिता गावः स्नानार्थं भास्करस्य तु ॥ 49 ॥
1.187.m: For the benefit of all worlds and for the gratification of the gods, / and for the bath of Bhāskara, these cows dwell having taken refuge in me.

1.187.s:
tāsāmaṃgāni puṇyāni ṣaḍrasāḥ khagasattama ..
khagādiṣu ca sarveṣu sthirāṇītyupadhāraya .. 1.187.50 ..
1.187.d:
तासामंगानि पुण्यानि षड्रसाः खगसत्तम ॥
खगादिषु च सर्वेषु स्थिराणीत्युपधारय ॥ 1.187.50 ॥
1.187.m:
Know, O best of birds, that their limbs are holy,
and the six tastes are firmly established in all birds and other creatures.

1.187.s:
gomayaṃ rocanaṃ mūtraṃ kṣīraṃ dadhi ghṛtaṃ gavām ..
ṣaḍaṃgāni pavitrāṇi sarvasiddhikarāṇi ca .. 51 ..
1.187.d:
गोमयं रोचनं मूत्रं क्षीरं दधि घृतं गवाम् ॥
षडंगानि पवित्राणि सर्वसिद्धिकराणि च ॥ 51 ॥
1.187.m:
Cow dung, yellow orpiment, urine, milk, curd, and ghee:
these six limbs of cows are purifying and grant all perfections.

1.187.s:
gomayādutthitaḥ śrīmānbilvavṛkṣo'rkavallabhaḥ ..
tatrāste padmahastā śrīrvṛkṣastena ca sa smṛtaḥ .. 52 ..
1.187.d:
गोमयादुत्थितः श्रीमान्बिल्ववृक्षोऽर्कवल्लभः ॥
तत्रास्ते पद्महस्ता श्रीर्वृक्षस्तेन च स स्मृतः ॥ 52 ॥
1.187.m:
From cow dung arose the glorious bilva tree, beloved of the sun;
there sits Śrī with lotus in hand, and therefore it is remembered as that tree.

1.187.s:
paṃkānyutpalapadmāni punarjātāni gomayāt ..
gorocanaṃ ca maṃgalya pavitraṃ sarvakāmadam .. 53 ..
1.187.d:
पंकान्युत्पलपद्मानि पुनर्जातानि गोमयात् ॥
गोरोचनं च मंगल्य पवित्रं सर्वकामदम् ॥ 53 ॥
1.187.m:
From cow dung also arose lotuses and blue lotuses from the mud;
and cow-gall is auspicious, purifying, and grants all desires.

1.187.s:
gomūtrādguggulurjātaḥ sugaṃdhiḥ priyadarśanaḥ ..
āhāraḥ sarvadevānāṃ bhāskarasya viśeṣataḥ .. 54 ..
1.187.d:
गोमूत्राद्गुग्गुलुर्जातः सुगंधिः प्रियदर्शनः ॥
आहारः सर्वदेवानां भास्करस्य विशेषतः ॥ 54 ॥
1.187.m:
From cow urine arose bdellium, fragrant and pleasing to look upon;
it is food for all the gods, especially for the Sun.

1.187.s:
yadbījaṃ jagataḥ kiṃcittajjñeyaṃ kṣīrasaṃbhavam ..
dadhnaḥ sarvāṇi jātāni māṃgalyānyarthasiddhaye .. 55 ..
1.187.d:
यद्बीजं जगतः किंचित्तज्ज्ञेयं क्षीरसंभवम् ॥
दध्नः सर्वाणि जातानि मांगल्यान्यर्थसिद्धये ॥ 55 ॥
1.187.m:
Whatever seed there is of the world, know that to have arisen from milk;
from curd all auspicious things have arisen for the attainment of goals.

1.187.s:
ghṛtādamṛtamutpannamamarāṇāmatipriyam ..
tasmāddhṛtena payasā dadhnā yaḥ snāpayedravim .. 56 ..
1.187.d:
घृतादमृतमुत्पन्नममराणामतिप्रियम् ॥
तस्माद्धृतेन पयसा दध्ना यः स्नापयेद्रविम् ॥ 56 ॥
1.187.m:
From ghee arose the nectar most dear to the immortals;
therefore, whoever bathes the Sun with ghee, milk, and curd,

1.187.s:
tadaṃte coṣṇatoyena kaṣāyaiśca nirūpayet ..
snāpya śītāṃbunā paścādbhānuṃ rocanayālabhet .. 57 ..
1.187.d:
तदंते चोष्णतोयेन कषायैश्च निरूपयेत् ॥
स्नाप्य शीतांबुना पश्चाद्भानुं रोचनयालभेत् ॥ 57 ॥
1.187.m:
and then concludes it with warm water and examines him with decoctions,
having bathed [him] afterwards with cold water, should smear the Sun with yellow orpiment.

1.187.s:
pūjayedbilvapatraiśca padmairnīlotpalaistathā ..
arghyaṃ dadyāttataḥ paścātsavajraṃ guggulaṃ khaga .. 58 ..
1.187.d:
पूजयेद्बिल्वपत्रैश्च पद्मैर्नीलोत्पलैस्तथा ॥
अर्घ्यं दद्यात्ततः पश्चात्सवज्रं गुग्गुलं खग ॥ 58 ॥
1.187.m:
He should worship with bilva leaves, lotuses, and blue lotuses;
then afterwards, O bird, he should offer water of respect, and bdellium with diamonds.

1.187.s:
pāyasaṃ dadhibhaktaṃ ca vajraṃ ca madhunā saha ..
nivedayecca sadbhaktyā bhakṣyāṇi vividhāni ca .. 59 ..
1.187.d:
पायसं दधिभक्तं च वज्रं च मधुना सह ॥
निवेदयेच्च सद्भक्त्या भक्ष्याणि विविधानि च ॥ 59 ॥
1.187.m:
Milk-rice, curd-rice, and vajra along with honey,
he should present with true devotion, along with various foods.

1.187.s:
kṛtvā pradakṣiṇaṃ paścātpraṇipatya kṣamāpayet ..
anena vidhinā bhānuṃ ṣaḍaṃgena divaspatim .. 1.187.60 ..
1.187.d:
कृत्वा प्रदक्षिणं पश्चात्प्रणिपत्य क्षमापयेत् ॥
अनेन विधिना भानुं षडंगेन दिवस्पतिम् ॥ 1.187.60 ॥
1.187.m:
Having made circumambulation, bowed down, he should beg for forgiveness.
By this sixfold rite to the Sun, the lord of the day,

1.187.s:
iha loke pare caiva sarvānkāmānsa gacchati ..
ṣaḍaṃgavidhinā taṃ cāpūjyaivaṃ sumanā ravim .. 61 ..
1.187.d:
इह लोके परे चैव सर्वान्कामान्स गच्छति ॥
षडंगविधिना तं चापूज्यैवं सुमना रविम् ॥ 61 ॥
1.187.m:
he attains all desires in this world and in the next.
Having thus worshipped the Sun with cheerful mind by the sixfold rite,

1.187.s:
svargaṃ nayetsadhīmāṃstu kulānāmekaviṃśatim ..
svarge sthāpya svayaṃ gacchejjyautiṣaṃ nāma tatpadam .. 62 ..
1.187.d:
स्वर्गं नयेत्सधीमांस्तु कुलानामेकविंशतिम् ॥
स्वर्गे स्थाप्य स्वयं गच्छेज्ज्यौतिषं नाम तत्पदम् ॥ 62 ॥
1.187.m:
the wise man would lead twenty-one generations to heaven;
having established them in heaven, he himself would go to that abode called Jyotiṣa.

1.187.s:
aṃśena bhojakā vīra devakārye niyojitāḥ ..
prayāṃti svāminā sārdhaṃ śrīmadbhānuṃ paraṃ mahaḥ .. 63 ..
1.187.d:
अंशेन भोजका वीर देवकार्ये नियोजिताः ॥
प्रयांति स्वामिना सार्धं श्रीमद्भानुं परं महः ॥ 63 ॥
1.187.m:
O hero, the Bhojakas employed in the work of the god
go together with their master by a portion to the glorious Sun, the supreme radiance.

1.187.s:
bhuktvā bhogāṃstu vipulānbhojako bhogasaṃmitaḥ ..
kālātpunarihāyātaḥ pṛthivyāmekarāḍbhavet .. 64 ..
1.187.d:
भुक्त्वा भोगांस्तु विपुलान्भोजको भोगसंमितः ॥
कालात्पुनरिहायातः पृथिव्यामेकराड्भवेत् ॥ 64 ॥
1.187.m:
Having enjoyed extensive pleasures, the Bhojaka, filled with enjoyment,
having returned here in time, would become sole sovereign over the earth.

1.187.s:
puṣpaṃ patraṃ phalaṃ toyaṃ yadgataṃ bhāskarārcane ..
saurā gāvaśca gacchaṃti sūryalokaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 65 ..
1.187.d:
पुष्पं पत्रं फलं तोयं यद्गतं भास्करार्चने ॥
सौरा गावश्च गच्छंति सूर्यलोकं न संशयः ॥ 65 ॥
1.187.m:
Whatever flower, leaf, fruit, or water has gone into the worship of the Sun,
the Solar devotees and cows go to the world of the Sun without doubt.

1.187.s:
yaḥ pibedbhojane dhenoradattā bhānave payaḥ ..
sa gacchennarakaṃ ghoramakurvaṃstarpaṇaṃ raveḥ .. 66 ..
1.187.d:
यः पिबेद्भोजने धेनोरदत्ता भानवे पयः ॥
स गच्छेन्नरकं घोरमकुर्वंस्तर्पणं रवेः ॥ 66 ॥
1.187.m:
Whoever drinks the milk of a cow at a meal without offering it to the Sun,
he would go to a dreadful hell, not having made a libation to the Sun.

1.187.s:
ekakālaṃ pibetkṣīraṃ dhenūnāṃ bhāskarasya tu ..
anena snāpayeddevaṃ kṣīreṇa khagasattama .. 67 ..
1.187.d:
एककालं पिबेत्क्षीरं धेनूनां भास्करस्य तु ॥
अनेन स्नापयेद्देवं क्षीरेण खगसत्तम ॥ 67 ॥
1.187.m:
One should drink the milk of the Sun's cows at a single time;
with this milk, O best of birds, he should bathe the god.

1.187.s:
pratyūṣe yadbhavetkṣīraṃ dhenūnāṃ bhāskarasya tu ..
snāpayettena vai bhānuṃ kṛtsnena garuḍāgraja .. 68 ..
1.187.d:
प्रत्यूषे यद्भवेत्क्षीरं धेनूनां भास्करस्य तु ॥
स्नापयेत्तेन वै भानुं कृत्स्नेन गरुडाग्रज ॥ 68 ॥
1.187.m:
Whatever milk of the cows belongs to the Sun at dawn,
with all of it, O elder brother of Garuḍa, he should bathe the Sun.

1.187.s:
yastu loko bhajetsarva na devāya nivedayet ..
yāvanto romakūpāśca gavāṃ dehe khagādhipa ..
tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi narake pacyate khaga .. 69 ..
1.187.d:
यस्तु लोको भजेत्सर्व न देवाय निवेदयेत् ॥
यावन्तो रोमकूपाश्च गवां देहे खगाधिप ॥
तावद्वर्षसहस्राणि नरके पच्यते खग ॥ 69 ॥
1.187.m:
Whoever among people would enjoy everything and not offer it to the god,
as many pores of hair as there are in the body of cows, O lord of birds,
for so many thousands of years he is cooked in hell, O bird.

1.187.s:
pūjitaṃ pūjyamānaṃ vā yaḥ kaścicchṛṇuyādravim ..
śrutvānumodate yastu sa yajñaphalamaśnute .. 1.187.70 ..
1.187.d:
पूजितं पूज्यमानं वा यः कश्चिच्छृणुयाद्रविम् ॥
श्रुत्वानुमोदते यस्तु स यज्ञफलमश्नुते ॥ 1.187.70 ॥
1.187.m:
Whoever hears of the Sun worshipped or being worshipped,
and having heard rejoices, attains the fruit of sacrifice.

1.187.s:
bhāskaraṃ pṛjitaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate ..
harṣātpraṇamya vai bhānuṃ tasya loke mahīyate .. 71 ..
1.187.d:
भास्करं पृजितं दृष्ट्वा सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥
हर्षात्प्रणम्य वै भानुं तस्य लोके महीयते ॥ 71 ॥
1.187.m:
Having seen the Sun worshipped, he is freed from all sins;
having bowed down to the Sun in joy, he is magnified in his world.

1.187.s:
pūjyamānaṃ raviṃ bhaktyā yaḥ paśyenmānavaḥ khaga ..
so'pi yajñaphalaṃ kṛtsnaṃ prāpnuyānnātra saṃśayaḥ .. 72 ..
1.187.d:
पूज्यमानं रविं भक्त्या यः पश्येन्मानवः खग ॥
सोऽपि यज्ञफलं कृत्स्नं प्राप्नुयान्नात्र संशयः ॥ 72 ॥
1.187.m:
Whoever sees the Sun being worshipped with devotion, O bird,
he too would obtain the entire fruit of sacrifice; there is no doubt here.

1.187.s:
śrutvānumodate yastu pūjyamānaṃ divākaram ..
tatsarvaṃ phalamāpnoti prasādādbhāskarasya tu .. 73 ..
1.187.d:
श्रुत्वानुमोदते यस्तु पूज्यमानं दिवाकरम् ॥
तत्सर्वं फलमाप्नोति प्रसादाद्भास्करस्य तु ॥ 73 ॥
1.187.m:
And whoever, having heard of the Sun being worshipped, rejoices,
attains all that fruit through the grace of the Sun.

1.187.s:
ekajanmānugaṃ dānaṃ bhaktyā yacca niveditam ..
japayajñādviyuktebhyaḥ sahasrabhavikaṃ smṛtam ..
ābhūtasaṃplava sthāyi pradānaṃ japajīvinām .. 74 ..
1.187.d:
एकजन्मानुगं दानं भक्त्या यच्च निवेदितम् ॥
जपयज्ञाद्वियुक्तेभ्यः सहस्रभविकं स्मृतम् ॥
आभूतसंप्लव स्थायि प्रदानं जपजीविनाम् ॥ 74 ॥

1.187.s:
atyalpamapi yaddattaṃ vācakāya khagādhipa ..
tanmahāpralayaṃ yāvaddāturbhogāya kalpate .. 75 ..
1.187.d:
अत्यल्पमपि यद्दत्तं वाचकाय खगाधिप ॥
तन्महाप्रलयं यावद्दातुर्भोगाय कल्पते ॥ 75 ॥
1.187.m:
Even the tiniest bit that is given to a reciter, O lord of birds,
serves for the donor's enjoyment until the great dissolution.

1.187.s:
na dānamalpaṃ bahudhā kiṃcidasti vijānatām ..
deśakālavidhiśraddhāpātrayuktaṃ tadakṣayam .. 76 ..
1.187.d:
न दानमल्पं बहुधा किंचिदस्ति विजानताम् ॥
देशकालविधिश्रद्धापात्रयुक्तं तदक्षयम् ॥ 76 ॥
1.187.m:
For the wise, no gift is ever considered small;
endowed with place, time, rule, faith, and a worthy recipient, it is inexhaustible.

1.187.s:
pātre deśe ca kāle ca vidhinā śraddhayā ca yat ..
dattaṃ hutaṃ kṛtaṃ caiva tadanaṃtaphalaṃ bhavet .. 77 ..
1.187.d:
पात्रे देशे च काले च विधिना श्रद्धया च यत् ॥
दत्तं हुतं कृतं चैव तदनंतफलं भवेत् ॥ 77 ॥
1.187.m:
Whatever is given, offered in fire, and performed with a worthy recipient, in place and time,
according to rule and with faith, that becomes of endless fruit.

1.187.s:
tilārdhamapi yadvīra dīyate śraddhayā dvija ..
satpātre vidhivadbhaktyā tadbhavetsarvakāmikam .. 78 ..
1.187.d:
तिलार्धमपि यद्वीर दीयते श्रद्धया द्विज ॥
सत्पात्रे विधिवद्भक्त्या तद्भवेत्सर्वकामिकम् ॥ 78 ॥
1.187.m:
Even half a sesame seed, O hero, O twice-born, that is given with faith
to a worthy recipient according to rule and with devotion, becomes the granter of all desires.

1.187.s:
yatsnātaṃ jñānasalilaiḥ śīlabhasmapramārjitam .. snāna
tatpātraṃ sarvapātrebhya uttamaṃ parikīrtitam .. 79 ..
1.187.d:
यत्स्नातं ज्ञानसलिलैः शीलभस्मप्रमार्जितम् ॥ स्नान
तत्पात्रं सर्वपात्रेभ्य उत्तमं परिकीर्तितम् ॥ 79 ॥
1.187.m:
He who is bathed in the waters of knowledge, cleansed with the ashes of good conduct,
that recipient is proclaimed the highest of all recipients.

1.187.s:
japo damo yamaḥ puṃsāṃ trātā saṃsāgsāgarāt ..
ajñānāṃ pāpanetrāṇāṃ tatpātraṃ paramaṃ smṛtam .. 1.187.80 ..
1.187.d:
जपो दमो यमः पुंसां त्राता संसाग्सागरात् ॥
अज्ञानां पापनेत्राणां तत्पात्रं परमं स्मृतम् ॥ 1.187.80 ॥
1.187.m:
Muttering, self-restraint, and control are the saviour of men from the ocean of worldly existence;
for the ignorant whose eyes are sinful, that recipient is remembered as supreme.

1.187.s:
jñānaplavena copetaṃ śāstraṃ pāpamahārṇavāt ..
ajñānsaṃtārayennūnaṃ kiṃ śilā tārayecchilām .. 81 ..
1.187.d:
ज्ञानप्लवेन चोपेतं शास्त्रं पापमहार्णवात् ॥
अज्ञान्संतारयेन्नूनं किं शिला तारयेच्छिलाम् ॥ 81 ॥
1.187.m:
Endowed with the boat of knowledge, scripture can surely carry the ignorant across
from the great ocean of sin; can a stone cause a stone to cross?

1.187.s:
dvijānāṃ vedaviduṣāṃ kaṭisaṃbhogi yatphalam ..
haṃtakārapradānena tatphalaṃ japajīvine .. 82 ..
1.187.d:
द्विजानां वेदविदुषां कटिसंभोगि यत्फलम् ॥
हंतकारप्रदानेन तत्फलं जपजीविने ॥ 82 ॥
1.187.m:
Whatever fruit is attained by embracing the waists of twice-born scholars of the Veda,
that same fruit belongs to one who lives by muttering, through the giving of food.

1.187.s:
jīvo yasyaitya gṛhe ca bhuṅkte satkṛtisatkṛtaḥ ..
kulamuttārayettasya narakārṇavasaṃsthitam .. 83 ..
1.187.d:
जीवो यस्यैत्य गृहे च भुङ्क्ते सत्कृतिसत्कृतः ॥
कुलमुत्तारयेत्तस्य नरकार्णवसंस्थितम् ॥ 83 ॥
1.187.m:
He in whose house a living soul comes and eats, honoured with hospitality,
would deliver his family residing in the ocean of hell.

1.187.s:
yajñāgnihomatīrtheṣu yatphalaṃ parikīrtitam ..
japināmannadānena tatsamagraṃ phala labhet .. 84 ..
1.187.d:
यज्ञाग्निहोमतीर्थेषु यत्फलं परिकीर्तितम् ॥
जपिनामन्नदानेन तत्समग्रं फल लभेत् ॥ 84 ॥
1.187.m:
Whatever fruit is proclaimed in sacrifices, fire-oblations, and sacred bathing places,
he would obtain that entire fruit through the gift of food to those who mutter [prayers].

1.187.s:
bhojine śāṃtacittāya paridhyānaratāya ca ..
śraddhayānnaṃ sakṛddattvā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate .. 85 ..
1.187.d:
भोजिने शांतचित्ताय परिध्यानरताय च ॥
श्रद्धयान्नं सकृद्दत्त्वा सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥ 85 ॥
1.187.m:
Having once given food with faith to a diner whose mind is calm
and who is devoted to deep meditation, he is freed from all sins.

1.187.s:
japakāñchāṃtisaṃyuktānādityārpitacetasaḥ ..
bhojayitvā sakṛdbhaktyā sarvānkāmānavāpnuyāt .. 86 ..
1.187.d:
जपकाञ्छांतिसंयुक्तानादित्यार्पितचेतसः ॥
भोजयित्वा सकृद्भक्त्या सर्वान्कामानवाप्नुयात् ॥ 86 ॥
1.187.m:
Having once fed with devotion those who mutter [prayers], endowed with tranquility,
whose minds are offered to the Sun, one would obtain all desires.

1.187.s:
dhyāyamāno raveḥ sūktaṃ bhojayetsatataṃ ca yaḥ ..
tataḥ sākṣādanenaiva tadbhuktamaśana bhavet .. 87 ..
1.187.d:
ध्यायमानो रवेः सूक्तं भोजयेत्सततं च यः ॥
ततः साक्षादनेनैव तद्भुक्तमशन भवेत् ॥ 87 ॥
1.187.m:
And whoever continuously feeds [them] while meditating on the hymn to the Sun,
by that directly, that food becomes eaten by him.

1.187.s:
pitṝnudiśya yaḥ śrāddhe bhojayedbhojakaṃ naraḥ ..
sa sthānaṃ samavāpnoti bhānavīyamasaṃśayaḥ .. 88 ..
bhojakasatkāravarṇanam
1.187.d:
पितॄनुदिश्य यः श्राद्धे भोजयेद्भोजकं नरः ॥
स स्थानं समवाप्नोति भानवीयमसंशयः ॥ 88 ॥
भोजकसत्कारवर्णनम्
1.187.m:
The man who feeds a Bhojaka in an ancestral rite with reference to the ancestors,
he attains the abode belonging to the Sun without doubt.
Description of the Hospitality to a Bhojaka

1.188.s:
.. saptāśva uvāca .. ..
sūryāya sarvapākānnaṃ nivedyāgnau ca homayet ..
hutvāgnau prakṣipedvīra baliṃ dikṣu samaṃtataḥ .. 1 ..
1.188.d:
॥ सप्ताश्व उवाच ॥ ॥
सूर्याय सर्वपाकान्नं निवेद्याग्नौ च होमयेत् ॥
हुत्वाग्नौ प्रक्षिपेद्वीर बलिं दिक्षु समंततः ॥ 1 ॥

1.188.s:
sūryāgniguruviprāṇāṃ sarvapākānnamanvaham ..
yo'nivedyātmanā bhuṃkte sa bhuṃkte kilbiṣaṃ naraḥ .. 2 ..
1.188.d:
सूर्याग्निगुरुविप्राणां सर्वपाकान्नमन्वहम् ॥
योऽनिवेद्यात्मना भुंक्ते स भुंक्ते किल्बिषं नरः ॥ 2 ॥
1.188.m:
The man who himself eats every day all cooked food without offering it
to the Sun, fire, the guru, and the brāhmaṇas, eats sin.

1.188.s:
kṛṣipālye ca vāṇijye krodhasatyakṣayādibhiḥ ..
puṃsāṃ pāpāni vardhaṃte sūnādoṣaiśca paṃcabhiḥ .. 3 ..
1.188.d:
कृषिपाल्ये च वाणिज्ये क्रोधसत्यक्षयादिभिः ॥
पुंसां पापानि वर्धंते सूनादोषैश्च पंचभिः ॥ 3 ॥
1.188.m: In agriculture, animal husbandry, and trade, through anger, loss of truthfulness, and the like, / and through the five domestic slaughtering-faults, men's sins increase.

1.188.s:
kaṃḍanī peṣaṇī cullī udakuṃbhaḥ pramārjanī ..
paṃca sūnā gṛhasthasya tena svargaṃ na gacchati .. 4 ..
1.188.d:
कंडनी पेषणी चुल्ली उदकुंभः प्रमार्जनी ॥
पंच सूना गृहस्थस्य तेन स्वर्गं न गच्छति ॥ 4 ॥
1.188.m: The mortar, the grindstone, the hearth, the water jar, and the broom: / these are the five slaughterhouses of the householder; on account of them he does not go to heaven.

1.188.s:
sūryāgnigurupūjābhiḥ pāpairetairna lipyate ..
anyaiśca pātakaighoraistasmātsaṃpūjayetsadā .. 5 ..
1.188.d:
सूर्याग्निगुरुपूजाभिः पापैरेतैर्न लिप्यते ॥
अन्यैश्च पातकैघोरैस्तस्मात्संपूजयेत्सदा ॥ 5 ॥
1.188.m: By worshiping the sun, fire, and the guru, he is not stained by these sins / or by other terrible offenses; therefore, one should always worship them.

1.188.s:
sūryāgnigurunaivedyaṃ yāvatsyādannasaṃkhyayā ..
tāvadvarṣasahasrāṇi dātā sūryapure vaset .. 6 ..
1.188.d:
सूर्याग्निगुरुनैवेद्यं यावत्स्यादन्नसंख्यया ॥
तावद्वर्षसहस्राणि दाता सूर्यपुरे वसेत् ॥ 6 ॥
1.188.m: As many food-portions as there may be in the food offering to the sun, fire, and the guru, / for that many thousands of years the giver shall dwell in the city of the Sun.

1.188.s:
ghṛtapūpayutaiḥ siktaiḥ puṇyaṃ daśaguṇottaram ..
avadaṃśaguṇairyuktaṃ puṇyaṃ śataguṇaṃ khaga .. 7 ..
1.188.d:
घृतपूपयुतैः सिक्तैः पुण्यं दशगुणोत्तरम् ॥
अवदंशगुणैर्युक्तं पुण्यं शतगुणं खग ॥ 7 ॥
1.188.m: With [cakes] accompanied by and steeped in clarified butter, the merit is tenfold greater; / endowed with condiments, O bird, the merit is a hundredfold.

1.188.s:
ṣaṣṭikaudananaivedyaṃ sahasraguṇitaṃ phalam ..
sugaṃdhaśālinaivedyaṃ vijñeyamayutottaram.. 8 ..
1.188.d:
षष्टिकौदननैवेद्यं सहस्रगुणितं फलम् ॥
सुगंधशालिनैवेद्यं विज्ञेयमयुतोत्तरम्॥ 8 ॥
1.188.m: An offering of boiled ṣaṣṭika rice has a thousandfold fruit; / an offering of fragrant winter rice should be known to be ten thousandfold greater.

1.188.s:
bhakṣyānnapānadānāni tatphalāni tathātathā ..
yadvā tadvā sadā deyaṃ sūryāgnigurusādhuṣu ..
bhakṣyaṃ nivedya pūrvoktamakṣayaṃ labhate phalam .. 9 ..
1.188.d:
भक्ष्यान्नपानदानानि तत्फलानि तथातथा ॥
यद्वा तद्वा सदा देयं सूर्याग्निगुरुसाधुषु ॥
भक्ष्यं निवेद्य पूर्वोक्तमक्षयं लभते फलम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.188.m: Gifts of solid food, boiled food, and drinks bring corresponding fruits. / Whatever it may be, it should always be given to the sun, fire, the guru, and the virtuous; / having offered the previously mentioned food, one obtains imperishable fruit.

1.188.s:
evaṃ yaḥ kurute bhaktiṃ deva deve divākare ..
sa pitṝnsarvapāpebhyaḥ samuddhṛtya divaṃ nayet .. 1.188.10 ..
1.188.d:
एवं यः कुरुते भक्तिं देव देवे दिवाकरे ॥
स पितॄन्सर्वपापेभ्यः समुद्धृत्य दिवं नयेत् ॥ 1.188.10 ॥
1.188.m: He who thus renders devotion to the sun, god of gods, / having rescued his ancestors from all sins, leads them to heaven.

1.188.s:
gaṃgāsnānamidaṃ puṇyaṃ darśanātprāpnuyādraveḥ ..
sarvatīrthābhiṣekaṃ ca praṇāmādviṃdate khaga .. 11 ..
1.188.d:
गंगास्नानमिदं पुण्यं दर्शनात्प्राप्नुयाद्रवेः ॥
सर्वतीर्थाभिषेकं च प्रणामाद्विंदते खग ॥ 11 ॥
1.188.m: This merit of bathing in the Gaṅgā one obtains from the sight of the sun; / and one attains the ablution of all sacred fords from a reverent bow, O bird.

1.188.s:
mucyate sarvapāpebhyaḥ praṇamya śirasā ravim ..
śuśrūṣeta ca saṃdhyāyāṃ sūryaloke mahīyate .. 12..
1.188.d:
मुच्यते सर्वपापेभ्यः प्रणम्य शिरसा रविम् ॥
शुश्रूषेत च संध्यायां सूर्यलोके महीयते ॥ 12॥
1.188.m: Having bowed to the sun with his head, he is freed from all sins; / and if he attends upon [the sun] at twilight, he is exalted in the realm of the Sun.

1.188.s:
yugapatpūjitāstena brahmaviṣṇu maheśvarāḥ ..
pitaraḥ sarvadevāśca bhaveyuḥ pūjitā ravau .. 13 ..
1.188.d:
युगपत्पूजितास्तेन ब्रह्मविष्णु महेश्वराः ॥
पितरः सर्वदेवाश्च भवेयुः पूजिता रवौ ॥ 13 ॥
1.188.m: By him Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara are worshiped simultaneously; / the ancestors and all the gods become worshiped when the sun is worshiped.

1.188.s:
tuṣyaṃti pitarastasya sukṛṣṭeneva karṣukāḥ ..
yaḥ śrāddhe bhojayedbhaktyā brāhmaṇaṃ japajīvinam .. 14 ..
1.188.d:
तुष्यंति पितरस्तस्य सुकृष्टेनेव कर्षुकाः ॥
यः श्राद्धे भोजयेद्भक्त्या ब्राह्मणं जपजीविनम् ॥ 14 ॥
1.188.m: His ancestors rejoice just as farmers do over well-plowed land, / if in a śrāddha he devotedly feeds a brāhmaṇa who subsists on mantra-recitation.

1.188.s:
api naḥ sa kule kaṃciduddharetkiṃ khageśvara ..
yaḥ saṃpūjya raviṃ śrāddhe bhojayejjapajīvinam .. 15 ..
1.188.d:
अपि नः स कुले कंचिदुद्धरेत्किं खगेश्वर ॥
यः संपूज्य रविं श्राद्धे भोजयेज्जपजीविनम् ॥ 15 ॥
1.188.m: [The ancestors say:] “Could anyone in our family deliver us, O king of birds, / who, having worshiped the sun, feeds in the śrāddha one who subsists on mantra-recitation?”

1.188.s:
tṛpyaṃti pitarastasya gāyaṃti ca pitāmahāḥ ..
adya naḥ sa kule prājño vācakaṃ bhojayiṣyati .. 16 ..
1.188.d:
तृप्यंति पितरस्तस्य गायंति च पितामहाः ॥
अद्य नः स कुले प्राज्ञो वाचकं भोजयिष्यति ॥ 16 ॥
1.188.m: His fathers are satisfied and his grandfathers sing: / “Today in our family a wise man will feed the reader [of scriptures]!”

1.188.s:
purāṇavidamāyāṃtaṃ dṛṣṭvaiva saha saṃsthitāḥ ..
krīḍaṃtyoṣadhayaḥ sarvā yāsyāmaḥ svargamakṣayam .. 17 ..
1.188.d:
पुराणविदमायांतं दृष्ट्वैव सह संस्थिताः ॥
क्रीडंत्योषधयः सर्वा यास्यामः स्वर्गमक्षयम् ॥ 17 ॥
1.188.m: Upon seeing one versed in the Purāṇas arrive, all the medicinal plants, / standing together, rejoice: “We shall go to imperishable heaven!”

1.188.s:
anugrahāya lokānāṃ śraddhāyāśca parīkṣaṇe ..
caraṃtyatithirūpeṇa pitaro devatāstathā .. .. 18 ..
1.188.d:
अनुग्रहाय लोकानां श्रद्धायाश्च परीक्षणे ॥
चरंत्यतिथिरूपेण पितरो देवतास्तथा ॥ ॥ 18 ॥
1.188.m: To bestow grace upon people and to test their faith, / the ancestors and likewise the deities wander about in the form of guests.

1.188.s:
tasmādatithimāyāṃtamagre gacchetkṛtāṃjaliḥ ..
svāgatāsanapādyārghyasnānānnaśayanādibhiḥ .. 19 ..
1.188.d:
तस्मादतिथिमायांतमग्रे गच्छेत्कृतांजलिः ॥
स्वागतासनपाद्यार्घ्यस्नानान्नशयनादिभिः ॥ 19 ॥
1.188.m: Therefore, one should go out to meet an arriving guest with folded hands, / with welcome, a seat, water for the feet, guest-water, a bath, food, a bed, and the like.

1.188.s:
rūpānvitaṃ virūpaṃ vā malinaṃ malināṃbaram ..
velāyāmatithiṃ prāptaṃ paṃḍito na vicārayet .. 1.188.20 ..
1.188.d:
रूपान्वितं विरूपं वा मलिनं मलिनांबरम् ॥
वेलायामतिथिं प्राप्तं पंडितो न विचारयेत् ॥ 1.188.20 ॥
1.188.m: Whether handsome or deformed, dirty or dressed in soiled clothes, / when a guest arrives at mealtime, a wise person should not evaluate [him].

1.188.s:
bhojakānāṃ śarīreṣu nityaṃ sannihito raviḥ ..
ye bhojakāstyajaṃtyanye sarvapāpeṣvavasthitāḥ ..
adhomukhorddhvapādāste pataṃti narakāgniṣu .. 21 ..
1.188.d:
भोजकानां शरीरेषु नित्यं सन्निहितो रविः ॥
ये भोजकास्त्यजंत्यन्ये सर्वपापेष्ववस्थिताः ॥
अधोमुखोर्द्ध्वपादास्ते पतंति नरकाग्निषु ॥ 21 ॥
1.188.m: The sun is always present in the bodies of the Bhojakas. / Those others who abandon the Bhojakas, abiding in all sins, / fall head down and feet up into the fires of hell.

1.188.s:
kṛmibhirbhinnavadanāstapyamānāśca vahninā ..
pīḍyaṃte cāyudhai rghoṃrairyāvadiṃdrāścaturdaśa .. 22 ..
1.188.d:
कृमिभिर्भिन्नवदनास्तप्यमानाश्च वह्निना ॥
पीड्यंते चायुधै र्घोंरैर्यावदिंद्राश्चतुर्दश ॥ 22 ॥
1.188.m: Their faces torn open by worms and burning with fire, / they are tormented with terrible weapons as long as the fourteen Indras endure.

1.188.s:
ye cāpavādaṃ śṛṇvaṃti vimūḍhā brāhmaṇeṣu vai ..
te viśeṣeṇa pacyaṃte narakeṣu madicchayā .. 23 ..
1.188.d:
ये चापवादं शृण्वंति विमूढा ब्राह्मणेषु वै ॥
ते विशेषेण पच्यंते नरकेषु मदिच्छया ॥ 23 ॥
1.188.m: And those foolish people who listen to slander against brāhmaṇas / are especially cooked in the hells by my will.

1.188.s:
sarveṣāmeva pātrāṇāṃ satpātraṃ jāpakaḥ paraḥ ..
tasmātsarvaprayatnena pūjayetsusamāhitaḥ .. 24 .. ..
sauradharmeṣu saptāśvasaṃvādaḥ
1.188.d:
सर्वेषामेव पात्राणां सत्पात्रं जापकः परः ॥
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन पूजयेत्सुसमाहितः ॥ 24 ॥ ॥
सौरधर्मेषु सप्ताश्वसंवादः
1.188.m:
Among all recipients, the reciter [of mantras] is the supreme worthy recipient; / therefore, with all effort, well-concentrated, one should worship him.
Dialogue of Saptāśva on the Solar Ordinances.

1.189.s:
.. saptāśvatilaka uvāca .. ..
āmapātrarasā yadvannaśyaṃte naśyabhājane ..
japopekṣe tathā dānaṃ saha pātreṇa naśyati ..
sadbījamūṣare yadvatsamuptaṃ niṣphalaṃ bhavet ..1..
1.189.d:
॥ सप्ताश्वतिलक उवाच ॥ ॥
आमपात्ररसा यद्वन्नश्यंते नश्यभाजने ॥
जपोपेक्षे तथा दानं सह पात्रेण नश्यति ॥
सद्बीजमूषरे यद्वत्समुप्तं निष्फलं भवेत् ॥1॥
1.189.m: The ornament of Saptāśva said: / Just as the liquids in an unbaked vessel are ruined in a perishable container, / so a gift given to one who neglects mantra-recitation perishes along with the recipient; / just as good seed sown in barren soil becomes fruitless,

1.189.s:
bhasmanīva hutaṃ havyaṃ yathā hotuśca niṣphalam ..
japena rahite vipre tathā dānaṃ nirarthakam ..2..
1.189.d:
भस्मनीव हुतं हव्यं यथा होतुश्च निष्फलम् ॥
जपेन रहिते विप्रे तथा दानं निरर्थकम् ॥2॥
1.189.m: and just as an oblation poured into ashes is fruitless for the sacrificer, / so a gift to a vipra who is devoid of mantra-recitation is useless.

1.189.s:
yathā ṣaṇḍho'phalaḥ strīṣu yathā gaurgavi cāphalā ..
brāhmaṇasya tathā janma japahīnasya niṣphalam ..3..
1.189.d:
यथा षण्ढोऽफलः स्त्रीषु यथा गौर्गवि चाफला ॥
ब्राह्मणस्य तथा जन्म जपहीनस्य निष्फलम् ॥3॥
1.189.m: Just as a eunuch is fruitless with women, and just as a cow is fruitless with a cow, / so the birth of a brāhmaṇa devoid of mantra-recitation is fruitless.

1.189.s:
lohoḍupena pratarannimajjatyudake yathā ..
dātā dātā grahītā ca patatyaṃdhe tamasyatha..4..
1.189.d:
लोहोडुपेन प्रतरन्निमज्जत्युदके यथा ॥
दाता दाता ग्रहीता च पतत्यंधे तमस्यथ॥4॥
1.189.m: Just as one crossing over in an iron boat sinks into the water, / so the giver and the receiver fall into blind darkness.

1.189.s:
kāruṇyātsarvabhūteṣu śraddhayā yatpradīyate ..
dānaṃ tadvai khaga jñeyaṃ sārvakāmikamuttamam .. 5 ..
1.189.d:
कारुण्यात्सर्वभूतेषु श्रद्धया यत्प्रदीयते ॥
दानं तद्वै खग ज्ञेयं सार्वकामिकमुत्तमम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.189.m: Whatever is given with faith out of compassion for all beings, / that gift, O bird, should be known as fulfilling all desires and supreme.

1.189.s:
dīnāṃdhakṛpaṇānāṃ ca bālavṛddhātureṣu ca ..
yaddīyate khagaśreṣṭha tasyānantaphalaṃ bhavet .. 6 ..
1.189.d:
दीनांधकृपणानां च बालवृद्धातुरेषु च ॥
यद्दीयते खगश्रेष्ठ तस्यानन्तफलं भवेत् ॥ 6 ॥
1.189.m: Whatever is given to the poor, the blind, and the miserable, and among children, the aged, and the afflicted, / O best of birds, bears infinite fruit.

1.189.s:
na hi svārthaṃ samuddiśya pratigṛhṇaṃti sādhavaḥ ..
dāturevopakārāya jagṛhuḥ śravaṇādayaḥ .. 7 ..
1.189.d:
न हि स्वार्थं समुद्दिश्य प्रतिगृह्णंति साधवः ॥
दातुरेवोपकाराय जगृहुः श्रवणादयः ॥ 7 ॥
1.189.m: Virtuous men do not accept gifts for their own sake; / Śravaṇa and others accepted [them] solely for the benefit of the giver.

1.189.s:
dāturevopakārāya vadatyarthī dadasva me ..
yasmāddātā prayātyūrdhvamadhastiṣṭhetpratigrahī .. 8 ..
1.189.d:
दातुरेवोपकाराय वदत्यर्थी ददस्व मे ॥
यस्माद्दाता प्रयात्यूर्ध्वमधस्तिष्ठेत्प्रतिग्रही ॥ 8 ॥
1.189.m: It is solely for the benefit of the giver that the petitioner says: “Give to me!” / For the giver goes upward, while the recipient stays below.

1.189.s:
dehīti suvadannarthī dhanaṃ bodhayatīva saḥ ..
yanmayā kṛtamarthitvaṃ prage'dānaphalaṃ hi tat .. 9 ..
1.189.d:
देहीति सुवदन्नर्थी धनं बोधयतीव सः ॥
यन्मया कृतमर्थित्वं प्रगेऽदानफलं हि तत् ॥ 9 ॥
1.189.m: Saying politely, “Give!” the petitioner, as it were, instructs [the giver about] wealth: / “The fact that I have become a beggar is indeed the fruit of not giving in a past life.”

1.189.s:
bodhayaṃti na yācante dehīti kṛpaṇā janāḥ ..
avastheyamadānasya yadyācāmo gṛhegṛhe .. 1.189.10 ..
1.189.d:
बोधयंति न याचन्ते देहीति कृपणा जनाः ॥
अवस्थेयमदानस्य यद्याचामो गृहेगृहे ॥ 1.189.10 ॥
1.189.m: Wretched people teach, they do not beg, [when saying,] “Give!”: / “This is the state caused by nongiving, that we beg from house to house.”

1.189.s:
āyātyarthī gṛhaṃ yastu kastaṃ na pratipūjayet ..
koyamarthī na pūjyaḥ syādyācamāno dinedine .. 11 ..
1.189.d:
आयात्यर्थी गृहं यस्तु कस्तं न प्रतिपूजयेत् ॥
कोयमर्थी न पूज्यः स्याद्याचमानो दिनेदिने ॥ 11 ॥
1.189.m: When a petitioner comes to one's house, who would not honor him? / Who is this petitioner who should not be worshiped, begging day after day?

1.189.s:
yadbalādapyanicchaṃtaṃ yojayaṃti narāśrayān ..
ahanyahani yācaṃte dātuste darśayaṃti hi .. .. 12 ..
1.189.d:
यद्बलादप्यनिच्छंतं योजयंति नराश्रयान् ॥
अहन्यहनि याचंते दातुस्ते दर्शयंति हि ॥ ॥ 12 ॥
1.189.m: Because they forcibly attach human beings [to merit], even when unwilling, / and beg day after day, they are indeed showing [the path] to the giver.

1.189.s:
ekastiṣṭhati cādhastādanyaścopari tiṣṭhati ..
dātṛyācakayorbhedaḥ karābhyāmeva sūcitaḥ .. 13 ..
1.189.d:
एकस्तिष्ठति चाधस्तादन्यश्चोपरि तिष्ठति ॥
दातृयाचकयोर्भेदः कराभ्यामेव सूचितः ॥ 13 ॥
1.189.m: One hand stays below, and the other stays above; / the distinction between the giver and the beggar is indicated by the hands alone.

1.189.s:
yaḥ prāptāyārthine dānaṃ tyaktvā pātra mudīkṣate ..
sarvakarmasu yuktatvānna dātā pāramārthikaḥ ..14..
1.189.d:
यः प्राप्तायार्थिने दानं त्यक्त्वा पात्र मुदीक्षते ॥
सर्वकर्मसु युक्तत्वान्न दाता पारमार्थिकः ॥14॥
1.189.m: He who withholds a gift from an arrived petitioner and looks for a [more worthy] recipient, / because he is engaged in all [kinds of calculated] deeds, is not a true giver.

1.189.s:
yadyarthino narā na syurdānadharmaḥ kathaṃ bhavet..
tadarthiṣu bhaveddānaṃ svāgataṃ svāgataṃ priyam.. .. 15 ..
1.189.d:
यद्यर्थिनो नरा न स्युर्दानधर्मः कथं भवेत्॥
तदर्थिषु भवेद्दानं स्वागतं स्वागतं प्रियम्॥ ॥ 15 ॥
1.189.m: If there were no human beggars, how could the virtue of generosity exist? / Therefore, a gift to petitioners should be accompanied by a warm welcome and dear words.

1.189.s:
pādodakamanuvrajyātsvargasopānasaptakam ..
ciṃtāciṃtānurūpeṇa kadā kasya vinaṣyati .. 16 ..
1.189.d:
पादोदकमनुव्रज्यात्स्वर्गसोपानसप्तकम् ॥
चिंताचिंतानुरूपेण कदा कस्य विनष्यति ॥ 16 ॥
1.189.m: Water for the feet and accompanying [the guest] are a seven-rung ladder to heaven. / According to one's anxious or careless thought, when does [merit] perish for anyone?

1.189.s:
grāsādardhamapi grāsaṃ yuktaṃ dātuṃ sadārthinām ..
dānaṃ priyavinirmuktaṃ naṣṭamāhurmanīṣiṇaḥ .. 17 ..
1.189.d:
ग्रासादर्धमपि ग्रासं युक्तं दातुं सदार्थिनाम् ॥
दानं प्रियविनिर्मुक्तं नष्टमाहुर्मनीषिणः ॥ 17 ॥
1.189.m: Even half a mouthful from one's food is fit to be given always to petitioners; / wise men say that a gift devoid of affection is lost.

1.189.s:
tasmātsatkṛtya dātavyamanaṃtaphalamicchatā ..
pretyākhyānamapi śreyaḥ priyānunayapeśa lam ..18..
1.189.d:
तस्मात्सत्कृत्य दातव्यमनंतफलमिच्छता ॥
प्रेत्याख्यानमपि श्रेयः प्रियानुनयपेश लम् ॥18॥
1.189.m: Therefore, one desiring infinite fruit should give with hospitality; / even a refusal that is pleasing with kind persuasion is better [than a harsh gift].

1.189.s:
na taddānamasatkārapāruṣyamalinīkṛtam ..
varaṃ na dattamarthibhyaḥ saṃkruddhenāṃtarātmanā..19..
1.189.d:
न तद्दानमसत्कारपारुष्यमलिनीकृतम् ॥
वरं न दत्तमर्थिभ्यः संक्रुद्धेनांतरात्मना॥19॥
1.189.m: That which is soiled by disrespect and harshness is not a gift; / it is better that nothing be given to petitioners by an inwardly enraged mind.

1.189.s:
na taddhanaṃ na ca prītirna dharmaḥ priyavarjitaḥ ..
dānapradānaniyamayajñadhyānaṃ hutaṃ tapaḥ ..
yatnenāpi kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ krodho'sya niṣphalaṃ khaga .. 1.189.20 ..
1.189.d:
न तद्धनं न च प्रीतिर्न धर्मः प्रियवर्जितः ॥
दानप्रदाननियमयज्ञध्यानं हुतं तपः ॥
यत्नेनापि कृतं सर्वं क्रोधोऽस्य निष्फलं खग ॥ 1.189.20 ॥
1.189.m: That is not wealth, nor is there love, nor dharma when bereft of kindness. / Gift-giving, vows, sacrifices, meditation, offerings into the fire, and asceticism— / all of it, even if performed with effort, O bird, anger renders fruitless.

1.189.s:
yaḥ śraddhayārcitaṃ dadyātprati gṛhṇāti cārcitam ..
tāvubhau gacchataḥ svargaṃ naraka tadviparyayāt .. 21 ..
1.189.d:
यः श्रद्धयार्चितं दद्यात्प्रति गृह्णाति चार्चितम् ॥
तावुभौ गच्छतः स्वर्गं नरक तद्विपर्ययात् ॥ 21 ॥
1.189.m: Whoever gives what is offered with faith, and whoever receives what is offered, / both of them go to heaven; from the opposite, to hell.

1.189.s:
audāryaṃ svāgataṃ maitrī hyanukaṃpā ca matsaraḥ ..
paṃcabhistu gurau dānaṃ dāturdāne mahāphalam..22..
1.189.d:
औदार्यं स्वागतं मैत्री ह्यनुकंपा च मत्सरः ॥
पंचभिस्तु गुरौ दानं दातुर्दाने महाफलम्॥22॥
1.189.m: Generosity, welcoming words, friendliness, compassion, and absence of malice— / through these five, a gift given to an elder brings great fruit to the giver.

1.189.s:
vārāṇasī kurukṣetraṃ prayāgaṃ puṣkarāṇi ca ..
gātaṭaṃ samudraśca naimiṣāraṇyameva ca .. 23 ..
1.189.d:
वाराणसी कुरुक्षेत्रं प्रयागं पुष्कराणि च ॥
गातटं समुद्रश्च नैमिषारण्यमेव च ॥ 23 ॥
1.189.m: Vārāṇasī, Kurukṣetra, Prayāga, and the Puṣkaras, / the bank of the Gaṅgā, the ocean, and the Naimiṣa forest,

1.189.s:
mūlasthānaṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ puṃḍīrasvāmikaṃ tathā ..
kālapriyaṃ khagaśreṣṭha kṣīrikāvāsa eva ca .. 24 ..
1.189.d:
मूलस्थानं महापुण्यं पुंडीरस्वामिकं तथा ॥
कालप्रियं खगश्रेष्ठ क्षीरिकावास एव च ॥ 24 ॥
1.189.m: the exceedingly sacred Mūlasthāna, likewise Puṇḍīrasvāmin, / Kālapriya, O best of birds, and Kṣīrikāvāsa:

1.189.s:
ityete kīrtitā deśāḥ surasiddhaniṣevitāḥ ..
sarve sūryāśramāḥ puṇyāḥ sarvā nadyaḥ saparvatāḥ ..
gosiddhamuni vāsāśca deśāḥ puṇyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ .. 25 ..
1.189.d:
इत्येते कीर्तिता देशाः सुरसिद्धनिषेविताः ॥
सर्वे सूर्याश्रमाः पुण्याः सर्वा नद्यः सपर्वताः ॥
गोसिद्धमुनि वासाश्च देशाः पुण्याः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ 25 ॥
1.189.m: These regions are proclaimed as frequented by gods and siddhas. / All hermitage-abodes of the Sun are holy; all rivers along with mountains, / and regions that are the dwellings of cows, siddhas, and sages, are proclaimed holy.

1.189.s:
sūryāyatanasaṃsthānāṃ yadyadalpaṃ tu dīyate ..
tadanaṃtaphalaṃ jñeyaṃ vacaḥ kṣetrānubhāvataḥ.. 36 ..
1.189.d:
सूर्यायतनसंस्थानां यद्यदल्पं तु दीयते ॥
तदनंतफलं ज्ञेयं वचः क्षेत्रानुभावतः॥ 36 ॥
1.189.m: Whatever little is given to those residing at an abode of the Sun, / that should be known to bear endless fruit by virtue of the sacred site.

1.189.s:
grahaṇaṃ caṃdrasūryābhyāmuttarāyaṇamuttamam ..
viṣuvaṃ savyatīpātaṃ ṣaḍaśītimukhaṃ tathā .. 27 ..
1.189.d:
ग्रहणं चंद्रसूर्याभ्यामुत्तरायणमुत्तमम् ॥
विषुवं सव्यतीपातं षडशीतिमुखं तथा ॥ 27 ॥
1.189.m: An eclipse of the moon or the sun, the excellent northern course of the sun, / the equinox, along with a vyatīpāta, and the ṣaḍaśītimukha,

1.189.s:
dinacchidrāṇi saṃkrāṃtiḥ puṇyaṃ viṣupadaṃ khaga ..
iti kālaḥ samā khyātaḥ puṃsāṃ puṇyavivardhanaḥ .. 28 ..
1.189.d:
दिनच्छिद्राणि संक्रांतिः पुण्यं विषुपदं खग ॥
इति कालः समा ख्यातः पुंसां पुण्यविवर्धनः ॥ 28 ॥
1.189.m: the dinacchidras, the solar transit, and the holy viṣupada, O bird— / thus is time declared, increasing the merit of men.

1.189.s:
bhaktibhāvaḥ parā prītirdharmo dharmaikabhāvanaḥ ..
pratipattiriti jñeyaṃ śraddhāparyāyapaṃcakam ..29..
1.189.d:
भक्तिभावः परा प्रीतिर्धर्मो धर्मैकभावनः ॥
प्रतिपत्तिरिति ज्ञेयं श्रद्धापर्यायपंचकम् ॥29॥
1.189.m: Devotional disposition, supreme affection, dharma, reflection on dharma alone, / [and] reverent reception—these are to be known as the five synonyms of faith.

1.189.s:
śraddhayā vidhivatpātre pratipāditamuttamam ..
tasmācchraddhāṃ samāsthāya deyamakṣayamicchatā .. 1.189.30 ..
1.189.d:
श्रद्धया विधिवत्पात्रे प्रतिपादितमुत्तमम् ॥
तस्माच्छ्रद्धां समास्थाय देयमक्षयमिच्छता ॥ 1.189.30 ॥
1.189.m: Given with faith according to rule to a worthy recipient, [a gift] is supreme. / Therefore, relying upon faith, one who desires what is imperishable should give.

1.189.s:
yaddānaṃ śraddhayā pātre vidhivatpratipāditam ..
tadanaṃtaphalaṃ jñeya mapi vā bhāramātrakam .. 31 ..
1.189.d:
यद्दानं श्रद्धया पात्रे विधिवत्प्रतिपादितम् ॥
तदनंतफलं ज्ञेय मपि वा भारमात्रकम् ॥ 31 ॥
1.189.m: Whatever gift is bestowed with faith upon a worthy recipient according to rule, / that should be known to yield endless fruit, even if it is only a weight of a bhāra.

1.189.s:
ārteṣu dīneṣu guṇānviteṣu yaḥ śraddhayā svalpamapi pradadyāt ..
sa sarvakāmānsamupaiti lokāñcchraddhaiva dānaṃ pravadaṃti tajjñāḥ .. 32 ..
1.189.d:
आर्तेषु दीनेषु गुणान्वितेषु यः श्रद्धया स्वल्पमपि प्रदद्यात् ॥
स सर्वकामान्समुपैति लोकाञ्च्छ्रद्धैव दानं प्रवदंति तज्ज्ञाः ॥ 32 ॥
1.189.m: Whoever with faith gives even a very little to the afflicted, the wretched, and the virtuous, / he attains worlds where all desires are fulfilled; those who know the truth declare that faith itself is the gift.

1.189.s:
śraddhā dānaṃ paraṃ jñeyaṃ śraddhā eva tapaḥ param ..
śraddhāṃ yajñamuśantīha śraddhā paramupoṣitam .. 33 ..
1.189.d:
श्रद्धा दानं परं ज्ञेयं श्रद्धा एव तपः परम् ॥
श्रद्धां यज्ञमुशन्तीह श्रद्धा परमुपोषितम् ॥ 33 ॥
1.189.m: Faith is to be known as the supreme gift; faith alone is supreme asceticism; / here they declare faith to be sacrifice; faith is the supreme fast.

1.189.s:
athāhiṃsā kṣamā satyaṃ hrīḥ śraddheṃdriyasaṃyamaḥ ..
dānamiṣṭaṃ tapo dhyānaṃ daśakaṃ dharmasādhanam .. 34 ..
1.189.d:
अथाहिंसा क्षमा सत्यं ह्रीः श्रद्धेंद्रियसंयमः ॥
दानमिष्टं तपो ध्यानं दशकं धर्मसाधनम् ॥ 34 ॥
1.189.m: Now, non-violence, patience, truth, modesty, faith, restraint of the senses, / gift-giving, worship, asceticism, and meditation: this is the tenfold means of dharma.

1.189.s:
haṃtavyastaiḥ samastairvā sūryadharmairanuṣṭhitaiḥ ..
sūryaukasāṃ ca saṃprāptergatirekā prakīrtitā .. 35 ..
1.189.d:
हंतव्यस्तैः समस्तैर्वा सूर्यधर्मैरनुष्ठितैः ॥
सूर्यौकसां च संप्राप्तेर्गतिरेका प्रकीर्तिता ॥ 35 ॥
1.189.m: By all these practices of the dharma of the Sun when performed, [evil] is destroyed; / and for attaining the abode of the Sun, one single path is proclaimed.

1.189.s:
yathā bhūḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ śāṃtiratiśayaḥ smṛtaḥ ..
kuryātpuṇyaṃ mahattasmānmama lokepsayā sudhī .. 36 ..
1.189.d:
यथा भूः सर्वभूतानां शांतिरतिशयः स्मृतः ॥
कुर्यात्पुण्यं महत्तस्मान्मम लोकेप्सया सुधी ॥ 36 ॥
1.189.m: Just as the earth is recalled as the utmost resting place of all beings, / so should the wise man perform great merit out of a desire for my world.

1.189.s:
parastrīdravyasaṃkalpaṃ yaḥ sāpekṣaṃ karoti ca ..
gurumārtamaśaktaṃ vā videśe prasthitaṃ tathā ..
aribhiḥ paribhūtaṃ ca saṃtyajeccaiva pāpakṛt .. 37 ..
1.189.d:
परस्त्रीद्रव्यसंकल्पं यः सापेक्षं करोति च ॥
गुरुमार्तमशक्तं वा विदेशे प्रस्थितं तथा ॥
अरिभिः परिभूतं च संत्यजेच्चैव पापकृत् ॥ 37 ॥
1.189.m: He who looks covetously upon another’s wife and property, / or who, performing evil, abandons a guru who is afflicted or helpless, / or set out in a foreign land, or humiliated by enemies,

1.189.s:
tadbhāryāmitraputreṣu yaścāvajñāṃ karoti ca ..
ityetatpātakaṃ jñeyaṃ guruniṃdāsamaṃ bhavet .. 38 ..
1.189.d:
तद्भार्यामित्रपुत्रेषु यश्चावज्ञां करोति च ॥
इत्येतत्पातकं ज्ञेयं गुरुनिंदासमं भवेत् ॥ 38 ॥
1.189.m: and who shows disrespect toward his wife, friend, or sons— / this is to be known as a sin equal to reviling one’s guru.

1.189.s:
brahmaghnaśca surāpaśca steyī ca gurutalpagaḥ ..
mahāpātakinastvete tatsaṃyogī ca pañcamaḥ .. 39 ..
1.189.d:
ब्रह्मघ्नश्च सुरापश्च स्तेयी च गुरुतल्पगः ॥
महापातकिनस्त्वेते तत्संयोगी च पञ्चमः ॥ 39 ॥
1.189.m: The killer of a brāhmaṇa, the drinker of liquor, the thief, and he who violates the bed of his guru— / these are the perpetrators of great sins, and he who associates with them is the fifth.

1.189.s:
krodhāddveṣādbhayāllobhādbrāhmaṇasya vadeta yaḥ ..
prāṇāṃtikaṃ mahādoṣaṃ brahmahā sa udāhṛtaḥ .. 1.189.40 ..
1.189.d:
क्रोधाद्द्वेषाद्भयाल्लोभाद्ब्राह्मणस्य वदेत यः ॥
प्राणांतिकं महादोषं ब्रह्महा स उदाहृतः ॥ 1.189.40 ॥
1.189.m: He who out of anger, hatred, fear, or greed speaks against a brāhmaṇa / a grave accusation bringing death, he is declared a killer of a brāhmaṇa.

1.189.s:
brāhmaṇaṃ ca samāhūya yācamānamakiṃcanam ..
yannāstīti ca yo brūyātsa cāṇḍālaṃ udāhṛtaḥ .. 41 ..
1.189.d:
ब्राह्मणं च समाहूय याचमानमकिंचनम् ॥
यन्नास्तीति च यो ब्रूयात्स चाण्डालं उदाहृतः ॥ 41 ॥
1.189.m: And he who, having summoned a destitute brāhmaṇa who is begging, / says, 'There is nothing,' is declared an outcaste.

1.189.s:
devadvijagavāṃ bhūmiṃ pūrvadattāṃ hareta yaḥ ..
pranaṣṭāmapi kāle tu tamāhurbrahmaghātakam .. 42 ..
1.189.d:
देवद्विजगवां भूमिं पूर्वदत्तां हरेत यः ॥
प्रनष्टामपि काले तु तमाहुर्ब्रह्मघातकम् ॥ 42 ॥
1.189.m: He who takes away land previously given to gods, brāhmaṇas, or cows, / even if it has fallen into ruin over time, him they call a slayer of a brāhmaṇa.

1.189.s:
adhītya yo raverjñānaṃ parityajati maṃdadhīḥ ..
surāpena samaṃ jñeyaṃ tasya pāpaṃ ca suvrata .. 43 ..
1.189.d:
अधीत्य यो रवेर्ज्ञानं परित्यजति मंदधीः ॥
सुरापेन समं ज्ञेयं तस्य पापं च सुव्रत ॥ 43 ॥
1.189.m: The dull-witted person who, having learned the knowledge of the Sun, abandons it— / his sin, O you of good vows, is to be known as equal to that of a drinker of liquor.

1.189.s:
agnihotraparityāgaḥ paṃcayajñiyakarmaṇām ..
mātāpitṛparityāgaḥ kūṭasākṣyaṃ suhṛdvadhaḥ .. 44 ..
1.189.d:
अग्निहोत्रपरित्यागः पंचयज्ञियकर्मणाम् ॥
मातापितृपरित्यागः कूटसाक्ष्यं सुहृद्वधः ॥ 44 ॥
1.189.m: Abandonment of the agnihotra and of the rites of the five sacrifices, / abandonment of mother and father, false testimony, murder of a friend,

1.189.s:
apriyaṃ sūryabhaktānāmabhakṣyasya ca bhakṣaṇam ..
evaṃ niraparādhānāṃ prāṇināṃ ca pramāraṇam .. 45 ..
1.189.d:
अप्रियं सूर्यभक्तानामभक्ष्यस्य च भक्षणम् ॥
एवं निरपराधानां प्राणिनां च प्रमारणम् ॥ 45 ॥
1.189.m: displeasure toward devotees of the Sun, eating what is inedible, / and likewise the slaughter of innocent living beings—

1.189.s:
sarvādhipatyameteṣāṃ nāsti devapurottame ..
ātmalokādhipatyaṃ tu yacchetsarvajatpatiḥ .. 46 ..
1.189.d:
सर्वाधिपत्यमेतेषां नास्ति देवपुरोत्तमे ॥
आत्मलोकाधिपत्यं तु यच्छेत्सर्वजत्पतिः ॥ 46 ॥
1.189.m: for these people there is no sovereignty over all in the supreme city of the gods; / rather, the Lord of all creatures grants them sovereignty only in their own world.

1.189.s:
kecidatraiva mucyante jñānayogaparā narāḥ ..
āvartaṃte punaścānye saṃsāre bhogatatparāḥ .. 47 ..
1.189.d:
केचिदत्रैव मुच्यन्ते ज्ञानयोगपरा नराः ॥
आवर्तंते पुनश्चान्ये संसारे भोगतत्पराः ॥ 47 ॥
1.189.m: Some men, devoted to the yoga of knowledge, are liberated right here; / while others, devoted to worldly pleasures, turn back again into the cycle of existence.

1.189.s:
tasmādvimokṣamanvicchanbhogāsaktiṃ vivarjayet ..
viraktaḥ śāṃtacittātmā sauralokamavāpnuyāt .. 48 ..
1.189.d:
