तस्माद्विमोक्षमन्विच्छन्भोगासक्तिं विवर्जयेत् ॥
विरक्तः शांतचित्तात्मा सौरलोकमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 48 ॥
1.189.m: Therefore, one seeking liberation should abandon attachment to worldly pleasures; / detached, with a tranquil mind and self, he would attain the world of the Sun.

1.189.s:
yaccāpyasaktahṛdayā japantīmaṃ prasaṃgataḥ ..
teṣāmapi vadatyekaḥ svānubhāvānurūpataḥ .. 49 ..
1.189.d:
यच्चाप्यसक्तहृदया जपन्तीमं प्रसंगतः ॥
तेषामपि वदत्येकः स्वानुभावानुरूपतः ॥ 49 ॥
1.189.m: And as for those who, with unattached hearts, chant this [hymn] on occasion, / the One declares for them as well according to their own spiritual power:

1.189.s:
tannārcayanti ye bhānuṃ sakṛducchiṣṭadehinaḥ ..
teṣāṃ piśācaloke tu bhogānbhānuḥ prayacchati .. 1.189.50 ..
1.189.d:
तन्नार्चयन्ति ये भानुं सकृदुच्छिष्टदेहिनः ॥
तेषां पिशाचलोके तु भोगान्भानुः प्रयच्छति ॥ 1.189.50 ॥
1.189.m: Those with impure bodies who do not worship the Sun even once— / to them the Sun gives worldly pleasures in the world of the piśācas.

1.189.s:
dvirjapaṃti ca ye bhānuṃ krūrāḥ saṃkruddhalocanāḥ ..
rakṣoloke ravisteṣāṃ mahābhāgyaṃ prayacchati .. 51 ..
1.189.d:
द्विर्जपंति च ये भानुं क्रूराः संक्रुद्धलोचनाः ॥
रक्षोलोके रविस्तेषां महाभाग्यं प्रयच्छति ॥ 51 ॥
1.189.m: Those who, being cruel and with enraged eyes, chant to the Sun twice— / to them the Sun grants great fortune in the world of the rakṣasas.

1.189.s:
trirarcayanti ye bhānuṃ madyamāṃsaratā narāḥ ..
ṛṣiloke ravisteṣāṃ bhogāndivyānprayacchati .. 52 ..
1.189.d:
त्रिरर्चयन्ति ये भानुं मद्यमांसरता नराः ॥
ऋषिलोके रविस्तेषां भोगान्दिव्यान्प्रयच्छति ॥ 52 ॥
1.189.m: Those men who, indulging in wine and meat, worship the Sun thrice— / to them the Sun grants divine pleasures in the world of the sages.

1.189.s:
ye nṛtyagītaṃ kurvaṃti triścaturdhā yadṛcchayā ..
sūryasyāgre tu te yāṃti gaṃdharvabhavanaṃ khaga .. 53 ..
1.189.d:
ये नृत्यगीतं कुर्वंति त्रिश्चतुर्धा यदृच्छया ॥
सूर्यस्याग्रे तु ते यांति गंधर्वभवनं खग ॥ 53 ॥
1.189.m: Those who spontaneously perform dance and song three or four times / before the Sun, O bird, go to the abode of the gandharvas.

1.189.s:
lokāḥ khyātiṃ samuddiśya pūjayaṃti ca gopatim ..
teṣāṃ śakrālaye bhānuḥ kāmāntsarvānprayacchati .. 54 ..
1.189.d:
लोकाः ख्यातिं समुद्दिश्य पूजयंति च गोपतिम् ॥
तेषां शक्रालये भानुः कामान्त्सर्वान्प्रयच्छति ॥ 54 ॥
1.189.m: People who worship the Lord of rays with an eye to fame— / to them the Sun grants all desires in the abode of Śakra.

1.189.s:
kāmāsaktena cittena yaḥ ṣaḍarcayate ravim ..
prājāpatye ravistasya loke bhogānprayacchati .. 55 ..
1.189.d:
कामासक्तेन चित्तेन यः षडर्चयते रविम् ॥
प्राजापत्ये रविस्तस्य लोके भोगान्प्रयच्छति ॥ 55 ॥
1.189.m: He who worships the Sun six times with a mind clinging to desire— / to him the Sun grants worldly pleasures in the world of Prajāpati.

1.189.s:
navakṛtvorcayedyastu citrabhānuṃ khagādhipa ..
sa yāti viṣṇusālokyaṃ viṣṇunā saha modate .. 56..
1.189.d:
नवकृत्वोर्चयेद्यस्तु चित्रभानुं खगाधिप ॥
स याति विष्णुसालोक्यं विष्णुना सह मोदते ॥ 56॥
1.189.m: Whoever worships the Sun of variegated rays nine times, O king of birds, / goes to the same world as Viṣṇu and rejoices with Viṣṇu.

1.189.s:
tasmādapi paraṃ sthānaṃ yadbhūtānāṃ manoharam ..
aprameyaguṇaidivyairvimānaiḥ sārvakāmikaiḥ .. 57 ..
1.189.d:
तस्मादपि परं स्थानं यद्भूतानां मनोहरम् ॥
अप्रमेयगुणैदिव्यैर्विमानैः सार्वकामिकैः ॥ 57 ॥
1.189.m: Higher even than that is the place delightful to living beings, / [endowed] with divine celestial chariots of immeasurable qualities, granting all desires,

1.189.s:
asaṃkhyairvastubhirvyāptaṃ gairikai raktacitrakaiḥ ..
nānāgṛhasamākīrṇaiḥ sūryakoṭisamaprabham .. 58 ..
1.189.d:
असंख्यैर्वस्तुभिर्व्याप्तं गैरिकै रक्तचित्रकैः ॥
नानागृहसमाकीर्णैः सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभम् ॥ 58 ॥
1.189.m: filled with countless objects, with red-coloured minerals, / crowded with various mansions, equal in splendour to ten million suns.

1.189.s:
tatsthānaṃ te pragacchaṃti arcayanti ca ye dvijān ..
tatra loke khagaśreṣṭha vasaṃti viharaṃti ca ..
tasmādapi paraṃ sthānaṃ jyotiṣkaṃ sauramucyate .. 59 ..
1.189.d:
तत्स्थानं ते प्रगच्छंति अर्चयन्ति च ये द्विजान् ॥
तत्र लोके खगश्रेष्ठ वसंति विहरंति च ॥
तस्मादपि परं स्थानं ज्योतिष्कं सौरमुच्यते ॥ 59 ॥
1.189.m: To that place go those who worship brāhmaṇas; / in that world, O best of birds, they reside and sport; / higher even than that is declared the luminous realm of the Sun.

1.189.s:
evaṃ sūryānubhāvena nikṛṣṭenāpi karmaṇā ..
naraiḥ sthānānyavāpyante śraddhābhāvānurūpataḥ .. ..1.189.60..
sauradharmeṣu sūryānūrusaṃvādavarṇanam
1.189.d:
एवं सूर्यानुभावेन निकृष्टेनापि कर्मणा ॥
नरैः स्थानान्यवाप्यन्ते श्रद्धाभावानुरूपतः ॥ ॥1.189.60॥
सौरधर्मेषु सूर्यानूरुसंवादवर्णनम्
1.189.m:
Thus, by the power of the Sun, even through lowly action, / places are attained by men according to the nature of their faith.
Description of the dialogue between Sūrya and Anūru concerning solar duties.

1.190.s:
.. .. saptāśvatilaka uvāca .. ..
tārārūpavimānānāmimāḥ saṃti ca koṭayaḥ ..
yaḥ kuryāttu namaskāraṃ tasyaiva ca phalaṃ bhavet .. 1 ..
1.190.d:
॥ ॥ सप्ताश्वतिलक उवाच ॥ ॥
तारारूपविमानानामिमाः संति च कोटयः ॥
यः कुर्यात्तु नमस्कारं तस्यैव च फलं भवेत् ॥ 1 ॥
1.190.m:
Saptāśvatilaka said:
There are crores of these celestial chariots having the form of stars.
Whoever pays homage [to them] obtains that very reward.

1.190.s:
ityetā gatayaḥ proktā mahatyaḥ sauradharmiṇām ..
tasmātsauraḥ sadā dharmaḥ kartavyaḥ sukhamicchatā .. 2 ..
1.190.d:
इत्येता गतयः प्रोक्ता महत्यः सौरधर्मिणाम् ॥
तस्मात्सौरः सदा धर्मः कर्तव्यः सुखमिच्छता ॥ 2 ॥
1.190.m:
In this way, these exalted destinies of those who follow solar duties have been declared.
Therefore, one who desires happiness should always practice the solar duty.

1.190.s:
idānīṃ pāpanicayāḥ sthūlā narakahetavaḥ ..
te samāsena kathyante manovākkāyasādhanaiḥ .. 3 ..
1.190.d:
इदानीं पापनिचयाः स्थूला नरकहेतवः ॥
ते समासेन कथ्यन्ते मनोवाक्कायसाधनैः ॥ 3 ॥
1.190.m:
Now, the major accumulations of sin that cause hell,
committed by means of mind, speech, and body, are recounted in brief.

1.190.s:
gavāṃ mārge vane cāgneḥ pure grāme samarpaṇam ..
ityetānīha pāpāni surāpānasamāni ca .. 4 ..
1.190.d:
गवां मार्गे वने चाग्नेः पुरे ग्रामे समर्पणम् ॥
इत्येतानीह पापानि सुरापानसमानि च ॥ 4 ॥
1.190.m:
Setting fire to the path of cows, to a forest,
to a city, or to a village—
such sins as these in this world are considered equal to drinking liquor.

1.190.s:
vane sarvasya haraṇaṃ narastrīgajavājinām ..
gobhūsamīpajātānāmoṣadhīnāṃ ca khecara .. 5 ..
1.190.d:
वने सर्वस्य हरणं नरस्त्रीगजवाजिनाम् ॥
गोभूसमीपजातानामोषधीनां च खेचर ॥ 5 ॥
1.190.m:
Stealing everything in the forest, [stealing] men, women, elephants, and horses,
and medicinal plants that grow near cows or land, O bird,

1.190.s:
candanāgurukarpūrakastūrīpaṭṭavāsasām ..
hastanyāsāpa haraṇaṃ rukmasteyasamaṃ smṛtam .. 6 ..
1.190.d:
चन्दनागुरुकर्पूरकस्तूरीपट्टवाससाम् ॥
हस्तन्यासाप हरणं रुक्मस्तेयसमं स्मृतम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.190.m:
and the misappropriation of sandalwood, agarwood, camphor,
musk, and silk garments entrusted to one's hands is traditionally regarded as equal to stealing gold.

1.190.s:
kanyānāṃ varayogyānāmākarṣaṇamasaṃgataḥ ..
putramitrakalatreṣu gamanaṃ bhaginīṣu ca .. 7 ..
1.190.d:
कन्यानां वरयोग्यानामाकर्षणमसंगतः ॥
पुत्रमित्रकलत्रेषु गमनं भगिनीषु च ॥ 7 ॥
1.190.m:
Abducting maidens fit for a husband without due connection,
having intercourse with the wives of sons or friends, and with sisters,

1.190.s:
kumārīsāhasaṃ ghoramaṃtyajastrīniṣevaṇam ..
savarṇāyāśca gamanaṃ gurutalpasamaṃ smṛtam .. 8 ..
1.190.d:
कुमारीसाहसं घोरमंत्यजस्त्रीनिषेवणम् ॥
सवर्णायाश्च गमनं गुरुतल्पसमं स्मृतम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.190.m:
terrible violence against an unmarried girl, resorting to an outcaste woman,
and intercourse with a woman of one's own caste is regarded as equal to defiling the guru's bed.

1.190.s:
mahāpātakatulyāni pāpānyuktāni yāni tu ..
tāni pātakasaṃjñāni brūmahe copapātakam .. 9 ..
1.190.d:
महापातकतुल्यानि पापान्युक्तानि यानि तु ॥
तानि पातकसंज्ञानि ब्रूमहे चोपपातकम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.190.m:
Now, those sins that have been stated as equal to the major sins
are designated as pātaka; and we also declare the secondary sins.

1.190.s:
dvijāyārthaṃ pariśrutya na prayacchati yo dvija ..
sadbhāryāṇāṃ ca saṃtyāgaḥ sādhubandhutapasvinām .. 1.190.10 ..
1.190.d:
द्विजायार्थं परिश्रुत्य न प्रयच्छति यो द्विज ॥
सद्भार्याणां च संत्यागः साधुबन्धुतपस्विनाम् ॥ 1.190.10 ॥
1.190.m:
A twice-born man who, having promised wealth to a twice-born man, does not give it;
the abandonment of good wives, of virtuous people, relatives, and ascetics;

1.190.s:
gobhū hiraṇyavastrāṇāmapahāraḥ prayatnataḥ ..
īśvarārpitabuddhīnāṃ pīḍanaṃ sumahatkṛtam .. 11 ..
1.190.d:
गोभू हिरण्यवस्त्राणामपहारः प्रयत्नतः ॥
ईश्वरार्पितबुद्धीनां पीडनं सुमहत्कृतम् ॥ 11 ॥
1.190.m:
the deliberate theft of cows, land, gold, and clothes;
inflicting great torment upon those whose intellects are dedicated to the Lord;

1.190.s:
yaḥ pīḍāmāśramasthāna ācaredalpikāmapi ..
tadbhūtyuparibhūtasya paśudhānyadhanasya ca .. 12 ..
1.190.d:
यः पीडामाश्रमस्थान आचरेदल्पिकामपि ॥
तद्भूत्युपरिभूतस्य पशुधान्यधनस्य च ॥ 12 ॥
1.190.m:
he who commits even the slightest torment against a hermitage-dweller,
or against the cattle, grain, and wealth that constitute his prosperity;

1.190.s:
kūpadhānyapaśusteyamayājyānāṃ ca yājanam ..
yajñārāmataḍāgānāṃ dārāpatyasya vikrayaḥ .. 13 ..
1.190.d:
कूपधान्यपशुस्तेयमयाज्यानां च याजनम् ॥
यज्ञारामतडागानां दारापत्यस्य विक्रयः ॥ 13 ॥
1.190.m:
the theft of a well, grain, or cattle, officiating at sacrifices for those unfit to be sacrificed for,
the sale of sacrifices, pleasure gardens, ponds, wives, and children;

1.190.s:
tīrtha yātropavāsānāṃ vrate ca japakarmaṇi ..
strīdhanānyupakarṣaṃti ye janāḥ pāpakarmaṇā .. 14 ..
1.190.d:
तीर्थ यात्रोपवासानां व्रते च जपकर्मणि ॥
स्त्रीधनान्युपकर्षंति ये जनाः पापकर्मणा ॥ 14 ॥
1.190.m:
those people who, by wicked deeds, carry off women's property
during pilgrimages to sacred fords, fasts, votive observances, and rites of recitation;

1.190.s:
arakṣaṇaṃ ca nārīṇāṃ madyapastrīniṣevaṇam ..
ṛṣīṇāmapradānaṃ ca dhānyavṛddhyupasevanam .. 15 ..
1.190.d:
अरक्षणं च नारीणां मद्यपस्त्रीनिषेवणम् ॥
ऋषीणामप्रदानं च धान्यवृद्ध्युपसेवनम् ॥ 15 ॥
1.190.m:
neglecting to protect women, having intercourse with a woman who drinks liquor,
not making offerings to sages, and practicing usury on grain;

1.190.s:
devāgnisādhusādhvīnāṃ nindā gobrāhmaṇasya ca ..
pratyakṣaṃ vā parokṣaṃ vā rājamāṇḍalikānapi .. 16 ..
1.190.d:
देवाग्निसाधुसाध्वीनां निन्दा गोब्राह्मणस्य च ॥
प्रत्यक्षं वा परोक्षं वा राजमाण्डलिकानपि ॥ 16 ॥
1.190.m:
reviling gods, fire, virtuous men, chaste women,
cows, and brahmins, whether openly or behind their backs, as well as feudatory kings;

1.190.s:
utsannapitṛdevāśca svakarmatyāginaśca ye ..
duḥśīlā nāstikāḥ pāpāḥ sadasacchūnyavādinaḥ .. 17 ..
1.190.d:
उत्सन्नपितृदेवाश्च स्वकर्मत्यागिनश्च ये ॥
दुःशीला नास्तिकाः पापाः सदसच्छून्यवादिनः ॥ 17 ॥
1.190.m:
those by whom ancestors and gods are neglected, those who abandon their own duties,
the ill-behaved, atheists, sinners, and nihilists who argue about existence and non-existence;

1.190.s:
evaṃ kāme pravṛtte tu viyonau paśuyoniṣu ..
rajasvalāsvayonau tu maithunaṃ yaḥ samācaret .. 18 ..
1.190.d:
एवं कामे प्रवृत्ते तु वियोनौ पशुयोनिषु ॥
रजस्वलास्वयोनौ तु मैथुनं यः समाचरेत् ॥ 18 ॥
1.190.m:
likewise, when lust is aroused, he who engages in copulation
in an unnatural womb, among animals, with menstruating women, or in a non-generative orifice;

1.190.s:
strīputramitrasaṃprīte rārāmocchedakāśca ye ..
janasyāpriyavaktāro janābhiprāyabhedinaḥ .. 19 ..
1.190.d:
स्त्रीपुत्रमित्रसंप्रीते रारामोच्छेदकाश्च ये ॥
जनस्याप्रियवक्तारो जनाभिप्रायभेदिनः ॥ 19 ॥
1.190.m:
those who destroy pleasure gardens dear to wives, sons, and friends,
those who speak unpleasant words to people, and those who thwart people's intentions;

1.190.s:
bhettā taḍāgavaprāṇāṃ saṃkramāṇāṃ rasasya ca ..
ekapaṃktisthitānāṃ ca paṃktibhedaṃ karoti yaḥ ..1.190.20..
1.190.d:
भेत्ता तडागवप्राणां संक्रमाणां रसस्य च ॥
एकपंक्तिस्थितानां च पंक्तिभेदं करोति यः ॥1.190.20॥
1.190.m:
he who breaches the embankments of ponds, bridges, or channels of liquid,
and he who creates a division in a line among those seated in a single row—

1.190.s:
ityetaistu narāḥ pāpairupapātakinaḥ smṛtāḥ ..21..
saptāśvatilakāruṇasaṃvādam
1.190.d:
इत्येतैस्तु नराः पापैरुपपातकिनः स्मृताः ॥21॥
सप्ताश्वतिलकारुणसंवादम्
1.190.m:
by these sins, men are traditionally considered to be guilty of secondary sins.
The dialogue between Saptāśvatilaka and Aruṇa.

1.191.s:
.. saptāśvatilaka uvāca .. ..
ye gobrāhmaṇasasyānāṃ sādhūnāṃ tu tapasvinām ..
dūṣakāścaiva vartaṃte narā narakagāminaḥ .. 1 ..
1.191.d:
॥ सप्ताश्वतिलक उवाच ॥ ॥
ये गोब्राह्मणसस्यानां साधूनां तु तपस्विनाम् ॥
दूषकाश्चैव वर्तंते नरा नरकगामिनः ॥ 1 ॥
1.191.m:
Saptāśvatilaka said:
Those men who persist in abusing cows,
brahmins, crops, virtuous people, and ascetics go to hell.

1.191.s:
pariśrameṇa tapyante ye'pare tasya sūcakāḥ ..
paradāraratānāṃ ca kanyāyā dūṣakāśca ye .. 2 ..
1.191.d:
परिश्रमेण तप्यन्ते येऽपरे तस्य सूचकाः ॥
परदाररतानां च कन्याया दूषकाश्च ये ॥ 2 ॥
1.191.m:
Others who are distressed by another's toil, those who inform upon him,
those who delight in other men's wives, and those who deflower maidens;

1.191.s:
goṣṭhāgnijalaramyāsu tarucchāyānageṣu ca ..
tyajaṃti ye purīṣāṇi ārāmā yataneṣu ca .. 3 ..
1.191.d:
गोष्ठाग्निजलरम्यासु तरुच्छायानगेषु च ॥
त्यजंति ये पुरीषाणि आरामा यतनेषु च ॥ 3 ॥
1.191.m:
those who discharge excrement in cowpens, near fire, in pleasant waters,
in the shade of trees, on hills, in gardens, or in temples;

1.191.s:
madyapānaratā nityaṃ gītavādyaratā narāḥ ..
kāmakrodhamadāviṣṭā raṃdhrānveṣaṇatatparāḥ .. 4 ..
1.191.d:
मद्यपानरता नित्यं गीतवाद्यरता नराः ॥
कामक्रोधमदाविष्टा रंध्रान्वेषणतत्पराः ॥ 4 ॥
1.191.m:
men who are constantly addicted to drinking liquor, devoted to singing and instrumental music,
possessed by lust, anger, and arrogance, intent upon seeking out [others'] vulnerabilities;

1.191.s:
pākhaṇḍamatasaṃyuktā vṛthā saṃlāpa kautukāḥ ..
ye mārgānuparudhaṃti parasīmāṃ haraṃti ca .. 5 ..
1.191.d:
पाखण्डमतसंयुक्ता वृथा संलाप कौतुकाः ॥
ये मार्गानुपरुधंति परसीमां हरंति च ॥ 5 ॥
1.191.m:
those endowed with heretical doctrines, eager for idle chatter,
those who obstruct pathways, and those who seize another's boundary;

1.191.s:
kūṭaśāsanakartāraḥ kūṭakarmakṛto narāḥ ..
dhanuṣaḥ śilpiśastrāṇāṃ yaḥ kartā yaśca vikrayī .. 6 ..
1.191.d:
कूटशासनकर्तारः कूटकर्मकृतो नराः ॥
धनुषः शिल्पिशस्त्राणां यः कर्ता यश्च विक्रयी ॥ 6 ॥
1.191.m:
men who forge royal edicts, who engage in deceitful practices,
and he who makes or sells bows, artisans' tools, or weapons;

1.191.s:
nirdayotīvabhṛtyeṣu paśūnāṃ damakaśca yaḥ ..
mithyā pravadato vācamākarṇayati yaḥ śanaiḥ ..
svāmimitragurudrohī māyāvī capalaḥ śaṭhaḥ .. 7 ..
1.191.d:
निर्दयोतीवभृत्येषु पशूनां दमकश्च यः ॥
मिथ्या प्रवदतो वाचमाकर्णयति यः शनैः ॥
स्वामिमित्रगुरुद्रोही मायावी चपलः शठः ॥ 7 ॥

1.191.s:
ye bhāryāputramitrāṇi bālavṛddhakuśāturān ..
bhṛtyānatithibandhūṃśca tyajaṃti ca bubhukṣitān .. 8 ..
1.191.d:
ये भार्यापुत्रमित्राणि बालवृद्धकुशातुरान् ॥
भृत्यानतिथिबन्धूंश्च त्यजंति च बुभुक्षितान् ॥ 8 ॥
1.191.m:
those who abandon their wives, sons, friends, children, the elderly,
the afflicted, servants, guests, and relatives while they are hungry;

1.191.s:
yaḥ svayaṃ pakvamaśnāti viprāyānnaṃ na yacchati ..
vṛthā pākaḥ sa vijñeyo brahmavādiṣu garhitaḥ .. 9 ..
1.191.d:
यः स्वयं पक्वमश्नाति विप्रायान्नं न यच्छति ॥
वृथा पाकः स विज्ञेयो ब्रह्मवादिषु गर्हितः ॥ 9 ॥
1.191.m:
he who eats food cooked for himself and does not give food to a brahmin,
is to be known as one who cooks in vain, censured among the knowers of the Veda;

1.191.s:
niyamaṃ svayamādāya ye tyajaṃtyajiteṃdriyāḥ ..
pravrajyāvasitā ye ca rahasyānāṃ tu bhedakāḥ .. 1.191.10 ..
1.191.d:
नियमं स्वयमादाय ये त्यजंत्यजितेंद्रियाः ॥
प्रव्रज्यावसिता ये च रहस्यानां तु भेदकाः ॥ 1.191.10 ॥
1.191.m:
those who, lacking control over their senses, take a religious vow upon themselves and then abandon it,
those who lapse from ascetic wandering, and those who disclose secrets;

1.191.s:
ye tāḍayaṃti gāṃ mūḍhāstrāsayaṃti muhurmuhuḥ ..
durbalaṃ na ca puṣṇaṃti pranaṣṭānnānviṣaṃti ca .. 11 ..
1.191.d:
ये ताडयंति गां मूढास्त्रासयंति मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
दुर्बलं न च पुष्णंति प्रनष्टान्नान्विषंति च ॥ 11 ॥
1.191.m:
the fools who beat a cow and frighten it repeatedly,
who do not nourish a weak [cow], and who do not search for lost ones;

1.191.s:
pīḍayaṃtyatibhāreṇa akṣayaṃ vāhayaṃti ca ..
vṛṣāṇāṃ vṛṣaṇānanye pāpiṣṭhā gālayaṃti hi ..
vāhayaṃti ca gāṃ vaṃdhyāṃ te pāpiṣṭhā narādhamāḥ .. 12 ..
1.191.d:
पीडयंत्यतिभारेण अक्षयं वाहयंति च ॥
वृषाणां वृषणानन्ये पापिष्ठा गालयंति हि ॥
वाहयंति च गां वंध्यां ते पापिष्ठा नराधमाः ॥ 12 ॥

1.191.s:
anarthavikalaṃ hīnaṃ bālavṛddhakṛśānugam ..
nānukaṃpaṃti ye mūḍhāste yāṃti narakaṃ narāḥ .. 13 ..
1.191.d:
अनर्थविकलं हीनं बालवृद्धकृशानुगम् ॥
नानुकंपंति ये मूढास्ते यांति नरकं नराः ॥ 13 ॥
1.191.m:
those foolish men who have no compassion for one who is destitute, distressed, destitute of resources,
or accompanied by children, the aged, or the emaciated—they go to hell.

1.191.s:
ajāvikā māhiṣikāḥ savitrīvṛṣalīpatiḥ ..
kṣatraviṭśūdravṛddhāśca svadharmavihatāḥ sadā .. 14 ..
1.191.d:
अजाविका माहिषिकाः सवित्रीवृषलीपतिः ॥
क्षत्रविट्शूद्रवृद्धाश्च स्वधर्मविहताः सदा ॥ 14 ॥
1.191.m:
Those who keep goats, sheep, or buffaloes, the husband of an outcaste woman who has borne children,
and the elders of kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras who have perpetually ruined their own duties;

1.191.s:
śilpinaḥ kārukā veśyāḥ kṣemakāranṛpadhvajāḥ ..
nartakyo jyotiṣi hatāḥ sarve narakagāminaḥ .. 15 ..
1.191.d:
शिल्पिनः कारुका वेश्याः क्षेमकारनृपध्वजाः ॥
नर्तक्यो ज्योतिषि हताः सर्वे नरकगामिनः ॥ 15 ॥
1.191.m:
artisans, craftsmen, prostitutes, those who harm the welfare [of others] or bear the insignia of kings,
female dancers, and those ruined by astrology—all of these go to hell.

1.191.s:
ghṛta tailānupānāni madhumāṃsarasāsavam ..
guḍekṣukṣīraśākānhi dadhimūlaphalāni ca .. 16 ..
1.191.d:
घृत तैलानुपानानि मधुमांसरसासवम् ॥
गुडेक्षुक्षीरशाकान्हि दधिमूलफलानि च ॥ 16 ॥
1.191.m:
Ghee, oil, drinks taken with medicine, honey, meat, meat-broth, liquor,
molasses, sugarcane, milk, vegetables, curd, roots, and fruits;

1.191.s:
tṛṇāni kāṣṭhaṃ puṣpāṇi bījauṣadhimanuttamām ..
upānacchatra śakaṭamāsanaṃ śayanaṃ mṛdaḥ .. 17 ..
1.191.d:
तृणानि काष्ठं पुष्पाणि बीजौषधिमनुत्तमाम् ॥
उपानच्छत्र शकटमासनं शयनं मृदः ॥ 17 ॥
1.191.m:
grass, wood, flowers, excellent seeds and medicinal herbs,
shoes, a royal parasol, a cart, a seat, a bed, clay,

1.191.s:
tāmraṃ sīsaṃ trapuṃ kāṃsyaṃ śaṃkhādyaṃ ca jalodbhavam ..
vārkṣaṃ vā vaiṇavaṃ vāpi gṛhopakaraṇāni ca ..18..
1.191.d:
ताम्रं सीसं त्रपुं कांस्यं शंखाद्यं च जलोद्भवम् ॥
वार्क्षं वा वैणवं वापि गृहोपकरणानि च ॥18॥
1.191.m:
copper, lead, tin, bronze, aquatic products beginning with conch shells,
objects made of wood or bamboo, household utensils,

1.191.s:
aurṇakārpāsakauśeyabhaṃgapaṭṭodbhavāni ca ..
sthūlasūkṣmāṇi saṃmūḍhā ye ca lokā haraṃti vai ..19..
1.191.d:
और्णकार्पासकौशेयभंगपट्टोद्भवानि च ॥
स्थूलसूक्ष्माणि संमूढा ये च लोका हरंति वै ॥19॥
1.191.m:
and items made of wool, cotton, silk, hemp, or woven cloth,
both coarse and fine—those utterly deluded people who steal these

1.191.s:
evamādīni cānyāni dravyāṇi vividhāni ca..
narakeṣu dhruvaṃ gacchedyau hareta pumānbalāt .. 1.191.20 ..
1.191.d:
एवमादीनि चान्यानि द्रव्याणि विविधानि च॥
नरकेषु ध्रुवं गच्छेद्यौ हरेत पुमान्बलात् ॥ 1.191.20 ॥
1.191.m:
and various other goods such as these—
a man who steals them by force would certainly go to the hells.

1.191.s:
yadvā tadvā tu pārokṣyamapi sarṣapamātrakam ..
apahṛtya naro yāti narakaṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 21 ..
1.191.d:
यद्वा तद्वा तु पारोक्ष्यमपि सर्षपमात्रकम् ॥
अपहृत्य नरो याति नरकं नात्र संशयः ॥ 21 ॥
1.191.m: Stealing whatever it may be behind one's back, even a mere mustard seed, / a person goes to hell; of this there is no doubt.

1.191.s:
evamādyairnaraḥ pāpairutkrāṃteḥ samanaṃtaram ..
śarīrayātanārthaṃ tatpūrvakāyamavāpnuyāt .. 22 ..
1.191.d:
एवमाद्यैर्नरः पापैरुत्क्रांतेः समनंतरम् ॥
शरीरयातनार्थं तत्पूर्वकायमवाप्नुयात् ॥ 22 ॥
1.191.m: Through such sins and the like, immediately after departure [from life], / a person obtains that former body for the sake of bodily torments.

1.191.s:
yamaloke vrajedevaṃ śarīreṇa yamājñayā ..
yamadūtairmahāghorairnīyamānaḥ suduḥkhitaḥ .. 23 ..
1.191.d:
यमलोके व्रजेदेवं शरीरेण यमाज्ञया ॥
यमदूतैर्महाघोरैर्नीयमानः सुदुःखितः ॥ 23 ॥
1.191.m: He thus goes with that body to Yama's world by Yama's command, / led by the exceedingly terrifying messengers of Yama, in great misery.

1.191.s:
devamānuṣajīvānāmadharmaniratātmanām ..
dharmarājaḥ smṛtaḥ śāstā sughorairvividhairvadhaiḥ .. 24 ..
1.191.d:
देवमानुषजीवानामधर्मनिरतात्मनाम् ॥
धर्मराजः स्मृतः शास्ता सुघोरैर्विविधैर्वधैः ॥ 24 ॥
1.191.m: For divine and human beings whose minds are devoted to unrighteousness, / Dharmarāja is declared to be the punisher by various most terrible executions.

1.191.s:
vinayābhāvayuktānāṃ pramādā tsvalitātmanām ..
prāyaścittairbahuvidhaiḥ pātakaṃ naṣṭatāmiyāt .. 25 ..
1.191.d:
विनयाभावयुक्तानां प्रमादा त्स्वलितात्मनाम् ॥
प्रायश्चित्तैर्बहुविधैः पातकं नष्टतामियात् ॥ 25 ॥
1.191.m: For those lacking discipline who have stumbled out of negligence, / sin is destroyed through various kinds of expiations.

1.191.s:
pāradārikacorāṇāmanyāyavyavahāriṇām ..
śāstā kṣitipatiḥ proktaḥ pracchannānāṃ ca dharmarāṭ .. 26 ..
1.191.d:
पारदारिकचोराणामन्यायव्यवहारिणाम् ॥
शास्ता क्षितिपतिः प्रोक्तः प्रच्छन्नानां च धर्मराट् ॥ 26 ॥
1.191.m: For adulterers, thieves, and those conducting unjust dealings, / the ruler of the earth is declared the punisher, while Dharmarāṭ punishes those [sins] done in secret.

1.191.s:
tasmātkṛtasya pāpasya prāyaścittaṃ samācaret ..
nābhuktasyānyathā nāśaḥ kalpakoṭiśatairapi .. 27 ..
1.191.d:
तस्मात्कृतस्य पापस्य प्रायश्चित्तं समाचरेत् ॥
नाभुक्तस्यान्यथा नाशः कल्पकोटिशतैरपि ॥ 27 ॥
1.191.m: Therefore, one should perform expiation for a committed sin; / otherwise, an unexperienced [sin] is not destroyed even in hundreds of millions of kalpas.

1.191.s:
yaḥ karoti śubhaṃ karma kārayedanumodayet ..
kāyena manasā vācā sa viṃdetottamaṃ sukham ..28..
1.191.d:
यः करोति शुभं कर्म कारयेदनुमोदयेत् ॥
कायेन मनसा वाचा स विंदेतोत्तमं सुखम् ॥28॥
1.191.m: He who performs an auspicious deed, causes it to be done, or approves of it / with body, mind, or speech, attains supreme happiness.

1.191.s:
iti saṃkṣepataḥ proktā pāpabhedāttridhā gatiḥ ..
tathānyā gatayaścitrāḥ kathyaṃte karmabhedataḥ .. 29 ..
saptāśvatilakānūrusaṃvādavarṇanam
1.191.d:
इति संक्षेपतः प्रोक्ता पापभेदात्त्रिधा गतिः ॥
तथान्या गतयश्चित्राः कथ्यंते कर्मभेदतः ॥ 29 ॥
सप्ताश्वतिलकानूरुसंवादवर्णनम्
1.191.m:
Thus the threefold destiny has been concisely described according to different sins; / likewise, other diverse destinies are described according to different deeds.
Description of the Dialogue Between Saptāśvatilaka and Anūru

1.192.s:
saptāśvatilaka uvāca .. ..
saṃtrāsajananaṃ ghoraṃ pāpānāṃ pāpakāriṇām ...
garbhasthairjāyamānaiśca bālaistaruṇamadhyamaiḥ .. 1
1.192.d:
सप्ताश्वतिलक उवाच ॥ ॥
संत्रासजननं घोरं पापानां पापकारिणाम् ॥।
गर्भस्थैर्जायमानैश्च बालैस्तरुणमध्यमैः ॥ 1
1.192.m: Saptāśvatilaka said: / Producing great terror, frightful for the wicked who commit sins, / [the path] must be trodden by those in the womb, those being born, children, youths, and the middle-aged,

1.192.s:
strīpunapuṃsakairvṛddhairgaṃtavyaṃ sarvajaṃtuṣu ..
śubhāśubhaphalaṃ tatra bhoktavyaṃ dehibhistathā .. 2 ..
1.192.d:
स्त्रीपुनपुंसकैर्वृद्धैर्गंतव्यं सर्वजंतुषु ॥
शुभाशुभफलं तत्र भोक्तव्यं देहिभिस्तथा ॥ 2 ॥
1.192.m: by women, men, eunuchs, and the aged, among all creatures; / and there the fruit of good and evil must be experienced by embodied beings.

1.192.s:
citraguptādibhiḥ sarvairdharmasthaiḥ satyavādibhi ..
proktaṃ vai dharmarājasya nikaṭe yacchubhāśubham ..
avaśyaṃ hi kṛtaṃ karma bhoktavyaṃ tadvicāritam .. 3 ..
1.192.d:
चित्रगुप्तादिभिः सर्वैर्धर्मस्थैः सत्यवादिभि ॥
प्रोक्तं वै धर्मराजस्य निकटे यच्छुभाशुभम् ॥
अवश्यं हि कृतं कर्म भोक्तव्यं तद्विचारितम् ॥ 3 ॥
1.192.m: Whatever good and evil is spoken in the presence of Dharmarāja / by all those abiding in righteousness, speakers of truth, Citragupta and the others— / a deed that was performed must necessarily be experienced; so it has been judged.

1.192.s:
tatra ye śubhakarmāṇaḥ saumya cittā dayānvitāḥ ..
te narā yāṃti saumyena yathā yamaniketanam .. 4 ..
1.192.d:
तत्र ये शुभकर्माणः सौम्य चित्ता दयान्विताः ॥
ते नरा यांति सौम्येन यथा यमनिकेतनम् ॥ 4 ॥
1.192.m: There, those of good deeds, of gentle mind, and endowed with compassion, / those people go pleasantly, as [befits them], to Yama's abode.

1.192.s:
yaḥ pradadyāddvijeṃdrāṇāmupānatkāṣṭhachatrakam ..
sa ca dharmeṇa mahatā sukhaṃ yāti yamālayam .. 5 ..
1.192.d:
यः प्रदद्याद्द्विजेंद्राणामुपानत्काष्ठछत्रकम् ॥
स च धर्मेण महता सुखं याति यमालयम् ॥ 5 ॥
1.192.m: He who gives shoes, wooden [sandals], and a parasol to eminent twice-born men, / goes comfortably to Yama's abode through great merit.

1.192.s:
sopānatko naro yastu devāyatanamāviśet ..
viśeṣato garbhagṛhaṃ sa saṃtrāsamupāśnute ..6..
1.192.d:
सोपानत्को नरो यस्तु देवायतनमाविशेत् ॥
विशेषतो गर्भगृहं स संत्रासमुपाश्नुते ॥6॥
1.192.m: A man who enters a temple wearing shoes, / especially the inner sanctum, experiences terror.

1.192.s:
sopānatkāni dānāni tathānnaṃ tu viśeṣataḥ ..
evaṃ dānaviśeṣeṇa dharmarājapuraṃ naraḥ ..
yasmādyāti sukhenaiva tasmāddharmaṃ samācaret ..7..
1.192.d:
सोपानत्कानि दानानि तथान्नं तु विशेषतः ॥
एवं दानविशेषेण धर्मराजपुरं नरः ॥
यस्माद्याति सुखेनैव तस्माद्धर्मं समाचरेत् ॥7॥
1.192.m: Gifts accompanied by shoes, and especially food— / through such specific gifts a man / goes to the city of Dharmarāja in comfort; therefore, one should practice dharma.

1.192.s:
ye punaḥ krūrakarmāṇo narāḥ pāparatāḥ khaga ..
te ghoreṇa tathā yāṃti dakṣiṇena yamālayam .. 8 ..
1.192.d:
ये पुनः क्रूरकर्माणो नराः पापरताः खग ॥
ते घोरेण तथा यांति दक्षिणेन यमालयम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.192.m: Moreover, those people of cruel deeds who are devoted to sin, O bird, / go to Yama's abode along the dreadful southern [path].

1.192.s:
ṣaḍaśītisahasrāṇi yojanānāmaśīti ca ..
vaivasvatapuraṃ jñeyaṃ nānārūpamiti sthitam .. 9 ..
1.192.d:
षडशीतिसहस्राणि योजनानामशीति च ॥
वैवस्वतपुरं ज्ञेयं नानारूपमिति स्थितम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.192.m: The city of Vaivasvata is known to be eighty-six thousand / and eighty yojanas [distant]; such is its established, multifaceted nature.

1.192.s:
samīpasthamivābhāti narāṇāṃ śubhacāriṇām ..
pāpānāmatidūrasthaṃ tathā raudreṇa gacchatām .. 1.192.10 ..
1.192.d:
समीपस्थमिवाभाति नराणां शुभचारिणाम् ॥
पापानामतिदूरस्थं तथा रौद्रेण गच्छताम् ॥ 1.192.10 ॥
1.192.m: It appears as if nearby to people who act virtuously; / to sinners, who travel along the terrible [path], it is situated exceedingly far away:

1.192.s:
tīkṣṇakaṃṭakayuktena śarkarānicitena ca ..
kṣuradhārātinistriṃśaiḥ pāṣāṇaiściṃtitena ca .. 11 ..
1.192.d:
तीक्ष्णकंटकयुक्तेन शर्करानिचितेन च ॥
क्षुरधारातिनिस्त्रिंशैः पाषाणैश्चिंतितेन च ॥ 11 ॥
1.192.m: strewn with sharp thorns, covered with gravel, / and beset with stones as sharp as razor edges and swords;

1.192.s:
kvacidarkeṇa mahatā duraṃtaiścaiva khātakaiḥ ..
lohaśaṃkubhirācchinnāstathā khaḍgaiḥ samanvitāḥ .. .. 32 ..
1.192.d:
क्वचिदर्केण महता दुरंतैश्चैव खातकैः ॥
लोहशंकुभिराच्छिन्नास्तथा खड्गैः समन्विताः ॥ ॥ 32 ॥
1.192.m: in some places with intense sun, and bottomless pits, / pierced by iron spikes, and beset with blades.

1.192.s:
tataḥ patadbhirvimalaiḥ parvatairvṛkṣasaṃkulaiḥ ..
pretaprākārayuktena yāṃti mārgeṇa duḥkhitāḥ .. 13 ..
1.192.d:
ततः पतद्भिर्विमलैः पर्वतैर्वृक्षसंकुलैः ॥
प्रेतप्राकारयुक्तेन यांति मार्गेण दुःखिताः ॥ 13 ॥
1.192.m: Then, in misery, they go along a road enclosed by walls of pretas, / with clear mountains falling, crowded with trees;

1.192.s:
kvacidviṣamagartābhiḥ kvacilloṣṭhaiḥ sapicchalaiḥ ..
sutaptavālukābhiśca tathā tīkṣṇaiśca śaṃkubhiḥ .. 14 ..
1.192.d:
क्वचिद्विषमगर्ताभिः क्वचिल्लोष्ठैः सपिच्छलैः ॥
सुतप्तवालुकाभिश्च तथा तीक्ष्णैश्च शंकुभिः ॥ 14 ॥
1.192.m: in some places with uneven pits, in some with slippery clods of earth, / with extremely hot sands, and with sharp spikes;

1.192.s:
anekaśākhāracitairvyāptairvaṃśavanaiḥ kvacit ..
kaṣṭena tamasaḥ mārga anā laṃbe sudāruṇi ..15..
1.192.d:
अनेकशाखारचितैर्व्याप्तैर्वंशवनैः क्वचित् ॥
कष्टेन तमसः मार्ग अना लंबे सुदारुणि ॥15॥
1.192.m: in some places dense with bamboo thickets formed of countless branches, / along a painful road of darkness, devoid of support and extremely dreadful;

1.192.s:
atha śṛṃgāṭakairvyāptaiḥ kvaciddāvāgninā punaḥ ..
kvacittaptaśilābhiśca kvacidvyāptaṃ himena tu .. 16 ..
1.192.d:
अथ शृंगाटकैर्व्याप्तैः क्वचिद्दावाग्निना पुनः ॥
क्वचित्तप्तशिलाभिश्च क्वचिद्व्याप्तं हिमेन तु ॥ 16 ॥
1.192.m: then filled with caltrops, in some places again with forest fire, / in some places with scorching stones, and in some places covered with snow;

1.192.s:
kvacidvālukayā vyāptamākaṃṭhāṃtaṃ praveśayet ..
kvacidduṣṭāṃbunā vyāptaṃ kvacicca kariṣāgninā..17..
1.192.d:
क्वचिद्वालुकया व्याप्तमाकंठांतं प्रवेशयेत् ॥
क्वचिद्दुष्टांबुना व्याप्तं क्वचिच्च करिषाग्निना॥17॥
1.192.m: in some places covered in sand, which makes one sink up to the neck; / in some places covered with foul water, and in some places with fire from dried cow dung;

1.192.s:
kvacitsiṃhaiḥ kvacidvyāghrairdaṃśaiḥ kīṭaiśca dāruṇaiḥ ..
kvacinmahājalaukābhiḥ kvaci dvājagaraiḥ punaḥ ..18..
1.192.d:
क्वचित्सिंहैः क्वचिद्व्याघ्रैर्दंशैः कीटैश्च दारुणैः ॥
क्वचिन्महाजलौकाभिः क्वचि द्वाजगरैः पुनः ॥18॥
1.192.m: in some places with lions, in some with tigers, biting insects, and terrifying bugs; / in some places with huge leeches, and in some places again with pythons;

1.192.s:
makṣikābhiśca raudrābhiḥ kvacitsapeṃrviṣolbaṇaiḥ ..
mahāgajeṃdrayūnaiśca balonmattaiḥ pramāthibhiḥ ..19..
1.192.d:
मक्षिकाभिश्च रौद्राभिः क्वचित्सपेंर्विषोल्बणैः ॥
महागजेंद्रयूनैश्च बलोन्मत्तैः प्रमाथिभिः ॥19॥
1.192.m: and with savage flies, in some places with serpents possessing virulent poison; / and by young lordly elephants, mad with strength and crushing everything;

1.192.s:
paṃthānamullikhadbhiśca tīkṣṇa śṛṃgairmahāvṛṣaiḥ ..
mahāśṛṃgaiśca mahiṣairuṣṭrairmattairmadāturaiḥ..1.192.20..
1.192.d:
पंथानमुल्लिखद्भिश्च तीक्ष्ण शृंगैर्महावृषैः ॥
महाशृंगैश्च महिषैरुष्ट्रैर्मत्तैर्मदातुरैः॥1.192.20॥
1.192.m: by great bulls with sharp horns tearing up the path; / and by buffaloes with great horns, and by rutting, lust-crazed camels;

1.192.s:
ḍākinībhiśca raudrābhirvikarālaiśca rākṣasaiḥ..
vyādhibhiśca mahāghoraiḥ pīḍyamānā vrajaṃti hi .. .. 21 ..
1.192.d:
डाकिनीभिश्च रौद्राभिर्विकरालैश्च राक्षसैः॥
व्याधिभिश्च महाघोरैः पीड्यमाना व्रजंति हि ॥ ॥ 21 ॥
1.192.m: by terrible ḍākinīs and dreadful rākṣasas; / tormented by frightful diseases, they indeed proceed;

1.192.s:
mahāpāśavimiśreṇa mahācaṃḍena vāyunā ..
mahāpāṣāṇavarṣeṇa hanyamānā nirāśrayāḥ .. 22..
1.192.d:
महापाशविमिश्रेण महाचंडेन वायुना ॥
महापाषाणवर्षेण हन्यमाना निराश्रयाः ॥ 22॥
1.192.m: by a violent wind mingled with great nooses, / struck by a rain of great stones, devoid of refuge.

1.192.s:
kvacidvidyutprapātena dīryamāṇā vrajaṃti hi ..
patadbhirvajrasaṃghātairulkāpātaiśca dāruṇaiḥ .. 23 ..
1.192.d:
क्वचिद्विद्युत्प्रपातेन दीर्यमाणा व्रजंति हि ॥
पतद्भिर्वज्रसंघातैरुल्कापातैश्च दारुणैः ॥ 23 ॥
1.192.m: In some places shattered by falling lightning, they indeed proceed, / with falling masses of thunderbolts and dreadful meteors.

1.192.s:
pradīptāṃgāravarṣeṇa dahyamānā vrajaṃti hi ..
mahāṃdhakāraśukreṇa pīḍyamānā vrajaṃti hi .. 24 ..
1.192.d:
प्रदीप्तांगारवर्षेण दह्यमाना व्रजंति हि ॥
महांधकारशुक्रेण पीड्यमाना व्रजंति हि ॥ 24 ॥
1.192.m: Burned by a rain of blazing coals, they indeed proceed; / afflicted by profound darkness [...], they indeed proceed.

1.192.s:
mahāmegharavairghorairvitrāsyaṃte muhurmuhuḥ ..
tīkṣṇapāṣāṇayuktena pūryamāṇāḥ samantataḥ .. 25 ..
1.192.d:
महामेघरवैर्घोरैर्वित्रास्यंते मुहुर्मुहुः ॥
तीक्ष्णपाषाणयुक्तेन पूर्यमाणाः समन्ततः ॥ 25 ॥
1.192.m: They are repeatedly terrified by the frightful roaring of great storm clouds; / filled from all sides with sharp stones,

1.192.s:
mahākṣurāṃbudhārābhiḥ sevyamānā vrajaṃti hi ..
mahāmegharavairghorai rvitrāsyante muhurmuhuḥ ..26..
1.192.d:
महाक्षुरांबुधाराभिः सेव्यमाना व्रजंति हि ॥
महामेघरवैर्घोरै र्वित्रास्यन्ते मुहुर्मुहुः ॥26॥
1.192.m: lashed by streams of water like great razor blades, they indeed proceed; / they are repeatedly terrified by the frightful roaring of great storm clouds;

1.192.s:
bhṛśaṃ śītena tīkṣṇena rūkṣeṇa mārutena ca ..
itthaṃ mārgeṇa raudreṇa pātheyarahitena ca ..27..
1.192.d:
भृशं शीतेन तीक्ष्णेन रूक्षेण मारुतेन च ॥
इत्थं मार्गेण रौद्रेण पाथेयरहितेन च ॥27॥
1.192.m: by intensely cold, piercing, and harsh wind; / thus, along that dreadful road, devoid of provisions,

1.192.s:
nirālaṃbena durgeṇa nirjanena samaṃtataḥ ..
aviśrāmeṇa mahatā vigatāpāyadurdharaiḥ .. 28 ..
1.192.d:
निरालंबेन दुर्गेण निर्जनेन समंततः ॥
अविश्रामेण महता विगतापायदुर्धरैः ॥ 28 ॥
1.192.m: devoid of support, difficult to traverse, completely desolate, / without any rest, by inescapable and unendurable [terrors],

1.192.s:
nīyaṃte dehinaḥ sarve ye mūḍhāḥ pāpakāriṇaḥ ..
iti jñātvā naraḥ kuryātpuṇyaṃ pāpaṃ ca varjayet ..
puṇyena yāti devatvaṃ pāpena narakaṃ vrajet .. 29 ..
1.192.d:
नीयंते देहिनः सर्वे ये मूढाः पापकारिणः ॥
इति ज्ञात्वा नरः कुर्यात्पुण्यं पापं च वर्जयेत् ॥
पुण्येन याति देवत्वं पापेन नरकं व्रजेत् ॥ 29 ॥
1.192.m: all embodied beings who are foolish evil-doers are led. / Knowing this, a person should perform merit and avoid sin: / through merit one attains godhood; through sin one goes to hell.

1.192.s:
yairmanāgapi deveśo manasā pūjito raviḥ ..
te kadāpi na paśyaṃti yamasya vadanaṃ khaga .. .. 1.192.30 ..
1.192.d:
यैर्मनागपि देवेशो मनसा पूजितो रविः ॥
ते कदापि न पश्यंति यमस्य वदनं खग ॥ ॥ 1.192.30 ॥
1.192.m: Those by whom Ravi, the lord of gods, has been worshipped with the mind even in the slightest, / never behold the face of Yama, O bird.

1.192.s:
kiṃ tu pāpairmahāghoraiḥ kiñcitkālaṃ tavājñayā ..
bhavaṃti pretarājānastato yāṃti raveḥ puram.. 31 ..
1.192.d:
किं तु पापैर्महाघोरैः किञ्चित्कालं तवाज्ञया ॥
भवंति प्रेतराजानस्ततो यांति रवेः पुरम्॥ 31 ॥
1.192.m: However, due to very dreadful sins, by your command, for a short time / they become king of pretas, and then they go to the city of Ravi.

1.192.s:
ye punaḥ sarvabhāvena bhajante bhuvi bhāska ram ..
na te limpaṃti pāpena padmapatramivāṃbhasā .. 32 ..
1.192.d:
ये पुनः सर्वभावेन भजन्ते भुवि भास्क रम् ॥
न ते लिम्पंति पापेन पद्मपत्रमिवांभसा ॥ 32 ॥
1.192.m: Moreover, those who revere the Sun on earth with all their heart / are not stained by sin, like a lotus leaf by water.

1.192.s:
tasmātprakuryādbhaktiṃ vai bhāskare satataṃ naraḥ ..
śraddhayā pūjayedbhānuṃ ya icchedvipulaṃ dhanam .. 33 ..
dantakāṣṭhavidhivarṇanam
1.192.d:
तस्मात्प्रकुर्याद्भक्तिं वै भास्करे सततं नरः ॥
श्रद्धया पूजयेद्भानुं य इच्छेद्विपुलं धनम् ॥ 33 ॥
दन्तकाष्ठविधिवर्णनम्
1.192.m:
Therefore, a person should always direct devotion to the Sun; / he who desires abundant wealth should worship the Sun with faith.
Description of the rules for the tooth-cleaning stick

1.193.s:
.. .. saptāśvatilaka uvāca .. ..
ayane viṣuve vāre saṃkrāṃtau grahaṇe tathā ..
pūjayetsatataṃ bhānuṃ saptamyāṃ tu viśeṣataḥ .. 1 ..
1.193.d:
॥ ॥ सप्ताश्वतिलक उवाच ॥ ॥
अयने विषुवे वारे संक्रांतौ ग्रहणे तथा ॥
पूजयेत्सततं भानुं सप्तम्यां तु विशेषतः ॥ 1 ॥
1.193.m: The Sun said: / At the solstices, equinoxes, on [the Sun's] day, at solar transits, and during eclipses, / one should worship the Sun constantly, but especially on the seventh lunar day.

1.193.s:
vainateya nibodha tvaṃ vidhānaṃ saptamīvrate ..
etaddhi paramaṃ guhyaṃ raverārādhanaṃ param .. 2 ..
1.193.d:
वैनतेय निबोध त्वं विधानं सप्तमीव्रते ॥
एतद्धि परमं गुह्यं रवेराराधनं परम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.193.m: Learn, O son of Vinatā, the procedure for the observance of the seventh lunar day; / for this is the supreme secret, the highest adoration of the Sun.

1.193.s:
siddhārthakaistu prathamā dvitīyā cārkasaṃpuṭaiḥ ..
tṛtīyā maricaiḥ kāryā caturthī tila saptamī .. 3 ..
1.193.d:
सिद्धार्थकैस्तु प्रथमा द्वितीया चार्कसंपुटैः ॥
तृतीया मरिचैः कार्या चतुर्थी तिल सप्तमी ॥ 3 ॥
1.193.m: The first is [done] with white mustard seeds, the second with calotropis buds; / the third should be performed with black pepper, and the fourth is the sesame seventh lunar day.

1.193.s:
saptamī caudanairvīra saptamī parikīrtitā ..
ityetāḥ sapta saptamyaḥ kartavyā bhūtimicchatā .. 4 ..
1.193.d:
सप्तमी चौदनैर्वीर सप्तमी परिकीर्तिता ॥
इत्येताः सप्त सप्तम्यः कर्तव्या भूतिमिच्छता ॥ 4 ॥
1.193.m: And the seventh is proclaimed as the seventh lunar day [performed] with cooked rice, O hero; / thus these seven seventh lunar days should be observed by one who desires prosperity.

1.193.s:
tathā cānukrame tāsāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ kathayā myaham ..
māghe vā mārgaśīrṣe vā kāryā śuklā tu saptamī .. 5 ..
1.193.d:
तथा चानुक्रमे तासां लक्षणं कथया म्यहम् ॥
माघे वा मार्गशीर्षे वा कार्या शुक्ला तु सप्तमी ॥ 5 ॥
1.193.m: And so I shall explain their characteristics in proper order: / the bright seventh lunar day should be observed either in the month of Māgha or Mārgaśīrṣa.

1.193.s:
ārtasya tu na niyamaḥ pakṣamāsakṛto bhavet ..
ardhapraharaśeṣe tu kuryādvai daṃtadhāva nam .. 6 ..
1.193.d:
आर्तस्य तु न नियमः पक्षमासकृतो भवेत् ॥
अर्धप्रहरशेषे तु कुर्याद्वै दंतधाव नम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.193.m: For a sick person, however, there is no restriction regarding the fortnight and month; / but when half a watch [of the night] remains, one should clean one's teeth.

1.193.s:
pañcamyāṃ tatra ye vṛkṣāḥ kāmitāstānvadāmyaham ..
madhūke putralābhaḥ syādduḥkhahā mārkavo bhavet .. 7 ..
1.193.d:
पञ्चम्यां तत्र ये वृक्षाः कामितास्तान्वदाम्यहम् ॥
मधूके पुत्रलाभः स्याद्दुःखहा मार्कवो भवेत् ॥ 7 ॥
1.193.m: I shall state the trees that are desired for that on the fifth lunar day: / with the madhūka there is the gain of a son; the bhṛṅgarāja removes distress.

1.193.s:
badaryā ca bṛhatyā ca kṣipraṃ rogātpramucyate ..
aiśvaryaṃ ca bhavedbilvaiḥ khadireṇa ca saṃcayaḥ .. 8 ..
1.193.d:
बदर्या च बृहत्या च क्षिप्रं रोगात्प्रमुच्यते ॥
ऐश्वर्यं च भवेद्बिल्वैः खदिरेण च संचयः ॥ 8 ॥
1.193.m: And with the jujube and the bṛhatī, one is quickly freed from disease; / with bilva there is sovereign power, and with the khadira, accumulation [of wealth].

1.193.s:
śatrukṣayaḥ kadaṃbeṣu arthalābhotimuktake ..
gurutāṃ yāti sarvatra āṭarūṣakasaṃbhavaiḥ .. 9 ..
1.193.d:
शत्रुक्षयः कदंबेषु अर्थलाभोतिमुक्तके ॥
गुरुतां याति सर्वत्र आटरूषकसंभवैः ॥ 9 ॥
1.193.m: Destruction of enemies occurs with the kadamba, gain of wealth with the atimuktaka; / one gains importance everywhere through twigs produced from the vāsaka.

1.193.s:
jñātipradhānatāṃ yāti aśvattho yacchate yaśaḥ ..
karavīrātparijñānamacalaṃ syānna saṃśayaḥ .. 1.193.10 ..
1.193.d:
ज्ञातिप्रधानतां याति अश्वत्थो यच्छते यशः ॥
करवीरात्परिज्ञानमचलं स्यान्न संशयः ॥ 1.193.10 ॥
1.193.m: One attains primacy among kinsmen; the sacred fig tree gives fame; / from the oleander there is unshakable knowledge, without a doubt.

1.193.s:
śriyaṃ prāpnoti vipulāṃ śirīṣasya nive śane ..
priyaṃguṃ sevyamānasya saubhāgyaṃ paramaṃ bhavet .. 11 ..
1.193.d:
श्रियं प्राप्नोति विपुलां शिरीषस्य निवे शने ॥
प्रियंगुं सेव्यमानस्य सौभाग्यं परमं भवेत् ॥ 11 ॥
1.193.m: One attains great fortune by using the siris; / for one who employs the priyaṅgu, there will be supreme good fortune.

1.193.s:
abhīpsitārthasiddhyarthaṃ sukhāsīnotha vāgyataḥ ..
kāmaṃ yatheṣṭahṛdaye kṛtvā samabhi maṃtrya ca ..
maṃtreṇānena matimānaśnīyāddantadhāvanam.. 12 ..
1.193.d:
अभीप्सितार्थसिद्ध्यर्थं सुखासीनोथ वाग्यतः ॥
कामं यथेष्टहृदये कृत्वा समभि मंत्र्य च ॥
मंत्रेणानेन मतिमानश्नीयाद्दन्तधावनम्॥ 12 ॥
1.193.m: To accomplish the desired end, sitting comfortably and restraining his speech, / placing his wish as desired in his heart and reciting the mantra over it, / the wise man should chew the tooth-cleaning stick with this mantra:

1.193.s:
varaṃ dattvābhijānāsi kāmadaṃ ca vanaspate ..
siddhiṃ prayaccha me nityaṃ daṃtakāṣṭha namo'stu te .. 13 ..
1.193.d:
वरं दत्त्वाभिजानासि कामदं च वनस्पते ॥
सिद्धिं प्रयच्छ मे नित्यं दंतकाष्ठ नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 13 ॥
1.193.m: "Granting a boon, you recognise [me], O lord of the forest, granting desires; / grant me success always, O tooth-cleaning stick, homage to you!"

1.193.s:
trīnvārānparijapyaivaṃ bhakṣayeddaṃtadhāvanam ..
paścātprakṣālya kāṣṭhaṃ tu śucau deśe vinikṣipet .. 14 ..
1.193.d:
त्रीन्वारान्परिजप्यैवं भक्षयेद्दंतधावनम् ॥
पश्चात्प्रक्षाल्य काष्ठं तु शुचौ देशे विनिक्षिपेत् ॥ 14 ॥
1.193.m: Having recited this three times, he should chew the tooth-cleaning stick; / afterwards, having washed the stick, he should cast it down in a clean place.

1.193.s:
ūrdhve nipatite siddhistathā cābhi mukhe sthite ..
atonyathā tu patite ānīya punarutsṛjet .. 15 ..
1.193.d:
ऊर्ध्वे निपतिते सिद्धिस्तथा चाभि मुखे स्थिते ॥
अतोन्यथा तु पतिते आनीय पुनरुत्सृजेत् ॥ 15 ॥
1.193.m: If it falls upright or facing towards [him], there is success; / if it falls otherwise, he should bring it back and cast it down again.

1.193.s:
parāṅmukhaṃ yadi bhavettrīnvārāndaṃtadhāvanam ..
asiddhāṃ tu vijānīyānna grāhyā sā tu saptamī .. 16 ..
1.193.d:
पराङ्मुखं यदि भवेत्त्रीन्वारान्दंतधावनम् ॥
असिद्धां तु विजानीयान्न ग्राह्या सा तु सप्तमी ॥ 16 ॥
1.193.m: If the tooth-cleaning stick faces away three times, / one should know that it is unsuccessful, and that seventh lunar day should not be undertaken.

1.193.s:
brahmacārī tu tāṃ rātriṃ svapyānmaṃgalasevayā ..
bibhradvāsonupahataṃ śucirācārasaṃyutaḥ .. 17 ..
1.193.d:
ब्रह्मचारी तु तां रात्रिं स्वप्यान्मंगलसेवया ॥
बिभ्रद्वासोनुपहतं शुचिराचारसंयुतः ॥ 17 ॥
1.193.m: Remaining celibate, he should sleep that night by attending to auspicious rites, / wearing an unsoiled garment, pure, and endowed with proper conduct.

1.193.s:
tasyāṃ rātryāṃ vyatītāyāṃ prāta rutthāya vai khaga ..
prakṣālayenmukhaṃ dhīmānaśnīyāddantadhāvanam .. 18 ..
1.193.d:
तस्यां रात्र्यां व्यतीतायां प्रात रुत्थाय वै खग ॥
प्रक्षालयेन्मुखं धीमानश्नीयाद्दन्तधावनम् ॥ 18 ॥
1.193.m: When that night has passed, having risen in the morning, O bird, / the wise man should wash his face and chew the tooth-cleaning stick.

1.193.s:
upaviśya śucirbhūtvā praṇamya śirasā ravim ..
japaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ kṛtvā tu juhuyācca hutāśane .. 19 ..
1.193.d:
उपविश्य शुचिर्भूत्वा प्रणम्य शिरसा रविम् ॥
जपं यथेष्टं कृत्वा तु जुहुयाच्च हुताशने ॥ 19 ॥
1.193.m: Sitting down, being purified, and bowing his head to the Sun, / having recited his prayers as desired, he should make offerings into the sacrificial fire.

1.193.s:
tatoparāhnasamaye snātvā mṛdgomayāṃbubhiḥ ..
vidhivanniyamaṃ kṛtvā maunī śuklāṃbaraḥ śuciḥ .. 1.193.20 ..
1.193.d:
ततोपराह्नसमये स्नात्वा मृद्गोमयांबुभिः ॥
विधिवन्नियमं कृत्वा मौनी शुक्लांबरः शुचिः ॥ 1.193.20 ॥
1.193.m: Then, at the time of the afternoon, having bathed with clay, cow dung, and water, / having undertaken the vow in accordance with rule, maintaining silence, dressed in white, pure,

1.193.s:
pūjayitvā vidhiṃ bhaktyā devadevaṃ divākaram ..
svapyāddevasya purato gāyatrījapatatparaḥ .. 21 ..
sūryāruṇasaṃvāde svapnavarṇanam
1.193.d:
पूजयित्वा विधिं भक्त्या देवदेवं दिवाकरम् ॥
स्वप्याद्देवस्य पुरतो गायत्रीजपतत्परः ॥ 21 ॥
सूर्यारुणसंवादे स्वप्नवर्णनम्
1.193.m:
and having worshipped according to the rite with devotion the god of gods, the Day-maker, / he should sleep in front of the god, intent on reciting the Gāyatrī.
Description of dreams in the dialogue between the Sun and Aruṇa

1.194.s:
.. saptāśvatilaka uvāca .. ..
ataḥ paraṃ pravakṣyāmi yairyairya tphalamaśnute ..
svapne dṛṣṭe tu saptamyāṃ puruṣo niyatavrataḥ .. 1 ..
1.194.d:
॥ सप्ताश्वतिलक उवाच ॥ ॥
अतः परं प्रवक्ष्यामि यैर्यैर्य त्फलमश्नुते ॥
स्वप्ने दृष्टे तु सप्तम्यां पुरुषो नियतव्रतः ॥ 1 ॥
1.194.m: The Sun said: / Hereafter I shall explain the fruits that a man who maintains the observance / obtains through various dreams seen on the seventh lunar day.

1.194.s:
samāpya vidhivatsarvāṃ japahomādikāṃ kriyām ..
bhūmau śayyāṃ samāsthāya devadevaṃ vicintayet .. 2 ..
1.194.d:
समाप्य विधिवत्सर्वां जपहोमादिकां क्रियाम् ॥
भूमौ शय्यां समास्थाय देवदेवं विचिन्तयेत् ॥ 2 ॥
1.194.m: Having completed according to rule all rites such as recitation and fire offerings, / lying down on a bed upon the ground, he should meditate on the god of gods.

1.194.s:
hanta supto yadi naraḥ paśyetsvapne divākaram ..
śakradhvajaṃ vā candraṃ vā tasya sarvāḥ samṛddhayaḥ .. 3 ..
1.194.d:
हन्त सुप्तो यदि नरः पश्येत्स्वप्ने दिवाकरम् ॥
शक्रध्वजं वा चन्द्रं वा तस्य सर्वाः समृद्धयः ॥ 3 ॥
1.194.m: Behold: if a sleeping man sees in a dream the Sun, / or Indra's banner, or the Moon, all forms of prosperity belong to him.

1.194.s:
bhṛṃgāracamarādarśakanakābharaṇāni ca ..
rudhirasya srutiḥ keśapātaṃ aiśvaryakārakaḥ ..
svapne vṛkṣādhirohe tu kṣipramaiśvaryamāhave .. 4 ..
1.194.d:
भृंगारचमरादर्शकनकाभरणानि च ॥
रुधिरस्य स्रुतिः केशपातं ऐश्वर्यकारकः ॥
स्वप्ने वृक्षाधिरोहे तु क्षिप्रमैश्वर्यमाहवे ॥ 4 ॥
1.194.m: A golden pitcher, chowries, a mirror, and gold ornaments, / the flowing of blood, and the falling of hair bring sovereign power; / climbing a tree in a dream brings swift sovereign power in battle.

1.194.s:
dohanaṃ mahiṣīsiṃhīgodhenūnāṃ kare svake ..
bandhaścāsāṃ rājyalābho nābheḥ sparśe tu durmatiḥ .. 5 ..
1.194.d:
दोहनं महिषीसिंहीगोधेनूनां करे स्वके ॥
बन्धश्चासां राज्यलाभो नाभेः स्पर्शे तु दुर्मतिः ॥ 5 ॥
1.194.m: Milking female buffaloes, lionesses, and cows with one's own hand, / and tethering them, brings the gain of a kingdom; but touching the navel, the foolish-minded [loses it].

1.194.s:
aviṃ hatvā svayaṃ khādetsiṃhamaṃbujameva ca ..
svāṃgamasthi hutāśaṃ ca surāpānaṃ khagādhipa .. 6 ..
1.194.d:
अविं हत्वा स्वयं खादेत्सिंहमंबुजमेव च ॥
स्वांगमस्थि हुताशं च सुरापानं खगाधिप ॥ 6 ॥
1.194.m: Having killed a sheep, if one eats it oneself, or [eats] a lion, or a lotus, / or one's own limbs, bones, or fire, or drinks wine, O lord of birds,

1.194.s:
haime vā rājate vāpi yo bhuṃkte pāyasaṃ naraḥ ..
pātre tu padmapatre vā tasyaiśvaryaṃ samaṃ bhavet .. .. 7 ..
1.194.d:
हैमे वा राजते वापि यो भुंक्ते पायसं नरः ॥
पात्रे तु पद्मपत्रे वा तस्यैश्वर्यं समं भवेत् ॥ ॥ 7 ॥
1.194.m: or the man who eats rice boiled in milk from a golden or silver / vessel or from a lotus leaf, his sovereign power becomes boundless.

1.194.s:
dyūte ca vātha vā yuddhe vijayo hi sukhāvahaḥ ..
gātrasya svasya jvalanaṃ śirobandhaśca bhūtaye .. 8 ..
1.194.d:
द्यूते च वाथ वा युद्धे विजयो हि सुखावहः ॥
गात्रस्य स्वस्य ज्वलनं शिरोबन्धश्च भूतये ॥ 8 ॥
1.194.m: Victory in gambling or in battle brings happiness; / the burning of one's own body and the binding of a turban bring prosperity.

1.194.s:
mālyāṃbarāṇāṃ śuklānāṃ hayānāṃ paśupakṣiṇām ..
sadā lābhaṃ praśaṃsaṃti viṣṭhānāṃ cānulepanam .. 9 ..
1.194.d:
माल्यांबराणां शुक्लानां हयानां पशुपक्षिणाम् ॥
सदा लाभं प्रशंसंति विष्ठानां चानुलेपनम् ॥ 9 ॥
1.194.m: The acquisition of white garlands and white garments, of horses, beasts, and birds, / and the smearing of excrement are always praised.

1.194.s:
hayayāne bhavetkṣipraṃ rathayāne prajāgamaḥ ..
nānāśirobāhutā ca gṛhasthāṃ kurute śriyam .. 1.194.10 ..
1.194.d:
हययाने भवेत्क्षिप्रं रथयाने प्रजागमः ॥
नानाशिरोबाहुता च गृहस्थां कुरुते श्रियम् ॥ 1.194.10 ॥
1.194.m: Travelling by horse brings swift [success], and travelling by chariot brings offspring; / having multiple heads and arms produces wealth that stays in the house.

1.194.s:
agamyāgamanaṃ dhanyaṃ vedādhyayanamuttamam ..
devadvijaśreṣṭhavīraguruvṛddhatapasvinaḥ .. 11 ..
1.194.d:
अगम्यागमनं धन्यं वेदाध्ययनमुत्तमम् ॥
देवद्विजश्रेष्ठवीरगुरुवृद्धतपस्विनः ॥ 11 ॥
1.194.m: Intercourse with an forbidden woman is auspicious; Vedic study is excellent; / whatever the gods, best of the twice-born, heroes, teachers, elders, and ascetics

1.194.s:
yadvadaṃti naraṃ svapne satyameveti tadviduḥ ..
praśastaṃ darśanaṃ caiṣāmāśīrvādaḥ khagādhipa .. 12 ..
1.194.d:
यद्वदंति नरं स्वप्ने सत्यमेवेति तद्विदुः ॥
प्रशस्तं दर्शनं चैषामाशीर्वादः खगाधिप ॥ 12 ॥
1.194.m: tell a man in a dream, they know to be truly so; / and the sight of them and their blessing are praised, O lord of birds.

1.194.s:
rājyaṃ syātsvaśiraśchede dhanaṃ bahuvadhe bhavet ..
rudite bhakṣyasaṃprāptī rājyaṃ nigaḍabandhane..13..
1.194.d:
राज्यं स्यात्स्वशिरश्छेदे धनं बहुवधे भवेत् ॥
रुदिते भक्ष्यसंप्राप्ती राज्यं निगडबन्धने॥13॥
1.194.m: There is sovereignty if one's own head is cut off; wealth comes from slaughtering many; / in weeping there is the attainment of food; and there is a kingdom in being bound in iron chains.

1.194.s:
parvataṃ turagaṃ siṃhaṃ vṛṣabhaṃ gajameva hi ..
mahadaiśvaryamāpnoti yo vikramyādhirohati .. 14 ..
1.194.d:
पर्वतं तुरगं सिंहं वृषभं गजमेव हि ॥
महदैश्वर्यमाप्नोति यो विक्रम्याधिरोहति ॥ 14 ॥
1.194.m: He who advances boldly and mounts a mountain, / a horse, a lion, a bull, or an elephant attains great sovereign power.

1.194.s:
āgṛhṇāno grahāṃstārā marīciṃ parivartayan ..
unmūlayati parvatāṃśca rājā bhavati bhūtale .. 15 ..
1.194.d:
आगृह्णानो ग्रहांस्तारा मरीचिं परिवर्तयन् ॥
उन्मूलयति पर्वतांश्च राजा भवति भूतले ॥ 15 ॥
1.194.m: Seizing the planets, turning the rays of the stars, / and uprooting mountains, one becomes a king upon the earth.

1.194.s:
dehānniṣkāṃtiraṃtrāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ ca khagādhipa ..
pānaṃ samudrasaritāmaiśvaryasukhakārakam .. 16 ....
1.194.d:
देहान्निष्कांतिरंत्राणां सर्वेषां च खगाधिप ॥
पानं समुद्रसरितामैश्वर्यसुखकारकम् ॥ 16 ॥॥
1.194.m: The emergence of all one's entrails from the body, O lord of birds, / and drinking the oceans and rivers produce sovereign power and happiness.

1.194.s:
balaṃ cāṃbunidhiṃ vāpi tīrthapāraṃ prayāti yaḥ ..
tasyāpatyaṃ bhavedvīra acalaṃ ca khagādhipa .. 17 ..
1.194.d:
बलं चांबुनिधिं वापि तीर्थपारं प्रयाति यः ॥
तस्यापत्यं भवेद्वीर अचलं च खगाधिप ॥ 17 ॥
1.194.m: And he who reaches the other shore of an army, an ocean, or a sacred ford, / his lineage shall be enduring, O hero, O lord of birds.

1.194.s:
bhavatyarthāgamaḥ śīghraṃ kṛmirvā yadi bhakṣayet ...
aṃgānāṃ ca surūpāṇāṃ lābho darśanameva ca ..
saṃyogaścaiva māṃgalyairārogyaṃ dhanameva ca .. 18 ..
1.194.d:
भवत्यर्थागमः शीघ्रं कृमिर्वा यदि भक्षयेत् ॥।
अंगानां च सुरूपाणां लाभो दर्शनमेव च ॥
संयोगश्चैव मांगल्यैरारोग्यं धनमेव च ॥ 18 ॥
1.194.m:
or if a worm should devour [one], quick acquisition of wealth occurs.
And there is the gain and seeing of beautiful limbs,
and union with auspicious things, health, and wealth.

1.194.s:
aiśvaryaṃ rājyalābhaśca yasminsvapna udāhṛtaḥ ..
sapta syānnātra saṃdehaścaturbhiḥ śruta uttamaḥ .. 19 ..
1.194.d:
ऐश्वर्यं राज्यलाभश्च यस्मिन्स्वप्न उदाहृतः ॥
सप्त स्यान्नात्र संदेहश्चतुर्भिः श्रुत उत्तमः ॥ 19 ॥
1.194.m:
Sovereignty and the attainment of a kingdom [ensue] when [such] a dream is declared.
It would surely be seven [results], without doubt; one who hears with four [dreams] is excellent.

1.194.s:
paṃcabhiḥ putrabāhulyaṃ ṣaḍbhirāyuḥ sutāndhanam ..
saptabhirvividhānkāmānaṣṭabhirvividhaṃ yaśaḥ .. .. 1.194.20 ..
iti śrībhaviṣye mahāpurāṇe brāhme parvaṇi saptamīkalpe sūryāruṇasaṃvāde svapnavarṇanaṃ nāma caturnavatyadhikaśatatamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 194 ...5 ..
sūryāruṇasaṃvāde svapnavarṇanam
1.194.d:
पंचभिः पुत्रबाहुल्यं षड्भिरायुः सुतान्धनम् ॥
सप्तभिर्विविधान्कामानष्टभिर्विविधं यशः ॥ ॥ 1.194.20 ॥
इति श्रीभविष्ये महापुराणे ब्राह्मे पर्वणि सप्तमीकल्पे सूर्यारुणसंवादे स्वप्नवर्णनं नाम चतुर्नवत्यधिकशततमोऽध्यायः ॥ 194 ॥.5 ॥
सूर्यारुणसंवादे स्वप्नवर्णनम्
1.194.m:
With five, an abundance of sons; with six, longevity, sons, and wealth;
with seven, various desires; with eight, various kinds of renown.
Thus ends the one hundred and ninety-fourth chapter, entitled 'Description of Dreams', in the dialogue between Sūrya and Aruṇa, in the Saptamī Kalpa, in the Brāhma Book of the glorious Bhaviṣya Mahāpurāṇa.
Description of Dreams in the Dialogue between Sūrya and Aruṇa

1.195.s:
.. .. anūruruvāca .. ..
bhagavañchrotumicchāmi saptamīnāṃ paraṃ vidhim ..
sarvāsāmanurūpāṇāṃ kathayasva mahāmune .. 1 ..
1.195.d:
॥ ॥ अनूरुरुवाच ॥ ॥
भगवञ्छ्रोतुमिच्छामि सप्तमीनां परं विधिम् ॥
सर्वासामनुरूपाणां कथयस्व महामुने ॥ 1 ॥
1.195.m:
Anūru said:
O venerable one, I wish to hear the supreme rule of the saptamīs.
O great sage, tell [me] of all of them according to their suitability.

1.195.s:
.. saptāśvatilaka uvāca .. ..
śṛṇu vīra khagaśreṣṭha saptamīnāṃ paraṃ vidhim ..
kīrtayiṣyāmi te sarvaṃ yathāvatparipṛcchate .. 2 ..
1.195.d:
॥ सप्ताश्वतिलक उवाच ॥ ॥
शृणु वीर खगश्रेष्ठ सप्तमीनां परं विधिम् ॥
कीर्तयिष्यामि ते सर्वं यथावत्परिपृच्छते ॥ 2 ॥

1.195.s:
tulyaṃ kila khagaśreṣṭha yathākhyātaṃ vivasvatā ..
śuklapakṣe ravidine pravṛtte cottarāyaṇe .. 3 ..
1.195.d:
तुल्यं किल खगश्रेष्ठ यथाख्यातं विवस्वता ॥
शुक्लपक्षे रविदिने प्रवृत्ते चोत्तरायणे ॥ 3 ॥
1.195.m:
It is equal, O best of birds, to what was indeed spoken by Vivasvat,
in the bright fortnight on a Sunday, when the northward course of the sun has begun.

1.195.s:
putradāradhanakṣetre gṛhṇīyātsaptamīvratam ..
ṛṣibhirjñānasaṃpannaiḥ sarvakāmaphala pradaiḥ .. 4 ..
1.195.d:
पुत्रदारधनक्षेत्रे गृह्णीयात्सप्तमीव्रतम् ॥
ऋषिभिर्ज्ञानसंपन्नैः सर्वकामफल प्रदैः ॥ 4 ॥
1.195.m:
In [the presence of] sons, wife, wealth, and field, one should undertake the saptamī votive observance,
[taught] by the ṛṣis endowed with knowledge, bestowers of the fruits of all desires.

1.195.s:
saptamyaḥ saptaākhyātāstāsāṃ nāmāni me śṛṇu ..
arkasaṃpuṭakairekā dvitīyā maricaistathā .. 5 ..
1.195.d:
सप्तम्यः सप्तआख्यातास्तासां नामानि मे शृणु ॥
अर्कसंपुटकैरेका द्वितीया मरिचैस्तथा ॥ 5 ॥
1.195.m:
Seven saptamīs are declared; hear their names from me:
one with calotropis leaf-cups, and the second with black peppercorns,

1.195.s:
tṛtīyā niṃbapatraiśca caturthī phala saptamī ..
saptamī kāmikā nāmnā vidhimāsāṃ nibodha me .. 6 ..
1.195.d:
तृतीया निंबपत्रैश्च चतुर्थी फल सप्तमी ॥
सप्तमी कामिका नाम्ना विधिमासां निबोध मे ॥ 6 ॥
1.195.m:
the third with neem leaves, and the fourth is the fruit-saptamī,
[the fifth] named Kāmikā saptamī. Understand their procedure from me.

1.195.s:
paṃcamyāmekabhaktaṃ tu kuryānniyatamānasaḥ ..
alpāhāraṃ na kurvīta maithunaṃ dūratastyaje t .. 7 ..
1.195.d:
पंचम्यामेकभक्तं तु कुर्यान्नियतमानसः ॥
अल्पाहारं न कुर्वीत मैथुनं दूरतस्त्यजे त् ॥ 7 ॥
1.195.m:
On the pañcamī, with a restrained mind, one should take only a single meal;
one should not consume slight food, [and] should abandon sexual intercourse from afar.

1.195.s:
varjayenmadhu māṃsaṃ ca atyamlaṃ ca khagādhipa ..
prabhāte caiva ṣaṣṭhyāṃ tu ekaikaparṇasaṃpuṭe .. 8 ..
1.195.d:
वर्जयेन्मधु मांसं च अत्यम्लं च खगाधिप ॥
प्रभाते चैव षष्ठ्यां तु एकैकपर्णसंपुटे ॥ 8 ॥
1.195.m:
One should avoid honey, meat, and what is overly sour, O lord of birds.
And at dawn on the ṣaṣṭhī, in a single leaf-cup,

1.195.s:
ghṛtaśālyodanaṃ kṛtvā bhakṣayettu vidhānataḥ ..
anyadannamabhuṃjānaḥ saptamyāṃ bhojanaṃ bhavet .. 9 ..
1.195.d:
घृतशाल्योदनं कृत्वा भक्षयेत्तु विधानतः ॥
अन्यदन्नमभुंजानः सप्तम्यां भोजनं भवेत् ॥ 9 ॥
1.195.m:
having placed boiled rice made of śāli grain with clarified butter, one should eat it according to the injunction,
not consuming any other food; on the saptamī there should be a meal.

1.195.s:
ekaikavṛddhābhiyuktairyo vasettu khageśvara ..
anyatra maricaṃ bhakṣenniṃbapatrāṇyataḥ param .. 1.195.10 ..
1.195.d:
एकैकवृद्धाभियुक्तैर्यो वसेत्तु खगेश्वर ॥
अन्यत्र मरिचं भक्षेन्निंबपत्राण्यतः परम् ॥ 1.195.10 ॥
1.195.m:
O lord of birds, he who dwells with [portions] increased one by one—
elsewhere he should eat pepper, and after that neem leaves.

1.195.s:
evaṃ labdhaphalānīha pakṣayorubhayorapi..
annādai rahito yatnādanodana iti smṛtaḥ .. 11 ..
1.195.d:
एवं लब्धफलानीह पक्षयोरुभयोरपि॥
अन्नादै रहितो यत्नादनोदन इति स्मृतः ॥ 11 ॥
1.195.m:
Thus their fruits are obtained here in both fortnights.
Free from solid foods with effort, he is called 'non-rice-eater'.

1.195.s:
ācaredvidhivadbhaktyā pūjayitvā vibhāvasum ..
ahorātraṃ vāyubhakṣaḥ kuryādvijayasaptamīm .. 12 ..
1.195.d:
आचरेद्विधिवद्भक्त्या पूजयित्वा विभावसुम् ॥
अहोरात्रं वायुभक्षः कुर्याद्विजयसप्तमीम् ॥ 12 ॥
1.195.m:
One should observe [it] properly with devotion, having worshipped the fire.
Subsisting on air day and night, one should perform the Vijayasaptamī.

1.195.s:
ekaikaṃ sapta saptamīratraiva vidhivaccaret ..
prālekhya tāsāṃ nāmāni patrakeṣu pṛthakpṛthak .. 13 ..
1.195.d:
एकैकं सप्त सप्तमीरत्रैव विधिवच्चरेत् ॥
प्रालेख्य तासां नामानि पत्रकेषु पृथक्पृथक् ॥ 13 ॥
1.195.m:
One by one, one should observe the seven saptamīs here according to rule,
having written their names individually on leaves.

1.195.s:
tāni sarvāṇi nāmāni vilekhya susamāhitaḥ ..
śvetacaṃdanadigdhāṃge mālyadāmopaśobhite .. 14 ..
saptadhānyahiraṇyāḍhye śaśikundeṃdusannibhe.13 ..
1.195.d:
तानि सर्वाणि नामानि विलेख्य सुसमाहितः ॥
श्वेतचंदनदिग्धांगे माल्यदामोपशोभिते ॥ 14 ॥
सप्तधान्यहिरण्याढ्ये शशिकुन्देंदुसन्निभे.13 ॥
1.195.m:
Having inscribed all those names, well-composed in mind,
[upon a cloth/altar] smeared with white sandalwood, adorned with garlands of flowers,
rich in seven kinds of grains and gold, resembling the moon, jasmine, and the moon,

1.195.s: aśvatthāśokapatrāḍhye dadhyodanasamanvite .. 15 ..
1.195.d: अश्वत्थाशोकपत्राढ्ये दध्योदनसमन्विते ॥ 15 ॥
1.195.m: rich in leaves of sacred fig and aśoka, provided with curd-rice;

1.195.s:
tadarthaṃ pūjayedbhaktyā taistairdṛṣṭairna saṃśayaḥ ..
dṛṣṭvā tu śobhanaṃ svapnaṃ na bhūyaḥ śayanaṃ svapet..16..
1.195.d:
तदर्थं पूजयेद्भक्त्या तैस्तैर्दृष्टैर्न संशयः ॥
दृष्ट्वा तु शोभनं स्वप्नं न भूयः शयनं स्वपेत्॥16॥
1.195.m:
for that purpose one should worship with devotion by seeing each of those, without doubt.
And having seen an auspicious dream, one must not sleep again on a bed.

1.195.s:
prātaśca kī rtayetsvapne yathādṛṣṭaṃ khagādhipa ..
prājñabhojakaviprebhyaḥ suhṛdbhyaśca khagādhipa .. 17 ..
1.195.d:
प्रातश्च की र्तयेत्स्वप्ने यथादृष्टं खगाधिप ॥
प्राज्ञभोजकविप्रेभ्यः सुहृद्भ्यश्च खगाधिप ॥ 17 ॥
1.195.m:
And in the morning, O lord of birds, one should recount the dream as seen,
O lord of birds, to wise Bhojaka brāhmaṇas and friends.

1.195.s:
tato madhyāhnasamaye snātaḥ prayatamānasaḥ ..
taṃ caiva devaṃ vidhivatpūjayitvā divākaram .. 18 ..
1.195.d:
ततो मध्याह्नसमये स्नातः प्रयतमानसः ॥
तं चैव देवं विधिवत्पूजयित्वा दिवाकरम् ॥ 18 ॥
1.195.m:
Then at midday, bathed and with a subdued mind,
and having worshipped that god, the Sun, according to the rule,

1.195.s:
samyakkṛtajapo maunī naro hutahutāśanaḥ ..
niṣkramya devāyatanādbhojakāya nivedayet .. 19 ..
1.195.d:
सम्यक्कृतजपो मौनी नरो हुतहुताशनः ॥
निष्क्रम्य देवायतनाद्भोजकाय निवेदयेत् ॥ 19 ॥
1.195.m:
a man who has properly performed japa, is silent, and has offered into the sacred fire,
having stepped out from the temple, should present [it] to a Bhojaka.

1.195.s:
bhavedalābho yadi bhojakānāṃ viprāstamarhaṃti purāṇavijñāḥ ..
ye maṃtravedāvayaveṣu niścitā vibhuṃ samabhyarcya divaṃ vrajeyuḥ .. 1.195.20 ..
1.195.d:
भवेदलाभो यदि भोजकानां विप्रास्तमर्हंति पुराणविज्ञाः ॥
ये मंत्रवेदावयवेषु निश्चिता विभुं समभ्यर्च्य दिवं व्रजेयुः ॥ 1.195.20 ॥
1.195.m:
If there should be an absence of Bhojakas, brāhmaṇas knowing the Purāṇas are worthy of it,
who, resolute in the limbs of the mantras and Vedas, having worshipped the Lord, would go to heaven.

1.195.s:
kṛtvaivaṃ saptamī sapta naro bhakti samanvitaḥ ..
śraddadhānopi sūryasya sa kathaṃ nāpnuyātphalam ..21..
1.195.d:
कृत्वैवं सप्तमी सप्त नरो भक्ति समन्वितः ॥
श्रद्दधानोपि सूर्यस्य स कथं नाप्नुयात्फलम् ॥21॥
1.195.m:
Having observed the seven saptamīs thus, how could that man, endowed with devotion
and faith toward the Sun, not obtain the fruit?

1.195.s:
daśānāmaśvamedhānāṃ kṛtānāṃ yatphalaṃ bhavet ..
tatphalaṃ saptamī sapta kṛtvā bhaktyā labheta nā .. 22 ..
1.195.d:
दशानामश्वमेधानां कृतानां यत्फलं भवेत् ॥
तत्फलं सप्तमी सप्त कृत्वा भक्त्या लभेत ना ॥ 22 ॥
1.195.m:
Whatever fruit there may be from ten horse-sacrifices performed,
a man obtains that fruit by observing the seven saptamīs with devotion.

1.195.s:
duṣpāpaṃ nāsti tadvīra saptamyāṃ yanna dahyate ..
na ca rogo'styasau loke ya etābhirna śāmyati .. 23 ..
1.195.d:
दुष्पापं नास्ति तद्वीर सप्तम्यां यन्न दह्यते ॥
न च रोगोऽस्त्यसौ लोके य एताभिर्न शाम्यति ॥ 23 ॥
1.195.m:
There is no difficult sin, O hero, that is not burned on the saptamī,
nor is there that disease in the world which is not appeased by these.

1.195.s:
kuṣṭhāni yāni raudrāṇi duśchedyāni bhiṣagjanaiḥ ..
nīyante tāni sarvāṇi garuḍeneva pannagāḥ .. 24 ..
1.195.d:
कुष्ठानि यानि रौद्राणि दुश्छेद्यानि भिषग्जनैः ॥
नीयन्ते तानि सर्वाणि गरुडेनेव पन्नगाः ॥ 24 ॥
1.195.m:
Those terrible leprosies which are difficult to cure by physicians
are all removed, just as serpents by Garuḍa.

1.195.s:
sakalavibudhamānyaṃ svaprakāśaṃ janānāmabhimataphaladāne dīkṣitaṃ taṃ supūjyam ..
sutadhanakulabhogaiḥ saukhyapuṇyairupeto vrajati ca sutanuṃ kāṃ śāśvatā tigmaraśmeḥ .. 25 .. ..
nāmapūjāvidhivarṇanam
1.195.d:
सकलविबुधमान्यं स्वप्रकाशं जनानामभिमतफलदाने दीक्षितं तं सुपूज्यम् ॥
सुतधनकुलभोगैः सौख्यपुण्यैरुपेतो व्रजति च सुतनुं कां शाश्वता तिग्मरश्मेः ॥ 25 ॥ ॥
नामपूजाविधिवर्णनम्
1.195.m:
Honoured by all the gods, self-luminous, consecrated in granting the desired fruit of people, highly adorable—
endowed with sons, wealth, family, pleasures, happiness, and merits, he attains the eternal, fair body of the Hot-Rayed One.
Description of the Rule for the Worship of Names

1.196.s:
..saptāśvavatilaka uvāca.. ..
atītya bhuktaṃ puruṣaḥ saptamyāṃ garuḍāgraja ..
maitrīṃ vidadhyātsarvatra jīvahiṃsāṃ vivarjayet .. 1 ..
1.196.d:
॥सप्ताश्ववतिलक उवाच॥ ॥
अतीत्य भुक्तं पुरुषः सप्तम्यां गरुडाग्रज ॥
मैत्रीं विदध्यात्सर्वत्र जीवहिंसां विवर्जयेत् ॥ 1 ॥
1.196.m:
Saptāśvavatilaka said:
Having finished eating on the saptamī, O elder brother of Garuḍa, a person
should establish friendliness toward all and avoid injury to living beings.

1.196.s:
saptamyāṃ na spṛśettailaṃ nīlaṃ vastraṃ na dhārayet ..
na śayīta striyā sārdhaṃ na seveta durodaram .. 2 ..
1.196.d:
सप्तम्यां न स्पृशेत्तैलं नीलं वस्त्रं न धारयेत् ॥
न शयीत स्त्रिया सार्धं न सेवेत दुरोदरम् ॥ 2 ॥
1.196.m:
On the saptamī, one should not touch oil, nor wear blue clothing;
one should not lie with a woman, nor resort to gambling.

1.196.s:
na rudyādaśrupātena na vā dhyāyetpiśācakān ..
nākṛṣecchiraso yūkā na vṛthāvādamācaret ..
parasyāniṣṭakathanamativādaṃ ca varjayet .. 3 ..
1.196.d:
न रुद्यादश्रुपातेन न वा ध्यायेत्पिशाचकान् ॥
नाकृषेच्छिरसो यूका न वृथावादमाचरेत् ॥
परस्यानिष्टकथनमतिवादं च वर्जयेत् ॥ 3 ॥

1.196.s:
na kaṃcittāḍayejjaṃtuṃ na viśeta kadācana ..
brahmahatyāmavāpnoti viśamāno ravergṛham .. 4 ..
1.196.d:
न कंचित्ताडयेज्जंतुं न विशेत कदाचन ॥
ब्रह्महत्यामवाप्नोति विशमानो रवेर्गृहम् ॥ 4 ॥
1.196.m:
One should not strike any creature; [defiled,] one should never enter [the temple];
entering the house of the Sun [in impurity], one incurs the murder of a brāhmaṇa.

1.196.s:
ityete samayāḥ proktāḥ saurāṇāṃ garuḍāgraja ..
bhojakānāṃ viśeṣeṇa purā me bhānunānagha .. 5 ..
1.196.d:
इत्येते समयाः प्रोक्ताः सौराणां गरुडाग्रज ॥
भोजकानां विशेषेण पुरा मे भानुनानघ ॥ 5 ॥
1.196.m:
Thus these observances of the Sauras were spoken of, O elder brother of Garuḍa,
especially for Bhojakas, formerly to me by the Sun, O sinless one.

1.196.s:
bhojakaḥ khagaśārdūla yo lobhāddravyamutsṛjet ..
vṛddhyai tu satataṃ vīra sa gacchennarakaṃ dhuvam .. 6 ..
1.196.d:
भोजकः खगशार्दूल यो लोभाद्द्रव्यमुत्सृजेत् ॥
वृद्ध्यै तु सततं वीर स गच्छेन्नरकं धुवम् ॥ 6 ॥
1.196.m:
A Bhojaka, O tiger among birds, who out of greed lends out wealth
continually for interest, O hero, he would surely go to hell.

1.196.s:
viśeṣe cālpakaśate kāmayāne khagādhipa ..
prayujyamāno bhojakastu paṃcakena śatena vai .. 7 ..
1.196.d:
विशेषे चाल्पकशते कामयाने खगाधिप ॥
प्रयुज्यमानो भोजकस्तु पंचकेन शतेन वै ॥ 7 ॥
1.196.m:
Especially when desiring [interest] on a small hundred, O lord of birds,
a Bhojaka who lends at five percent [per month],

1.196.s:
prāyaścittī bhavedvīra na cārhaḥ pūjane raveḥ..
kṛtvā sāṃtapanaṃ kṛcchraṃ tatraḥ saṃpūjayedravim .. 8 ..
1.196.d:
प्रायश्चित्ती भवेद्वीर न चार्हः पूजने रवेः॥
कृत्वा सांतपनं कृच्छ्रं तत्रः संपूजयेद्रविम् ॥ 8 ॥
1.196.m:
becomes one who requires expiation, O hero, and is unworthy to worship the Sun.
Having performed the sāṃtapana penance, he may then worship the Sun.

1.196.s:
nānyadevapratiṣṭhā tu kartavyā bhojakena tu ..
kṛtvā tu tāṃ khagaśreṣṭha prāyaścittīyate naraḥ .. 9 ..
1.196.d:
नान्यदेवप्रतिष्ठा तु कर्तव्या भोजकेन तु ॥
कृत्वा तु तां खगश्रेष्ठ प्रायश्चित्तीयते नरः ॥ 9 ॥
1.196.m:
No consecration of any other deity must be performed by a Bhojaka;
by performing that, O best of birds, a man becomes in need of expiation.

1.196.s:
tasmāttu tāṃ na kuryādvai bhojakaḥ khagasattama ..
muktvā tu bhāskaraṃ devaṃ nānyaṃ devaṃ nivedayet .. 10 ..
1.196.d:
तस्मात्तु तां न कुर्याद्वै भोजकः खगसत्तम ॥
मुक्त्वा तु भास्करं देवं नान्यं देवं निवेदयेत् ॥ 10 ॥
1.196.m:
Therefore, a Bhojaka should not perform it, O excellent among birds;
leaving aside the god Bhāskara, he should offer to no other god.

1.196.s:
kṛtvādhiveśaṃ devānāṃ brahmādīnāṃ khagādhipa ..
bhojako na spṛśedbhānuṃ kuryātkṛcchraṃ ca śuddhaye .. 11 ..
1.196.d:
कृत्वाधिवेशं देवानां ब्रह्मादीनां खगाधिप ॥
भोजको न स्पृशेद्भानुं कुर्यात्कृच्छ्रं च शुद्धये ॥ 11 ॥
1.196.m: Having performed the installation of deities such as Brahmā and the others, O lord of birds, / a Bhojaka should not touch the sun and should perform a kṛcchra penance for purification.

1.196.s:
kṛtvā tu kṛcchraṃ vidhi vacchuddherhetuṃ khagādhipa ..
tataḥ pūjayituṃ bhānumadhikārī bhavennaraḥ .. 12 ..
1.196.d:
कृत्वा तु कृच्छ्रं विधि वच्छुद्धेर्हेतुं खगाधिप ॥
ततः पूजयितुं भानुमधिकारी भवेन्नरः ॥ 12 ॥
1.196.m: Having performed the kṛcchra penance according to rule for the sake of purification, O lord of birds, / only then does a man become qualified to worship the sun.

1.196.s:
na vijñātaṃ pradātavyaṃ na mlānaṃ na ca dūṣitam ..
na ca paryuṣitaṃ mālyaṃ dātavyamṛddhimicchatā .. 13 ..
1.196.d:
न विज्ञातं प्रदातव्यं न म्लानं न च दूषितम् ॥
न च पर्युषितं माल्यं दातव्यमृद्धिमिच्छता ॥ 13 ॥
1.196.m: A garland that is unknown, withered, defiled, / or stale must not be offered by one desiring prosperity.

1.196.s:
devamullocayedyastu sa khalaḥ puṣpalobhataḥ ..
puṣpāṇi ca sugaṃdhīni bhojako netarāṇi ca .. 14 ..
1.196.d:
देवमुल्लोचयेद्यस्तु स खलः पुष्पलोभतः ॥
पुष्पाणि च सुगंधीनि भोजको नेतराणि च ॥ 14 ॥
1.196.m: Whoever plucks from the deity, that rogue, out of greed for flowers— / fragrant flowers, and not others, [offered by] a Bhojaka—

1.196.s:
brahmahatyāmavāpnoti bhojako lobhamohitaḥ ..
mahārauravamāsādya pacyate śāśvatīḥ samāḥ .. 15 ..
1.196.d:
ब्रह्महत्यामवाप्नोति भोजको लोभमोहितः ॥
महारौरवमासाद्य पच्यते शाश्वतीः समाः ॥ 15 ॥
1.196.m: that Bhojaka, deluded by greed, incurs [the sin of] murdering a brāhmaṇa; / arriving in Mahāraurava, he is cooked for eternal years.

1.196.s:
haṃta te kīrtayiṣyāmi dhūpadānavidhiṃ param ..
pradāne devadevasya yena dhūpena yatphalam .. 16..
1.196.d:
हंत ते कीर्तयिष्यामि धूपदानविधिं परम् ॥
प्रदाने देवदेवस्य येन धूपेन यत्फलम् ॥ 16॥
1.196.m: Come, I shall declare to you the supreme rule for offering incense, / by which incense what fruit [is obtained] in offering to the god of gods.

1.196.s:
sadā caṃdanadhūpena sānnidhyaṃ kurute raviḥ ..
pradadyānmānase caiva yadyadicchati mānavaḥ ..17..
1.196.d:
सदा चंदनधूपेन सान्निध्यं कुरुते रविः ॥
प्रदद्यान्मानसे चैव यद्यदिच्छति मानवः ॥17॥
1.196.m: The sun always makes his presence felt through sandalwood incense; / and he gives in the mind whatever a man desires.

1.196.s:
tathaivāgurudhūpena varaṃ dadyā dabhīpsitam ..
ārogyaṃ vā striyaṃ prepsurnityadā guggulaṃ dahet .. 18 ..
1.196.d:
तथैवागुरुधूपेन वरं दद्या दभीप्सितम् ॥
आरोग्यं वा स्त्रियं प्रेप्सुर्नित्यदा गुग्गुलं दहेत् ॥ 18 ॥
1.196.m: In the same way, through agallochum incense he grants the desired boon. / Desiring health or a woman, one should always burn guggulu.

1.196.s:
maṃgalaṃ dhūpadānena sadā yacchati bhānumān ..
ārogyaṃ ca striyaṃ dadyā tsaukhyaṃ ca paramaṃ bhavet .. 19 ..
1.196.d:
मंगलं धूपदानेन सदा यच्छति भानुमान् ॥
आरोग्यं च स्त्रियं दद्या त्सौख्यं च परमं भवेत् ॥ 19 ॥
1.196.m: Through the offering of incense the sun always grants auspiciousness; / he gives health and a woman, and supreme happiness arises.

1.196.s:
sadā kuṃkumadhūpena saubhāgyaṃ labhate naraḥ ..
śrīvāsakasya dhūpena vāṇijyaṃ saphalaṃ bhavet .. 20 ..
1.196.d:
सदा कुंकुमधूपेन सौभाग्यं लभते नरः ॥
श्रीवासकस्य धूपेन वाणिज्यं सफलं भवेत् ॥ 20 ॥
1.196.m: Through saffron incense a man always obtains good fortune. / Through the incense of śrīvāsaka resin, commerce becomes fruitful.

1.196.s:
rasaṃ sarvarasopetaṃ dadatorthāgamo dhruvam ..
devadāruṃ ca dahato bhavatyannamathākṣayam .. 21 ..
1.196.d:
रसं सर्वरसोपेतं ददतोर्थागमो ध्रुवम् ॥
देवदारुं च दहतो भवत्यन्नमथाक्षयम् ॥ 21 ॥
1.196.m: To one offering resin endowed with all essences, the arrival of wealth is certain; / and to one burning deodar cedar, food becomes inexhaustible.

1.196.s:
vilepanaṃ kuṃkumena sarvakāmaphalapradam ..
iha loke sukhī bhūtvā dātā svargama vāpnuyāt .. 22 ..
1.196.d:
विलेपनं कुंकुमेन सर्वकामफलप्रदम् ॥
इह लोके सुखी भूत्वा दाता स्वर्गम वाप्नुयात् ॥ 22 ॥
1.196.m: Anointment with saffron yields the fruit of all desires; / having become happy in this world, the giver attains heaven.

1.196.s:
caṃdanasya pradānena śriyamāyuśca viṃdati ..
raktacaṃdanadānena sarvaṃ dadyāddivākaraḥ .. 23 ..
1.196.d:
चंदनस्य प्रदानेन श्रियमायुश्च विंदति ॥
रक्तचंदनदानेन सर्वं दद्याद्दिवाकरः ॥ 23 ॥
1.196.m: Through the giving of sandalwood one gains prosperity and long life; / through the giving of red sandalwood the sun gives everything.

1.196.s:
api rogaśatairgrastaiḥ kṣiprārogyamavā pnuyāt ..
vartigaṃdhaiśca saugaṃdhyaṃ paramaṃ viṃdate naraḥ .. 24 ..
1.196.d:
अपि रोगशतैर्ग्रस्तैः क्षिप्रारोग्यमवा प्नुयात् ॥
वर्तिगंधैश्च सौगंध्यं परमं विंदते नरः ॥ 24 ॥
1.196.m: Even when seized by hundreds of diseases, one quickly obtains health; / and through wick-incenses a man attains supreme fragrance.

1.196.s:
kastūrikālepanakairaiśvaryamatulaṃ labhet ..
karpūrasaṃyutairgaṃdhaiḥ kṣmādhipādhipatirbhavet .. 25 ..
1.196.d:
कस्तूरिकालेपनकैरैश्वर्यमतुलं लभेत् ॥
कर्पूरसंयुतैर्गंधैः क्ष्माधिपाधिपतिर्भवेत् ॥ 25 ॥
1.196.m: Through anointments of musk one obtains peerless sovereignty; / through fragrances mixed with camphor one becomes a lord over kings.

1.196.s:
catuḥsamena gaṃdhena kiṃ tulyaṃ prāpnuyānnaraḥ ..
devāgāraṃ tu tanmanye bhaktyā ya upalepayet .. 26 ..
1.196.d:
चतुःसमेन गंधेन किं तुल्यं प्राप्नुयान्नरः ॥
देवागारं तु तन्मन्ये भक्त्या य उपलेपयेत् ॥ 26 ॥
1.196.m: What equal to that could a man obtain through catuḥsama perfume? / I consider that [as attained] by one who devoutly plasters the temple of the deity.

1.196.s:
sa rogānmucyate kṣipraṃ puruṣo bhogavānbhavet ..
aṣṭādaśeha kuṣṭhāni ye cānye vyādhayo nṛṇām ..
pralayaṃ yāṃti te sarve mṛdā yadyupalepayet .. 27 ..
1.196.d:
स रोगान्मुच्यते क्षिप्रं पुरुषो भोगवान्भवेत् ॥
अष्टादशेह कुष्ठानि ये चान्ये व्याधयो नृणाम् ॥
प्रलयं यांति ते सर्वे मृदा यद्युपलेपयेत् ॥ 27 ॥
1.196.m: He is quickly freed from disease; the man becomes possessed of enjoyments. / The eighteen [forms of] leprosy here, and whatever other afflictions of mortals, / all go to destruction if one plasters with clay.

1.196.s:
pralepanānāṃ sarveṣāṃ raktacaṃdanamuttamam ..
nātaḥ parataraṃ kiṃcidbhānostuṣṭikaraṃ param .. 28 ..
1.196.d:
प्रलेपनानां सर्वेषां रक्तचंदनमुत्तमम् ॥
नातः परतरं किंचिद्भानोस्तुष्टिकरं परम् ॥ 28 ॥
1.196.m: Of all anointments, red sandalwood is the best; / there is nothing higher than this that brings supreme satisfaction to the sun.

1.196.s:
kiṃ tasya na bhavelloko yo hyanena pralepayet ..
sarvakāmasamṛddho'sau sūryaloke mahīyate .. 29 ..
1.196.d:
किं तस्य न भवेल्लोको यो ह्यनेन प्रलेपयेत् ॥
सर्वकामसमृद्धोऽसौ सूर्यलोके महीयते ॥ 29 ॥
1.196.m: What realm would not belong to him who plasters [the shrine] with this? / Abounding in all desires, he is magnified in the solar realm.

1.196.s:
upalipya ravergehaṃ kuryādvai maṃḍalaṃ punaḥ ..
ekenātha samāpnoti bhāgyamārogyamuttamam .. 30 ..
1.196.d:
उपलिप्य रवेर्गेहं कुर्याद्वै मंडलं पुनः ॥
एकेनाथ समाप्नोति भाग्यमारोग्यमुत्तमम् ॥ 30 ॥
1.196.m: Having smeared the abode of the sun, one should draw a mandala again; / through one [such rite], one obtains good fortune and excellent health.

1.196.s:
tribhiḥ saptabhiracchinnā bālo vānyopi yo naraḥ ..
tena pradāpayeddevānkuryāttānna nivārayet ..
anena vidhinā kuryādyāvatīḥ sapta saptamī .. 31 ..
1.196.d:
त्रिभिः सप्तभिरच्छिन्ना बालो वान्योपि यो नरः ॥
तेन प्रदापयेद्देवान्कुर्यात्तान्न निवारयेत् ॥
अनेन विधिना कुर्याद्यावतीः सप्त सप्तमी ॥ 31 ॥
1.196.m: Unbroken for three or seven [days], whether a boy or any other man, / by him one should cause the deities to be given [offerings], and one should let them perform it without preventing them. / Following this rule one should perform as many as seven Saptamīs.

1.196.s:
etā vai sapta saptamyo yathā proktā vivasvatā ..
kurvīta yo naro bhaktyā sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate ..32..
1.196.d:
एता वै सप्त सप्तम्यो यथा प्रोक्ता विवस्वता ॥
कुर्वीत यो नरो भक्त्या सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥32॥
1.196.m: These indeed are the seven Saptamīs as proclaimed by Vivasvat; / the man who performs [them] with devotion is freed from all sins.

1.196.s:
arkasaṃpuṭakairvittaṃ maricaiḥ priyasaṃgamam ..
niṃbapatrai roganāśaṃ phalaiḥ putrānyathepsitān ..
dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ suvarṇaṃ ca tato dadyādvivasvate .. 33 ..
1.196.d:
अर्कसंपुटकैर्वित्तं मरिचैः प्रियसंगमम् ॥
निंबपत्रै रोगनाशं फलैः पुत्रान्यथेप्सितान् ॥
धनं धान्यं सुवर्णं च ततो दद्याद्विवस्वते ॥ 33 ॥
1.196.m: One should then offer to Vivasvat [leaves in] sun-leaf cups for wealth, black pepper for union with a loved one, / nīm leaves for the destruction of disease, fruits for sons as desired, / and money, grain, and gold.

1.196.s:
jayaṃ prāpnoti vipulaṃ kṛtvā sarvatra khecara ..
sarvānkāmānkāmikastu prāpnuyānnātra saṃśayaḥ .. 34 ..
1.196.d:
जयं प्राप्नोति विपुलं कृत्वा सर्वत्र खेचर ॥
सर्वान्कामान्कामिकस्तु प्राप्नुयान्नात्र संशयः ॥ 34 ॥
1.196.m: Having done [this], he attains vast victory everywhere, O sky-wanderer; / one desiring objects of desire obtains all desires, there is no doubt of this.

1.196.s:
naro vā yadi vā nārī yathoktaṃ saptamīvratam ..
yaḥ karoti khagaśreṣṭha sa yāti paramaṃ padam .. 35 ..
1.196.d:
नरो वा यदि वा नारी यथोक्तं सप्तमीव्रतम् ॥
यः करोति खगश्रेष्ठ स याति परमं पदम् ॥ 35 ॥
1.196.m: Whether a man or a woman, whoever performs the Saptamī observance as stated, / O best of birds, goes to the supreme state.

1.196.s:
na teṣāṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiṃcidastīti durlabham ..
ye bhaktyā lokanāthasya vratinaḥ saṃyatendriyāḥ .. 36 ..
1.196.d:
न तेषां त्रिषु लोकेषु किंचिदस्तीति दुर्लभम् ॥
ये भक्त्या लोकनाथस्य व्रतिनः संयतेन्द्रियाः ॥ 36 ॥
1.196.m: There is nothing difficult to obtain in the three worlds for those / votaries of restrained senses who are devoted to the protector of the world.

1.196.s:
sarvayajñaphalaṃ teṣāṃ yathā vedoditaṃ bhavet..
brahmeṃdraviṣṇavastena pūjitā nātra saṃśayaḥ ..37 ..
1.196.d:
सर्वयज्ञफलं तेषां यथा वेदोदितं भवेत्॥
ब्रह्मेंद्रविष्णवस्तेन पूजिता नात्र संशयः ॥37 ॥
1.196.m: The fruit of all sacrifices, as declared in the Veda, belongs to them; / by him Brahmā, Indra, and Viṣṇu have been worshipped, of this there is no doubt.

1.196.s:
nāṃdho na kuṣṭhī na klībo na vyaṃgo na ca nirdhanaḥ ..
kadāpi ca bhavetkaścidyaścaretsaptamīvratam .. 38 ..
1.196.d:
नांधो न कुष्ठी न क्लीबो न व्यंगो न च निर्धनः ॥
कदापि च भवेत्कश्चिद्यश्चरेत्सप्तमीव्रतम् ॥ 38 ॥
1.196.m: No one who observes the Saptamī observance ever becomes blind, / leprous, impotent, crippled, or destitute.

1.196.s:
putrārthī śrutisaṃpannāllam̐bhetputrāścirāyuṣaḥ ..
na teṣāṃ triṣu lokeṣu kiṃcidastīti durlabham ..
bhogārthī labhate bhogānvratenānena suvrata.. 39 ..
1.196.d:
पुत्रार्थी श्रुतिसंपन्नाल्लम्̐भेत्पुत्राश्चिरायुषः ॥
न तेषां त्रिषु लोकेषु किंचिदस्तीति दुर्लभम् ॥
भोगार्थी लभते भोगान्व्रतेनानेन सुव्रत॥ 39 ॥
1.196.m: One desiring sons will obtain long-lived sons endowed with sacred learning; / there is nothing difficult to obtain for them in the three worlds; / one desiring enjoyments obtains enjoyments through this observance, O you of noble vows.

1.196.s:
krodhātpramādāllobhācca vratabhaṃgo yadā bhavet ..
prāyaścittamidaṃ kṛtvā punareva vratī bhavet ..40..
1.196.d:
क्रोधात्प्रमादाल्लोभाच्च व्रतभंगो यदा भवेत् ॥
प्रायश्चित्तमिदं कृत्वा पुनरेव व्रती भवेत् ॥40॥
1.196.m: When a breach of the observance occurs through anger, negligence, or greed, / having performed this expiation, he may become a votary once again.

1.196.s:
saptaiva yāvatsaptamyaḥ saṃprāptā guruṇā khaga ..
tāsu bhāskaramabhyarcya mālyadhūpādibhirnaraḥ ..
bhojayitvā dvijāñchaktyā prāpnuyātsvargamakṣayam .. 41 ..
1.196.d:
सप्तैव यावत्सप्तम्यः संप्राप्ता गुरुणा खग ॥
तासु भास्करमभ्यर्च्य माल्यधूपादिभिर्नरः ॥
भोजयित्वा द्विजाञ्छक्त्या प्राप्नुयात्स्वर्गमक्षयम् ॥ 41 ॥
1.196.m: As long as just seven Saptamīs have arrived with [the transit of] Jupiter, O bird, / a man who worships the sun on them with garlands, incense, and the like, / and feeds twice-born men according to his means, attains inexhaustible heaven.

1.196.s:
saptamyāṃ vipramukhyebhyo yo'nnaṃ dadyātkhageśvara ..
tadakṣayaṃ bhavettasya sa ca sūryagṛhaṃ vrajet .. 42 ..
1.196.d:
सप्तम्यां विप्रमुख्येभ्यो योऽन्नं दद्यात्खगेश्वर ॥
तदक्षयं भवेत्तस्य स च सूर्यगृहं व्रजेत् ॥ 42 ॥
1.196.m: Whoever gives food to the foremost of brāhmaṇas on a Saptamī, O lord of birds, / that becomes imperishable for him, and he goes to the abode of the sun.

1.196.s:
iti te kīrtitaṃ vīra saptamīvratamuttamam ..
bhūya evābhidhāsyāmi śṛṇu me vadatonagha .. 43 ..
1.196.d:
इति ते कीर्तितं वीर सप्तमीव्रतमुत्तमम् ॥
भूय एवाभिधास्यामि शृणु मे वदतोनघ ॥ 43 ॥
1.196.m: Thus has the excellent Saptamī observance been declared to you, O hero; / I shall speak again, listen to me as I speak, O sinless one,

1.196.s:
yena vrataprabhāveṇa kāmikaṃ phalamaśnute ..
saptamīṃ khagaśārdūla śuklāṃ dvādaśanāmikām .. 44 ..
1.196.d:
येन व्रतप्रभावेण कामिकं फलमश्नुते ॥
सप्तमीं खगशार्दूल शुक्लां द्वादशनामिकाम् ॥ 44 ॥
1.196.m: by the power of which observance one enjoys the desired fruit: / on the bright Saptamī of the twelve names, O tiger among birds,

1.196.s:
gomūtragomayāhāraḥ ṣaḍvṛtāhāra eva ca ..
atha vā yāvakāhāraḥ śīrṇaparṇāśanopi vā. .45..
1.196.d:
गोमूत्रगोमयाहारः षड्वृताहार एव च ॥
अथ वा यावकाहारः शीर्णपर्णाशनोपि वा॥45॥
1.196.m: subsisting on cow urine and cow dung, or subsisting on the six butter-preparations, / or subsisting on barley gruel, or feeding on withered leaves,

1.196.s:
kṣīrāśī caikabhaktaṃ(caiva bhaktaṃ?) vā sikthāhārotha vā punaḥ ..
jalāhārotha vā vidvānpūjayeta divākaram .. 46 ..
1.196.d:
क्षीराशी चैकभक्तं(चैव भक्तं?) वा सिक्थाहारोथ वा पुनः ॥
जलाहारोथ वा विद्वान्पूजयेत दिवाकरम् ॥ 46 ॥
1.196.m: subsisting on milk, or taking only a single meal, or subsisting on morsels of food, / or subsisting on water, the wise man should worship the maker of the day,

1.196.s:
puṣpopahārairvividhaiḥ padmasaugaṃdhikotpalaiḥ ..
nānāprakārairgaṃdhaiśca dhūpairguggulucaṃdanaiḥ .. 47 ..
1.196.d:
पुष्पोपहारैर्विविधैः पद्मसौगंधिकोत्पलैः ॥
नानाप्रकारैर्गंधैश्च धूपैर्गुग्गुलुचंदनैः ॥ 47 ॥
1.196.m: with various offerings of flowers—lotuses, red night-lotuses, and blue water-lilies— / and with various kinds of perfumes, and with incenses of guggulu and sandalwood,

1.196.s:
kṛśaraiḥ pāyasānnairvā vividhaiśca vibhūṣaṇaiḥ ..
arcayitvā dvijaśreṣṭha bhakṣyavastrādibhūṣaṇaiḥ .. 48 ..
1.196.d:
कृशरैः पायसान्नैर्वा विविधैश्च विभूषणैः ॥
अर्चयित्वा द्विजश्रेष्ठ भक्ष्यवस्त्रादिभूषणैः ॥ 48 ॥
1.196.m: with kṛśara or milk-rice dishes, and with various ornaments, / having worshipped [him], O best of the twice-born, with food, garments, and ornaments,

1.196.s:
sarvapakṣaphalaṃ prāpya sūryalokaṃ tato vrajet ..
tapasoṃte tato vīra kule mahati jāyate .. 49 ..
1.196.d:
सर्वपक्षफलं प्राप्य सूर्यलोकं ततो व्रजेत् ॥
तपसोंते ततो वीर कुले महति जायते ॥ 49 ॥
1.196.m: having obtained the fruit of all fortnights, he then goes to the solar realm; / and at the end of his austerity, O hero, he is born in a noble family.

1.196.s:
yathākramaṃ prayatnena nāmāni parikīrtayet ..
māghe ca phālgune māsi caitre ca garuḍāgraja .. 50 ..
1.196.d:
यथाक्रमं प्रयत्नेन नामानि परिकीर्तयेत् ॥
माघे च फाल्गुने मासि चैत्रे च गरुडाग्रज ॥ 50 ॥
1.196.m: With effort he should recite the names in proper order / in the months of Māgha, Phālguna, and Caitra, O elder brother of Garuḍa,

1.196.s:
vaiśākhe tvatha jyeṣṭhe tu āṣāḍhe śrāvaṇe tathā ..
māsi bhādrapade vīra tathā cāśvayuje khaga .. 51..
1.196.d:
वैशाखे त्वथ ज्येष्ठे तु आषाढे श्रावणे तथा ॥
मासि भाद्रपदे वीर तथा चाश्वयुजे खग ॥ 51॥
